tools.name: Claude in Chrome (Claude for Chrome)

variants.name: Claude in Chrome side panel (runs as a Cowork session on Max/Team, rolling out to Pro)
Browser tools for Claude Code (claude --chrome, VS Code extension)
variants.note: Exposed to Claude Code as the claude-in-chrome MCP server over a native messaging host and bridge.claudeusercontent.com; requires a claude.ai login (not API keys or third-party providers).

variants.name: Browser use from Cowork (Preferred browser: Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser)

summary: A Chrome extension (Chrome Web Store id fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn, version 1.0.94, updated 19 September 2026) that lets Claude read, click, type and navigate in the user's own browser with the user's live login state, from the side panel, from Cowork, or as tools for Claude Code. Inference runs on the Anthropic API under the signed-in claude.ai account (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise); page content, screenshots and actions leave the browser to Anthropic, and side-panel sessions are saved to history and synced across devices. It is the vendor-extension shape of the browser-agent drawing: no runtime of its own, the browser's APIs as its tools, and the profile's cookie jar as its credential, so the controls that bound it are the managed profile, browser extension policy and the secure web gateway the organisation supplies, plus the site lists and toggle in the vendor console.

Anthropic's safeguards are model training, injection and action-screening classifiers, default-blocked site categories (adult, piracy; financial sites need explicit permission), prohibited actions (purchases, account creation, captcha solving, permanent deletions, "completing instructions from emails or web content") and always-confirm actions (downloads, sensitive data entry, granting authorisations). Admin controls sit in the claude.ai console at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome: an org enable toggle (on by default on Team; on Enterprise it turns on by default starting 10 September 2026 unless an owner already turned it off), site allowlists and blocklists that override user permissions, a per-role capability on Enterprise, and forceLoginOrgUUID as a Chrome enterprise policy. Users choose Manually approve, Automatically approve (the Cowork side panel's default) or Skip all approvals, and the side panel keeps the choice; the console does not pin the mode. Zero data retention is not supported for Claude in Chrome, and the product does not yet honour role-level model or effort restrictions.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise, but not organisations covered by HIPAA; generally available in Cowork and Claude Code, beta in the Chrome side panel; extension 1.0.36+ for Claude Code; not through Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API with the claude.ai login; Claude Code sessions reach the extension through bridge.claudeusercontent.com, which must share the proxy egress used for claude.ai when IP allowlisting is on.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Page content, DOM and screenshots of the tabs Claude works in, console and network readers when used, and uploaded files (up to 10 MB) go to Anthropic; GIF recordings capture everything visible including logged-in account details.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Follows the account's plan policy (commercial: no training, 30-day retention); side-panel sessions are Cowork sessions saved to history; zero data retention is not supported for Claude in Chrome.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: support.claude.com Claude in Chrome articles (get started, safety, permissions, admin controls) and code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, platform.claude.com and wss://bridge.claudeusercontent.com; the bridge must leave through the same proxy egress as claude.ai when IP allowlisting is enabled, or that egress address must be on the org allowlist.

facts.label: Supported browsers
facts.value: The support article says only Google Chrome; the Claude Code page says Chrome and Edge, with detection in Brave, Arc, Vivaldi and Opera (not WSL). Plan for the wider set.

facts.label: Usage & model governance
facts.value: Side-panel work consumes as Cowork agentic work against organisation, group and user spend limits (managed under Organization settings > Cowork); model access and effort-level restrictions by role do not yet apply to Claude in Chrome.

facts.label: Extension permissions
facts.value: Requests sidePanel, storage, scripting, debugger, tabGroups, tabs, alarms, notifications, system.display, webNavigation, declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess, offscreen, nativeMessaging, downloads and unlimitedStorage; the Web Store listing declares handling of personally identifiable information, personal communications, location, web history, user activity and website content.

riskNotes.note: Web content is the attack surface; ShadowPrompt (March 2026, fixed 1.0.41) let any site inject prompts through a trusted *.claude.ai subdomain, and Anthropic's own safety article says the risk of a successful attack "is not zero". Allowlists and separate browser profiles are the practical containment.

Claude acts inside every session the user is logged into (Gmail, GitHub, Drive, banking if permitted) with no separate identity; ClaudeBleed (May 2026) showed another zero-permission extension could issue commands to it.

The extension requests debugger, scripting, nativeMessaging and downloads permissions and updates automatically from the Chrome Web Store (1.0.94 on 19 September 2026); the native messaging host for Claude Code is started by the browser, outside Claude Code's corporate launcher.

"Skip all approvals" disables safety checks entirely; "Automatically approve" is the Cowork side panel's default and nothing in the admin console pins the mode. Purchases are prohibited outright and downloads, sensitive-data entry and granting authorisations always ask, but sending messages and publishing are not in the always-ask set.

Screenshots and page text of authenticated apps leave the browser; Anthropic advises against use for financial, legal, medical or regulated data, and zero data retention is not available for this product.

controls.mechanism: Side-panel mode selector chosen by the user and kept for later sessions: Manually approve (each action; a plan to approve first in the classic panel), Automatically approve (an AI safety check on each action, the Cowork side panel's default) and Skip all approvals; always-ask on modifying permission settings, granting authorisations and entering sensitive information; per-site "Allow this action" / "Always allow actions on this site"; vendor-prohibited action classes; in Claude Code, managed permission rules on the claude-in-chrome tools and permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode

steps.title: Keep users on per-action approval
body: Have users pick Manually approve in the side panel's mode drop-down and answer site prompts with "Allow this action" rather than "Always allow actions on this site"; the side panel keeps the chosen mode and no admin setting pins it.

steps.title: Force prompts on browser tools in Claude Code
body: In managed settings add permissions.ask rules for mcp__claude-in-chrome__* with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, and set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" so plan-mode browser calls cannot run unprompted.

steps.title: Remove the classifier mode from Cowork
body: Turn off Allow "Automatically approve" mode under Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions; the page documents it for Cowork's mode selector and does not say it reaches the Chrome side panel, so test it there.

controls.note: Partial by the architecture rule: named consequential classes are confirmed by a present user, but the covered set is vendor-chosen and narrower than the pin's (purchases and financial transactions are prohibited outright and sensitive-data entry and authorisations always ask, while sending messages and publishing are not in the always-ask set), and nothing on the Chrome admin page removes Skip all approvals or Automatically approve. The permissions guide says the always-ask actions apply "regardless of your permission mode" yet describes Skip all approvals as never pausing; treat Skip as unconfirmed. Automatically approve is a model reviewer and never counts as human approval. "Always allow actions on this site" pre-approves every later action on that origin except the protected ones, and scheduled shortcuts run with nobody present. Only the Claude Code path is admin-enforceable, by managed permission rules.

original.mechanism: Manually approve (plan shown before acting), Automatically approve (pauses on flagged risks), Skip all approvals; always-confirm actions regardless of mode; Claude Code prompts "Claude in Chrome wants to" per site

steps.title: Set the approval mode
body: Choose Manually approve to review each action before it runs; Automatically approve still requires approval for downloads, sensitive data entry and granting authorisations, and Skip all approvals removes every pause.

steps.title: Keep state-changing browser tools behind a prompt in Claude Code
body: In plan mode read-only calls (read_page, get_page_text, find, screenshot) run without a prompt and clicks, typing, navigation and GIF recording prompt for approval.

original.note: The approval mode is a per-user choice with no admin setting that forces Manually approve; only the Claude Code path is admin-manageable, through permissions rules.

controls.mechanism: Organisation allowlist and blocklist at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome (the blocklist holds regardless of user permissions; the same lists govern Cowork's built-in browser); per-user site grants ("Allow this action" / "Always allow actions on this site", revocable under Extension settings > Permissions); vendor default-blocked categories and financial-site prompts; in Claude Code, managed permission rules per claude-in-chrome tool

steps.title: Scope sites in the vendor console
body: At Organization settings > Claude in Chrome add the sites Claude may work on to the allowlist and the sites it must never touch to the blocklist, which applies regardless of user permissions.

steps.title: Review users' standing grants
body: Users review and revoke "always allow" sites under Your approved sites on the Extension settings > Permissions page.

steps.title: Scope individual browser tools in Claude Code
body: Add permissions.deny or permissions.ask rules for mcp__claude-in-chrome__<tool> in managed settings to remove or gate single browser tools in Claude Code sessions.

controls.note: Partial by the architecture rule: the admin sets per-origin allow and block lists that the extension enforces over the user's grants, but there is no read-only tier (a permitted site is fully actionable, subject to the user's approval mode) and no per-tool or per-operation scope in the side panel. The extension's managed policy schema (managed_schema.json in 1.0.94) also accepts blockedUrlPatterns, a device-delivered block list by hostname and path, but no Anthropic page documents it. Chrome's ExtensionSettings runtime_blocked_hosts is not a usable scope for this extension: from Chrome 154 it disables chrome.debugger.attach() entirely for an extension with the debugger permission, which is how Claude clicks and types. Claude Code sessions inherit the extension's site permissions.

original.mechanism: Site-level scoping: org allowlist and blocklist at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome override user grants; per-site "Allow this action" / "Always allow actions on this site"; default-blocked categories and financial-site gating; Chrome ExtensionSettings runtime_blocked_hosts / runtime_allowed_hosts at the browser policy tier

steps.title: Scope by site in the vendor console
body: Add approved sites to the allowlist so Claude can only browse those, and forbidden sites to the blocklist, which applies regardless of user settings; the vendor recommends a restrictive allowlist during rollout.

steps.title: Let users grant the minimum per site
body: Advise "Allow this action" over "Always allow actions on this site"; users review and revoke always-allow grants under Extension settings > Permissions.

steps.title: Enforce host scope from browser policy
body: In ExtensionSettings for id fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn set runtime_blocked_hosts for origins the extension must never touch; the Chromium policy text warns that from Chrome 154 runtime_blocked_hosts on an extension with the debugger permission disables chrome.debugger.attach() entirely, so test before rollout.

original.note: Scoping is by site, not by tool: the org allowlist and blocklist hide sites, per-site grants pre-approve actions there, and default-blocked categories limit reach. In Claude Code the extension's tools follow permission rules.

controls.mechanism: No credential scoping in the extension: Claude acts with the profile's cookies on every site it may access; the organisation allowlist at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome bounds which signed-in origins it can use; 1Password for Claude (macOS, beta) is off by default under Control password manager access and fills credentials without passing them to Claude; the vendor recommends a separate profile without sensitive accounts but does not provision one

steps.title: Bound the signed-in origins the agent can use
body: Keep a restrictive allowlist at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome so Claude can act only in the sessions of the listed origins.

steps.title: Keep the password-manager bridge off
body: Leave 1Password for Claude off under Control password manager access at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome unless a team needs sign-in tasks.

steps.title: Install the extension only in a managed agent profile
body: Set installation_mode "force_installed" for fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn in ExtensionSettings only for the organisational unit or profile used for agent work, and block it everywhere else.

controls.note: Partial by the architecture rule: the admin allowlist denies the agent the sessions of unlisted origins and the 1Password bridge is an admin toggle, but the dedicated profile is vendor advice ("consider using a separate browser profile without access to sensitive accounts"), not something the product provisions or enforces, and nothing in the product keeps Chrome's own saved passwords away from the agent. On every allowed origin Claude acts with the user's full session: there is no agent identity or on-behalf-of exchange, and downstream applications see the user. Chrome's PasswordManagerEnabled false stops new saves only ("previously saved passwords will still work"). Claude Code and desktop-driven tasks use the same browser profile. Cowork's built-in browser, which does not see users' logins unless they import them, is the logged-out alternative (Organization settings > Cowork).

original.mechanism: The extension uses the profile's own sessions; the isolation is a dedicated browser profile with few signed-in origins and no saved passwords, which the vendor recommends but does not provision. 1Password for Claude access control is off by default (macOS only).

steps.title: Run the agent in a separate profile
body: Follow the vendor's advice to use a separate browser profile without access to sensitive accounts, and keep work accounts holding sensitive data out of it.

steps.title: Leave the password-manager bridge off
body: Keep "1Password for Claude access control" at its default off unless a task needs it; it is the only vendor path that hands stored credentials to the agent.

original.note: There is no agent identity or on-behalf-of exchange; downstream applications see the user. Provision the dedicated profile through Chrome enterprise policy so it is managed rather than a user habit.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's content classifier scans all untrusted content entering Claude's context and a second classifier checks every action before it runs (no administrator setting, threshold or event export); Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) can hold governed Cowork and Claude Code requests, including tool results, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's AI security server

steps.title: Put an inspector on returned page content (Enterprise, beta)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on "Allow for your organization", register your AI security server, set Failure handling to "Block the request" and turn on "Enforce verdicts".

steps.title: Know what the vendor screening covers
body: The safety article states that content classifiers scan all untrusted content entering Claude's context and flag potential injections; there is no setting for them.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal screening that is not admin-configurable, plus an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server does the classifying. No hidden or off-screen content stripping is documented; Claude reads pages from screenshots and page text. Inference hooks name claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Code and Claude Tag, not Claude in Chrome: the Cowork side panel runs as a Cowork session and Claude Code's browser tools return into a Claude Code session, but the classic side panel is not covered. Hooks return allow or deny only (no strip or quarantine). The action classifier and the confirmations are action policy, not input screening.

original.mechanism: Anthropic-side content injection classifier and action screening classifier; no admin-tunable detector or page-content stripping

steps.title: Keep the approving modes on
body: Advise users to stay in Manually approve or Automatically approve; Skip all approvals turns off the safety checks that screen actions.

steps.title: Reduce exposure with allowlists and profiles
body: Start with a restrictive org allowlist and recommend a separate browser profile for sensitive accounts, per the safety guidance.

original.note: The classifiers are Anthropic-operated and not tunable; they screen page content and proposed actions. Allowlists and profiles reduce exposure but detect nothing.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) let the organisation's DLP server deny governed Cowork and Claude Code requests, tool results included, that carry regulated content; the organisation blocklist and allowlist keep Claude off data-bearing sites; always-ask on entering sensitive information; Claude Code Read deny rules also block uploads; Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP and the SSE as the external layer

steps.title: Inspect what leaves for inference (Enterprise, beta)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks connect your DLP or AI security server and turn on "Enforce verdicts"; it can deny a request but not redact it.

steps.title: Keep Claude off data-bearing sites
body: Add sites holding regulated or confidential data to the blocklist at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome, or keep them off the allowlist.

steps.title: Block uploads of protected files from Claude Code
body: Permission rules that deny Read on a file also block uploading it through the extension; uploads are capped at 10 MB.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: an inline hook that can block is an attach point, and nothing in the product masks or tokenises a value; the vendor states Claude "can't filter sensitive content out of what it sees", and screenshots of the tabs it works in become part of the conversation. The hooks page does not name Claude in Chrome (it reaches the Cowork side panel and Claude Code as Cowork and Claude Code sessions, not the classic side panel) and does not say whether screenshots are sent. Site lists and always-ask are data minimisation, not detection. Claude in Chrome is not available to HIPAA organisations and does not support zero data retention. Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP rules (File uploaded, Content pasted) and an SSE with TLS inspection of the profile's traffic are the external content inspection.

original.mechanism: Always-confirm on sensitive data entry and downloads; org blocklist for data-bearing sites; Read deny rules govern uploads from Claude Code; Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP rules on upload and paste as the external layer

steps.title: Block uploads of protected files from Claude Code
body: Permission rules that deny Read on a file also block uploading it through the extension; uploads are capped at 10 MB.

steps.title: Inspect what the agent uploads and pastes
body: Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP rules on File uploaded and Content pasted block or audit content moving through the agent's profile.

original.note: Always-confirm and the site blocklist restrict actions and destinations; nothing in the extension inspects what is typed, uploaded or returned. Content inspection is Chrome Enterprise DLP or the SSE.

controls.mechanism: Account memory (off by default on Team and Enterprise, turned on at Organization settings > Capabilities) is shared with Cowork in the cloud, which the side panel runs as; side-panel sessions are saved to account history and synced across devices; shortcuts, scheduled shortcuts and recorded workflows (classic panel) keep standing instructions in the extension; "always allow" site grants persist

steps.title: Decide on account memory
body: Leave memory off or turn it on at Organization settings > Capabilities; turning it off deletes every member's memory entries immediately.

steps.title: Review saved instructions
body: Users edit or delete shortcuts through the extension settings, including any scheduled to run automatically.

steps.title: Review standing site grants
body: Users revoke "always allow" sites under Your approved sites on the Extension settings > Permissions page.

controls.note: Partial by the architecture rule (disable-only): the owner can switch account memory off and users can view and delete memory, history and shortcuts, but nothing scopes which origins may be remembered, treats remembered page content as untrusted on read, or validates what is written. The memory article says memory is shared with Cowork in the cloud, and the side panel runs as a Cowork session, but no Claude in Chrome page says whether the side panel reads it; test. Shortcuts and recorded workflows are user-level with no admin control, and the safety article warns that what is on the page is stored with the session. How long history is kept follows the organisation's retention setting, which is retention, not memory protection.

original.mechanism: Side-panel sessions are Cowork sessions saved to account history and synced to web, desktop and mobile; per-site permission history in Extension settings; no browser memories index and no admin memory controls

steps.title: Review saved permissions and sessions
body: Users open Extension settings > Permissions to revoke always-allow sites; session history follows the organisation's conversation retention setting.

original.note: Retention only: sessions are saved history the user can delete. Nothing validates or restores memory, and no admin control applies.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API local-session transcripts with product_surface claude_in_chrome (Enterprise, beta) carry the agent's browser tool calls (navigations, clicks, form input) and the text of their results; the extension exports no in-browser telemetry of its own; Chrome Enterprise reporting connectors and Chrome Enterprise Premium data-protection events cover the browser

steps.title: Pull the agent's browser actions (Enterprise, beta)
body: Walk /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local, keep sessions with product_surface claude_in_chrome, and fetch each one's messages with tool_use_input_max_bytes and tool_result_max_bytes set to -1.

steps.title: Turn on browser event reporting
body: In the Google Admin console enable Event reporting and select a reporting connector (Google Security Operations, Splunk, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto or Pub/Sub) under Devices > Chrome > Connectors; data-protection events need Chrome Enterprise Premium.

steps.title: Write DLP rules for the agent's profile
body: Under Security > Access and data control > Data protection create rules on File uploaded, Content pasted and URL visited, scoped to the organisational unit that holds the agent profile.

steps.title: Cover the native messaging host
body: Monitor com.anthropic.claude_code_browser_extension host registrations under the browser's NativeMessagingHosts directory (or HKCU registry key on Windows) and the process it starts.

controls.note: Partial by the architecture rule: the vendor's transcript export records what the agent navigated to, clicked and typed as tool calls, but it is reconstructed from API calls rather than observed in the browser, is Enterprise-only and beta for Claude in Chrome, omits screenshots ("[image content not shown]"), and names the extension's built-in chat, not the Cowork side panel. Baseline analysis is the SIEM's, and the in-browser vantage point (what the page actually loaded, the user's own browsing) is Chrome Enterprise reporting. The corporate-launcher page states the Chrome native-messaging host is started by the browser, not Claude Code's binary, so EDR must watch it directly.

original.mechanism: Nothing in-browser from the vendor; Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP rules (File uploaded, Content pasted, URL visited) and Chrome Enterprise reporting connectors with extension telemetry to a SIEM

steps.title: Turn on browser event reporting
body: Under Devices > Chrome > Connectors configure a reporting connector (Google Security Operations, Splunk, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto or Pub/Sub); extension telemetry needs the Chrome Enterprise Premium upgrade.

steps.title: Write DLP rules for the agent's profile
body: Under Security > Access and data control > Data protection create rules on File uploaded, Content pasted and URL visited with Block, Allow with warning or Audit only, scoped to the organisational unit that holds the agent profile.

original.note: The vendor exposes no telemetry of what the agent read or clicked beyond the session transcript.

original.mechanism: Browser and endpoint sensors; the native messaging host is started by the browser, outside Claude Code's corporate launcher
original.note: The corporate-launcher page states the Chrome native-messaging host is not covered by processWrapper; EDR must watch it directly.

steps.title: Cover the native messaging host
body: Monitor com.anthropic.claude_code_browser_extension host registrations under the browser's NativeMessagingHosts directory (or HKCU registry key on Windows) and the process it starts with endpoint tooling.

controls.mechanism: "Enable for your team" off at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome, or the Claude for Chrome capability withheld on Enterprise custom roles (up to 15 minutes); isLocalDevMcpEnabled false stops Claude Desktop driving the browser; Chrome ExtensionInstallBlocklist disables installed copies with no user re-enable, and removal from ExtensionInstallForcelist or installation_mode "removed" uninstalls; an Inference hooks deny (Enterprise, beta) refuses the account's next governed request; Claude Code deniedMcpServers

steps.title: Turn it off for the organisation
body: Turn off "Enable for your team" at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome, or withhold the capability from custom roles on Enterprise.

steps.title: Disable the extension on managed browsers
body: Add fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn to ExtensionInstallBlocklist, or, where it was force-installed, remove it from ExtensionInstallForcelist (the force list overrides the blocklist).

steps.title: Stop desktop-driven browser tasks
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false in the Claude Desktop Enterprise configuration so desktop tasks cannot drive Chrome.

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise, beta)
body: With "Enforce verdicts" on at Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks, have your AI security server deny that member's requests.

controls.note: Partial by the architecture rule: the vendor switch and the browser policy are both reachable without the user, but neither documents that a running task stops. The Chrome admin page gives no delay and no effect on a task in progress for the organisation toggle (custom-role changes take up to 15 minutes); the Chromium policy says a blocklisted extension is "disabled" on policy refresh, which ends its work in that browser, but a Cowork side-panel session lives in the cloud with the account and Anthropic does not document what it does next. An Inference hooks deny refuses the next governed request without terminating the session. Nothing here revokes the web sessions the profile is signed into; that is the IdP's and each application's job.

original.mechanism: Org toggle off, role capability removal, Chrome ExtensionInstallBlocklist (disables an installed extension with no user re-enable) or ExtensionSettings installation_mode "removed", user revocation of site permissions

steps.title: Turn it off for the organisation
body: Disable "Enable for your team" at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome or remove the capability from roles.

steps.title: Remove it from every browser
body: Add fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn to ExtensionInstallBlocklist; already-installed copies are disabled and users cannot re-enable them.

original.note: The organisation toggle applies at the extension's next model call; the Chrome policy blocklist applies at the browser's next policy refresh, and an action already in progress on a page completes.

controls.mechanism: Chrome (or Edge) extension management at the host, keyed on the extension id fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn: ExtensionInstallBlocklist "*" with ExtensionInstallAllowlist, or ExtensionSettings installation_mode per id with blocked_permissions and minimum_version_required; in Claude Code, deniedMcpServers blocks the built-in claude-in-chrome MCP server

variants.name: Claude Code GitHub Actions (anthropics/claude-code-action)
variants.note: Runs the Agent SDK on GitHub-hosted runners. Auth by ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret, or keyless via workload identity federation (anthropic_federation_rule_id); Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry via OIDC. summary: Anthropic's agentic coding tool, run by a present developer as a CLI, an IDE extension (VS Code, JetBrains), the Code tab of Claude Desktop, or unattended as a GitHub Action. Inference runs on the Anthropic API by default; organisations can route it to Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform (Vertex), Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, a self-hosted Claude apps gateway, or any LLM gateway via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. All prompts, tool results and file contents Claude reads leave the device to the configured provider over TLS; usage metrics go to Anthropic by default on the Anthropic API (error reports only for Pro and Max sign-ins) and are off on cloud providers.

Two admin channels share one top-precedence managed tier: endpoint-managed settings delivered as files or OS policies via MDM/GPO (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode, managed-settings.json plus managed-settings.d/), and server-managed settings configured by Owners at claude.ai Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings (Team/Enterprise) and fetched at startup with hourly polling. Managed settings outrank command-line flags and all user and project files. The docs state server-managed settings are a client-side control, not a security boundary, and that they are skipped when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY or a non-default ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set; endpoint policy or a Claude apps gateway is the enforcement channel there.

The enforcement points that matter are permissions.deny (evaluated before everything, cannot be overridden by any mode or the auto-mode classifier), PreToolUse hooks (fire in every permission mode including bypassPermissions), the OS-enforced Bash sandbox (Seatbelt / bubblewrap with a domain-allowlisting proxy and credential masking), managed MCP allow/deny lists, plugin marketplace allowlists, and OpenTelemetry export of every tool decision to the organisation's collector.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise (claude.ai login), Claude Console API keys or keyless Console sign-in, and Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS credentials. Server-managed settings, analytics dashboard and SSO need Team/Enterprise; SCIM, Compliance API and ZDR need Enterprise.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API by default. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS select a cloud provider; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN route through an LLM gateway; forceLoginMethod "gateway" plus forceLoginGatewayUrl pin sessions to a self-hosted Claude apps gateway that holds the upstream credential, maps IdP groups to models and managed settings, and relays OTLP telemetry. Third-party routing disables server-managed settings, Remote Control, cloud sessions and the Chrome integration.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, model outputs and everything a tool returns go to the model provider over TLS 1.2+. Metrics (no code, prompts or file paths) go to Anthropic and third-party logging infrastructure by default on the Anthropic API; redacted error reports go to a third-party error tracker by default only for Pro and Max sign-ins; DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC turn them off. WebFetch sends each hostname to api.anthropic.com for a safety-blocklist check (skipWebFetchPreflight disables). /feedback uploads the transcript.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Commercial (Team, Enterprise, API): no training; 30-day retention; ZDR available to qualified Enterprise accounts (disables cloud sessions, Remote Control, Claude Tag, artifacts and feedback). Consumer plans follow the user's training preference (5-year or 30-day retention). Local transcripts sit in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com, platform.claude.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com (claude.ai connectors), downloads.claude.ai, registry.npmjs.org, bridge.claudeusercontent.com (Chrome), plus optional Datadog intake hosts for telemetry. HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT/KEY mTLS are supported; SOCKS is not.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: code.claude.com/docs (machine-readable map at claude_code_docs_map.md)

items.title: Managed settings via MDM, GPO or the admin console
body: Endpoint paths: macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json (plus a managed-settings.d/ drop-in directory), Linux and WSL /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json — the legacy ProgramData path is no longer read as of v2.1.75 (CVE-2026-35603). OS-policy channels: the macOS managed-preference domain com.anthropic.claudecode and the Windows registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode (HKCU is a user-writable fallback, not an enforcement channel).

Server-managed settings cover the same keys from Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings (Owner role), with a caveat the docs state plainly: it is a client-side control, not a security boundary, and it is skipped when routing through Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a custom base URL. Endpoint management via MDM is the stronger channel; forceRemoteSettingsRefresh makes the server channel fail closed at startup. Cloud sessions read only server-managed settings; Cowork sessions never fetch them.

items.title: Permission, MCP and hook lockdown
body: Pin permission rules with permissions.allow / deny / ask, and set allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly to block user- and project-level rules (and --allowedTools) entirely. permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode and permissions.disableAutoMode remove the bypass and auto modes; autoMode.environment / hard_deny / soft_deny tune the auto-mode classifier, which the docs describe as a second gate after permissions.deny.

MCP admission: allowedMcpServers is the allowlist — undefined means unrestricted and an empty array is a full lockdown — with deniedMcpServers winning on conflict, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, managedMcpServers to push remote servers, and a managed-mcp.json file for exclusive control of MCP configuration. Hooks and sideloading close the remaining gaps: allowManagedHooksOnly, disableAllHooks, allowedHttpHookUrls, strictPluginOnlyCustomization, strictKnownMarketplaces / blockedMarketplaces, disableCommandPluginSources, and disableSideloadFlags to reject --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at the command line.

links.title: Control MCP server access for your organization

items.title: Forced login, credentials and audit telemetry
body: forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID pin sessions to the organisation; forceLoginOrgUUID also blocks startup on ambient API-key credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, apiKeyHelper). apiKeyHelper substitutes a managed credential script for stored keys; credentials otherwise live in the macOS Keychain or a 0600 ~/.claude/.credentials.json.

Fleet-wide audit: set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and the OTEL_* exporter variables in the managed env block; when the exporter endpoint comes from managed settings, conflicting developer-set OTel variables are removed at startup. Sessions then emit per-tool decision events, prompt and API events (text redacted by default) and usage metrics to the organisation's collector. Enterprise organisations can also pull local Claude Code session transcripts through the Compliance API.

riskNotes.note: Every file, web page, MCP result and IDE selection Claude reads is untrusted input. Anthropic's own mitigations are the permission prompts, an auto-mode classifier, an isolated context window for WebFetch and command-injection detection; the docs are explicit that no system is immune and recommend VMs for untrusted content. The hard controls are permissions.deny, PreToolUse hooks and the sandbox network allowlist.

Project files (.mcp.json, .claude/settings.json hooks, CLAUDE.md) are configuration the repository author controls. CVE-2025-59536 and CVE-2026-21852 showed they could execute code or redirect ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL before the trust prompt. allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, allowManagedHooksOnly, strictPluginOnlyCustomization and allowManagedMcpServersOnly move those decisions to the managed tier.

Read-only Bash commands can read the whole machine by default, including ~/.aws and ~/.ssh; sandbox.credentials deny/mask entries, sandbox.filesystem.denyRead and Read() deny rules are how an organisation fences secrets. Session transcripts are stored in plaintext locally and, with Remote Control, on Anthropic servers.

Auto mode is the built-in starting mode on Pro, Max and Team. There is no managed per-session token or turn budget in the CLI; spend is bounded at the organisation level (admin spend limits, Console workspace limits, or gateway per-user limits) and per run only through --max-turns and --max-budget-usd in print mode and GitHub Actions use.

Background agents (claude agents, --bg), agent teams, cross-session messaging and Remote Control all start Claude Code processes outside the developer's terminal; disableAgentView, processWrapper (corporate launcher), crossSessionInbound and disableRemoteControl are the switches.
