body: Deploy forceLoginMethod ("claudeai" or "console") and forceLoginOrgUUID (your org UUID from claude.ai/admin-settings/organization) through MDM or managed-settings.json; sessions on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper are then blocked at startup.

steps.title: Enforce SSO and SCIM at the organisation
body: Turn on "Require SSO for Claude" at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization after domain verification; Enterprise adds SCIM group-to-role mapping and automatic deprovisioning.

steps.title: On Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry use the Claude apps gateway
body: Run claude gateway with an OIDC IdP; developers sign in with corporate SSO, receive short-lived bearer tokens, and lose access when deprovisioned in the IdP.

controls.mechanism: Managed permissions.deny / ask / allow rules with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, and managed PreToolUse hooks (command, http, mcp_tool) under allowManagedHooksOnly, evaluated by the harness before every tool call in every permission mode; each decision is emitted as a claude_code.tool_decision event

steps.title: Author deny and ask rules no mode can override
body: Put permissions.deny and permissions.ask rules such as Bash(curl *), Read(./secrets/**) and mcp__server__tool in managed settings and set allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly so user, project, local, --settings and --allowedTools rules are ignored.

steps.title: Add a managed PreToolUse policy hook
body: Deploy a managed hooks.PreToolUse entry whose command or HTTP endpoint returns permissionDecision "deny" or "ask"; PreToolUse hooks fire before any permission-mode check, and a deny holds even with --dangerously-skip-permissions.

steps.title: Run only the organisation's hooks
body: Set allowManagedHooksOnly true in managed settings so user, project, local and non-forced plugin hooks are blocked and only managed hooks decide.

steps.title: Log every decision
body: Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY and OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER in the managed env block so each claude_code.tool_decision event, with its decision and source (config, hook or user), reaches your collector.

controls.note: Native: deterministic, admin-locked rules and hooks decide every built-in and MCP tool call outside the model, in every mode including bypassPermissions, and the decision is logged. Outside the decision point: files pulled in with an @ reference (no tool call; use a Read deny rule), EndConversation, what a remote MCP server does after the call, and processes a plugin's hooks or MCP servers start on their own. Bash deny patterns match the command as written, so pair them with a hook or the sandbox. The auto-mode classifier is a second, non-deterministic gate that deny and ask rules precede. Server-managed delivery is a client-side control; MDM delivery is the stronger channel.

original.mechanism: permissions.deny / ask / allow rules in managed settings plus PreToolUse hooks (command, http, mcp_tool); deny rules and hooks run before every permission mode, including bypassPermissions and the auto-mode classifier

steps.title: Author deny rules that no mode can override
body: Put permissions.deny entries such as Bash(curl *), Read(./.env), Read(./secrets/**) and mcp__* patterns in managed settings and set allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly so user, project and --allowedTools rules are ignored.

steps.title: Add a PreToolUse policy hook
body: Deploy a managed hooks.PreToolUse entry whose command or HTTP endpoint returns permissionDecision "deny" or "ask"; hooks fire in every permission mode and a hook deny applies even with --dangerously-skip-permissions.

steps.title: Constrain the auto-mode classifier
body: Deliver an autoMode block (environment, hard_deny, soft_deny, allow, classifyAllShell) through managed settings; note the docs call the classifier a second gate that permissions.deny always precedes.

original.note: Deny rules and hooks are deterministic and run before every mode, including bypass; the auto-mode classifier is not deterministic. Subagents inherit the rules; MCP tools are matched by mcp_tool hooks; a remote MCP server's own side effects are outside the hook.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center artifacts feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance table and Request access)
Claude Code security page (links the Trust Center)

controls.note: External: the assessment, its evidence expiry and the reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform, not in Claude Code. The Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, HIPAA and NIST 800-171 coverage for Claude Enterprise and the Anthropic API (Claude Team: all but HIPAA), with the reports, questionnaires and an infrastructure diagram behind Request access.

original.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 artifacts) feeds the buyer's TPRM platform
original.note: Vendor assurance artifacts are published at trust.anthropic.com and linked from the security page; the reassessment cadence and evidence expiry live in the organisation's own TPRM tooling, not in Claude Code.

steps.title: Collect vendor evidence from the Trust Center
body: Download the SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate referenced on the Claude Code security page and attach them to the vendor record.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) send each governed Claude Code request, with its tool calls and results, to the organisation's AI security server for an allow/deny verdict; a managed UserPromptSubmit hook can block a typed prompt; sandbox.credentials mask entries give sandboxed commands a placeholder; Read deny rules keep named paths out

steps.title: Inspect governed requests with Inference hooks
body: In claude.ai Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks, turn on Allow for your organization, register your AI security server and choose failure handling; Anthropic holds each governed request until the server returns allow or deny.

steps.title: Block prompts on the device
body: Deploy a managed UserPromptSubmit hook that passes the prompt to your DLP inspector and returns decision "block", which stops the prompt and erases it from context.

steps.title: Mask named secrets in the sandbox
body: List secrets under sandbox.credentials.envVars and sandbox.credentials.files with mode "mask" and set sandbox.network.tlsTerminate, so sandboxed commands see a placeholder and the proxy substitutes the value only for allowed hosts.

steps.title: Keep secret files out of context
body: Add managed permissions.deny rules such as Read(./.env) and Read(./secrets/**); matching files are excluded from discovery and reads.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: detection is the organisation's own inspector at two attach points — Anthropic-side Inference hooks (Enterprise claude.ai logins only; not Console API keys, Bedrock or Google Cloud) and a device-side hook — plus product masking of the secrets you list, inside the sandbox only. Inference hooks allow or deny (no redaction), read extracted attachment text but not images, have no response-side event yet, and fail open or closed by your failure-handling setting. Read deny rules are data minimisation, not detection.

original.mechanism: Read() / Edit() deny rules, sandbox.credentials masking and sandbox.filesystem.denyRead keep named secrets out of the context; Enterprise Inference hooks send each governed prompt to the organisation's AI security server for an allow/deny verdict

steps.title: Exclude sensitive files from the context
body: Add permissions.deny rules such as Read(./.env), Read(./.env.*) and Read(//**/.pem) in managed settings; the JetBrains and VS Code extensions honour Read deny rules for selection sharing too.

steps.title: Mask credentials inside the sandbox
body: Set sandbox.credentials.files and sandbox.credentials.envVars with mode deny or mask so sandboxed commands see placeholders and the proxy re-injects the real value only for allowed hosts.

steps.title: Inspect prompts inline with Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta)
body: Configure an AI security server endpoint; Anthropic POSTs each governed Claude Code prompt transcript for an allow/deny verdict before inference, with shadow mode and rollout percentages.

original.note: Deny rules and credential masking restrict paths; they inspect nothing. Inference hooks deliver each governed prompt to the organisation's own AI security server, so content inspection exists only where the organisation runs that server. Pastes and tool results outside governed prompts are not covered.

controls.mechanism: permissions.allow / ask / deny with tool specifiers, bare-name deny rules that remove a tool, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, permissions.defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode, disableAutoMode, additionalDirectories and blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories in managed settings

steps.title: Fix the starting mode and remove the escape hatches
body: In managed settings set permissions.defaultMode, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode "disable" and permissions.disableAutoMode "disable".

steps.title: Remove tools or scope them
body: Deny WebFetch or mcp__* by bare name to remove the tool, scope the rest with specifiers such as Bash(git push *), Read(./secrets/**) and mcp__server__tool, and set allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly so only managed rules count.

steps.title: Fence file access
body: Set permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories true and control permissions.additionalDirectories so reads and edits stay inside approved roots in every mode.

controls.note: Native: admin-locked allow, ask and deny per tool with argument and path specifiers, enforced by the harness outside the model, with bypass and auto modes removable. Limits: Bash specifiers match the command text (the sandbox is the OS-level backstop); MCP tools are scoped by server and tool name, not arguments; a resource-level limit such as one repository or bucket isn't expressible for most tools; tools run with the developer's own authority.

original.mechanism: permissions.allow/ask/deny with tool specifiers, bare-name deny rules that remove a tool from Claude's context, permissions.defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode, disableAutoMode, additionalDirectories and blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories

steps.title: Fix the starting permission mode and remove escape hatches
body: In managed settings set permissions.defaultMode, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode "disable" and permissions.disableAutoMode "disable" (auto mode can also be turned off for the organisation on Team and Enterprise).

steps.title: Remove tools or scope them
body: A bare deny such as "WebFetch" or "mcp__*" removes the tool from context; scoped rules like Bash(git push *) in permissions.ask force a prompt even in auto mode.

steps.title: Fence file access
body: Set permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories true and control permissions.additionalDirectories so reads and edits stay inside approved roots in every mode.

original.note: Bare-name deny hides a tool; allow pre-approves it; specifiers such as Bash(git push *) limit arguments. Bypass and auto modes must be disabled in managed settings or they override allow/ask; MCP tools use mcp__server__tool patterns, and a resource-level limit (which repository, which bucket) is not expressible for most tools.

controls.mechanism: sandbox.enabled with failIfUnavailable and allowUnsandboxedCommands false (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2), filesystem and network lists locked with allowManagedReadPathsOnly and allowManagedDomainsOnly; sandbox.excludedCommands has no managed-only lock

steps.title: Require the sandbox fleet-wide
body: Deliver sandbox.enabled true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable true and sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands false in managed settings, so a missing sandbox blocks startup and Claude can't retry a command unsandboxed.

steps.title: Keep developers from widening the lists
body: Set sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly and sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly in managed settings so only managed read paths and domains count.

steps.title: Pin the switches that weaken isolation
body: Set sandbox.allowAppleEvents, sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox and sandbox.network.allowAllUnixSockets to false in managed settings; Boolean sandbox keys take the managed value.

controls.note: Partial on the fall-back test: sandbox.excludedCommands merges from every settings scope with no managed-only lock, so a developer, or a repository's .claude/settings.json, can append commands that run outside the sandbox (still through the permission prompt); the vendor states this plainly. Inside: Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands and their children on macOS, Linux and WSL2; native Windows and WSL1 have no sandbox. Outside: built-in file tools (bounded by permission rules), MCP servers and hooks, the CLI process itself, and commands a developer types at the ! prompt. The proxy allows by client-supplied hostname without TLS inspection, and the sandbox shares the host kernel.

original.mechanism: sandbox.* block (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap plus socat on Linux/WSL2; not native Windows) with filesystem allow/deny paths, a hostname-allowlisting network proxy, failIfUnavailable and allowUnsandboxedCommands false

steps.title: Require the sandbox fleet-wide
body: Set sandbox.enabled true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable true and sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands false in managed settings so commands cannot fall back to running unsandboxed.

steps.title: Lock the filesystem and network lists to managed settings
body: Use sandbox.filesystem.denyRead / allowWrite with sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly, and sandbox.network.allowedDomains with sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly; these lock keys are honoured from any admin-controlled source.

steps.title: Know the limits
body: The proxy allowlists by client-supplied hostname and does not terminate TLS unless sandbox.network.tlsTerminate is set; the sandbox shares the host kernel. Use dev containers or VMs for untrusted content.

original.note: Inside the boundary: shell commands. Outside: MCP servers, WebFetch and the CLI process itself, which are bounded by permissions and network rules instead. macOS and Linux/WSL2 only — native Windows has no sandbox, so failIfUnavailable decides whether commands run unsandboxed there.

controls.mechanism: sandbox.credentials files and envVars entries (deny hides the credential; mask substitutes it at the proxy only for allowed hosts), sandbox.filesystem.denyRead, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB in the managed env block, and Unix sockets blocked in the sandbox by default; a Claude apps gateway keeps the upstream model credential off the device

steps.title: Deny credential paths to agent commands
body: In managed settings add sandbox.credentials.files entries such as ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials and envVars entries such as GITHUB_TOKEN with mode "deny"; no other settings scope can remove a deny entry.

steps.title: Inject credentials only for named hosts
body: Use mode "mask" with sandbox.network.tlsTerminate so sandboxed commands hold a placeholder and the proxy substitutes the secret only on requests to allowed hosts; sandbox.credentials.awsPairs re-signs AWS requests.

steps.title: Scrub credentials from every subprocess
body: Set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 in the managed env block to strip Anthropic, cloud-provider and other recognised credentials from Bash, hook and stdio MCP server environments.

steps.title: Keep the model credential off the device
body: Route through a Claude apps gateway so the upstream API or cloud credential stays in your infrastructure and developers hold only short-lived gateway tokens.

controls.note: Partial: the scoping is OS-enforced and admin-deliverable but lives in the Bash sandbox, which a developer can widen with sandbox.excludedCommands (no managed lock), and it covers only the paths and variables you list — there is no built-in deny list, so by default agent commands can read ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, git credential helpers, gh and cloud CLI config and browser profiles. The environment scrub reaches hooks and stdio MCP servers; credential files don't. File masking substitutes on Linux and WSL2 only (macOS blocks the file), mask needs the experimental tlsTerminate, and native Windows has no sandbox. Git, cloud CLIs and MCP servers still act as the developer; there is no on-behalf-of exchange.

original.mechanism: apiKeyHelper rotating credentials, Claude apps gateway holding the upstream key, sandbox credential masking with per-host re-injection, and per-purpose short-lived Remote Control credentials; the agent otherwise acts with the developer's own identity

steps.title: Keep the model credential out of the developer's hands
body: Route through a Claude apps gateway (developers hold only short-lived gateway tokens) or set apiKeyHelper to a vault-backed script with CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS.

steps.title: Inject tool credentials at the proxy, not in the shell
body: Use sandbox.credentials.envVars mask entries with sandbox.network.tlsTerminate so the sandbox holds placeholders and the proxy substitutes the secret only for allowed hosts; AWS SigV4 re-signing is supported via credentials.awsPairs.

original.note: Git, cloud CLI and MCP tools still run as the developer; there is no on-behalf-of exchange or delegation-chain tracking in the local product.

controls.mechanism: autoMemoryEnabled false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY in managed settings, the managed claudeMd key or managed-policy CLAUDE.md, pluginConfigs agents-md@builtin instructionFiles "managed-only", strictPluginOnlyCustomization and cleanupPeriodDays

steps.title: Decide whether auto memory runs
body: Set autoMemoryEnabled false in managed settings, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 in the managed env block, so Claude neither reads nor writes ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/.

steps.title: Load only organisation instructions
body: Set pluginConfigs "agents-md@builtin" options.instructionFiles to "managed-only" in managed settings, and put the organisation's instructions in the managed claudeMd key or the managed-policy CLAUDE.md path, which users can't exclude.

steps.title: Lock customisation sources
body: Set strictPluginOnlyCustomization true (or its skills, agents, hooks and mcp sub-keys) so user and project sources can't add instructions that run with tool access.

controls.note: Partial: an administrator can switch memory off or relocate it and narrow the instruction sources, but nothing validates, gates or reviews memory writes — Claude edits plain Markdown with its file tools and Claude Code only stamps a modified time — and memory files are exempt from the cleanupPeriodDays sweep. Under managed-only, a subdirectory's CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules files still load when Claude reads files there, and managed instructions arrive as a user message, not a system prompt. Session transcripts sit in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects for 30 days by default.

original.mechanism: autoMemoryEnabled, autoMemoryDirectory, claudeMd (managed org-wide CLAUDE.md), claudeMdExcludes, cleanupPeriodDays and fileCheckpointingEnabled in settings

steps.title: Decide whether auto memory runs
body: Set autoMemoryEnabled false (or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 in env) to stop Claude writing persistent memories under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, or point autoMemoryDirectory at a governed location.

steps.title: Bound transcript retention on the device
body: Set cleanupPeriodDays (default 30) and desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays so plaintext session transcripts are pruned.

original.note: Memory files are plain Markdown the agent edits with ordinary Write/Edit tools; there is no validation, quarantine or rollback of memory contents beyond file checkpoints.

original.mechanism: Managed policy CLAUDE.md (claudeMd key or file at the managed policy path), claudeMdExcludes, strictPluginOnlyCustomization for agents/hooks/skills, includeGitInstructions

steps.title: Deploy organisation-wide instructions
body: Put org instructions in the managed claudeMd key or the managed policy CLAUDE.md path; they load in every session and cannot be excluded by users.

steps.title: Lock custom agents, skills and hooks to managed or plugin sources
body: Set strictPluginOnlyCustomization true (or its agents / hooks / mcp sub-keys) so user and project sources cannot add instructions that run with tool access.

original.note: Project and user CLAUDE.md files remain untrusted instruction sources loaded into the same context; there is no structural hierarchy separating them from managed instructions.

controls.mechanism: Managed PostToolUse hooks that can replace a tool's output (updatedToolOutput) before Claude sees it, and Enterprise Inference hooks that send each governed request's transcript, tool results included, to the organisation's AI security server before inference; built-in safeguards are not configurable

steps.title: Screen tool results with a managed PostToolUse hook
body: Deploy a managed PostToolUse hook for WebFetch, Bash and mcp__ tools that sends the result to your injection classifier and returns updatedToolOutput with a quarantine notice; managed hooks keep running when a user sets disableAllHooks.

steps.title: Deny poisoned requests before inference
body: Allow Inference hooks for the organisation so your AI security server can deny a request whose transcript carries an injected tool result or file before the model reasons over it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: both are attach points for the organisation's own classifier; the product ships no admin-configurable input screening. Its built-in safeguards (an isolated context window for WebFetch, command-injection detection) are vendor-internal, and workspace and MCP trust prompts are admission, not screening. The auto-mode classifier judges the proposed action, not the input, and is credited under action policy. updatedToolOutput changes only what Claude sees (telemetry keeps the original); @-referenced files, CLAUDE.md and memory enter context without a tool call; Inference hooks cover Enterprise claude.ai logins only.

original.mechanism: Built-in context-aware analysis, command-injection detection, fail-closed command matching, an isolated context window for WebFetch, the auto-mode classifier's exfiltration rules, and the WebFetch hostname safety check

steps.title: Keep the built-in safeguards on
body: Do not set skipWebFetchPreflight; keep permissions.deny for curl/wget and rely on the auto-mode classifier's built-in hard_deny data-exfiltration rule by including "$defaults" in any autoMode override.

steps.title: Treat repositories and MCP servers as untrusted
body: Trust verification runs for new folders and MCP servers in interactive mode only (not with -p); use managed MCP allowlists and strictPluginOnlyCustomization so a checked-in file cannot add tools or hooks.

original.note: These are model- and heuristic-based; Anthropic states no system is immune. There is no admin-configurable classifier or third-party detector hook in the local product beyond PreToolUse hooks and Enterprise Inference hooks.

controls.mechanism: macOS Keychain storage (a 0600 ~/.claude/.credentials.json on Linux, a profile-protected file on Windows); rotating credentials through apiKeyHelper, awsCredentialExport, gcpAuthRefresh and otelHeadersHelper; short-lived Claude apps gateway tokens; keyless workload identity federation in GitHub Actions; managed forceLoginOrgUUID or forceLoginMethod "gateway" to refuse environment keys

steps.title: Use a helper instead of a stored key
body: Set apiKeyHelper in managed settings to a script that fetches a short-lived token from your vault; Claude Code re-runs it after five minutes (CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS), on a 401 or 403, and when a cached JWT has expired.

steps.title: Make machines gateway-only
body: Set forceLoginMethod "gateway" and forceLoginGatewayUrl in an on-machine managed source so Claude Code ignores leftover logins, API keys and apiKeyHelper and uses only the gateway's short-lived token.

steps.title: Go keyless in CI
body: In GitHub Actions pass anthropic_federation_rule_id and anthropic_organization_id with id-token: write instead of an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret.

steps.title: Refuse environment keys on claude.ai-login fleets
body: A managed forceLoginOrgUUID blocks startup on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and apiKeyHelper, so use it where developers sign in with claude.ai rather than through a helper.

controls.note: Partial: short-lived and keyless options exist and some static keys can be refused, but storage is encrypted only in the macOS Keychain (Linux and Windows keep a plaintext file protected by file permissions), and long-lived credentials aren't fully blockable: claude setup-token mints a one-year CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, a Console login under forceLoginOrgUUID creates and stores an API key, and cloud-provider credentials in the environment are neither refused nor held to gateway-only mode. Values in a settings env block are plain text. Keeping secrets out of the model's context is the sandbox masking under D3-CTS.

original.mechanism: apiKeyHelper / otelHeadersHelper / awsCredentialExport / gcpAuthRefresh scripts for rotating credentials; macOS Keychain or 0600 credentials file; CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and GitHub Actions secrets or workload identity federation for CI

steps.title: Use helper scripts instead of static keys
body: Set apiKeyHelper (re-run every five minutes by default) to fetch a short-lived token from your vault; forceLoginOrgUUID blocks ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY use.

steps.title: Go keyless in CI
body: In GitHub Actions pass anthropic_federation_rule_id and anthropic_organization_id with id-token write so the workflow exchanges its OIDC token for Claude API access through a Console service account; on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry use OIDC as well.

original.note: Storage (Keychain or a 0600 file) and ephemeral issuance (helper scripts, federation) are separate claims — a stored long-lived key is not ephemeral. Readers: shell commands read the developer's environment unless the sandbox masks it; the model sees a secret only if a tool returns it; MCP servers get their own configured credentials.

controls.mechanism: allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers serverUrl and serverCommand entries with allowManagedMcpServersOnly, an exclusive managed-mcp.json, strictKnownMarketplaces / blockedMarketplaces for plugins, plugin archive sha256 pins, and organisation connector tool controls (ask / blocked)

steps.title: Admit servers by exact command or URL
body: Deliver allowedMcpServers with serverCommand entries (the exact argv, including a pinned package version such as npx -y pkg@1.2.3) and serverUrl entries plus allowManagedMcpServersOnly, or deploy managed-mcp.json for exclusive control; serverName entries are not a control.

steps.title: Restrict plugin sources
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces, and disableSideloadFlags, so plugins and the MCP servers they carry come only from sources you list.

steps.title: Gate connector tools
body: Set individual claude.ai connector tools to ask or blocked in the organisation's connector tool controls; Claude Code enforces them in every mode.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits servers but pins nothing they serve. An exact serverCommand match that names a versioned package is version pinning for stdio servers only; remote serverUrl servers stay unpinned, list_changed notifications refresh a server's tool definitions with no re-approval, nothing scans tool descriptions, and Anthropic reviews Directory listings but doesn't security-audit MCP servers. A plugin archive's sha256 pin verifies the download, not the servers it starts.

original.mechanism: allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers / allowManagedMcpServersOnly / managedMcpServers, exclusive managed-mcp.json, disableClaudeAiConnectors, org connector tool controls (ask / blocked), strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces for plugins

steps.title: Deploy a fixed server set or an allowlist
body: Place managed-mcp.json in the system directory for exclusive control (an empty mcpServers object disables MCP entirely), or deliver allowedMcpServers plus allowManagedMcpServersOnly through server-managed settings.

steps.title: Restrict plugin and marketplace sources
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces to an allowlist (an empty array blocks every marketplace), blockedMarketplaces, disableCommandPluginSources true and disableSideloadFlags true.

steps.title: Mark sensitive MCP tools as always-ask
body: Servers can set _meta anthropic/requiresUserInteraction so a tool always prompts; claude.ai connector tools an Owner sets to ask or blocked are enforced in every mode.

original.note: Rated native on the same rule as Copilot CLI, Codex and Cowork: an exclusive managed-mcp.json and the allowlist admit servers by identity, and marketplace restrictions admit plugins by source. Admission is not integrity — Anthropic reviews Directory connectors against listing criteria but does not security-audit MCP servers, and nothing pins the tool descriptions a server returns or detects a changed implementation.

controls.mechanism: Managed permissions.ask rules (prompt in every mode, including auto and bypassPermissions), disableBypassPermissionsMode and disableAutoMode, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly (hides the always-allow choices) and allowManagedHooksOnly (no user hook answers prompts)

steps.title: Force a human checkpoint on named actions
body: Add permissions.ask entries such as Bash(git push *) and Bash(gh pr create *) to managed settings; the prompt shows the command, and no mode, allow rule or classifier can approve it silently.

steps.title: Remove the modes and persistence that bypass it
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode and disableAutoMode to "disable" and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly true, which hides the always-allow choices and stops saving new rules.

steps.title: Decide whether sandboxed commands prompt
body: Set sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed false in managed settings if sandboxed Bash commands should go through the prompt too.

controls.note: Native: a present developer approves each matched action with its current arguments, and an administrator can force the prompt and remove the modes and persistence that bypass it. Boundaries: acceptEdits stays selectable (in-scope edits and mkdir, touch, rm, mv, cp and sed run unprompted); a managed PermissionRequest hook can answer prompts; Remote Control approvals come from a phone; -p runs and GitHub Actions have no present human, so matched calls are denied or answered by the host. The auto-mode classifier is not human approval.

original.mechanism: Manual permission mode, permissions.ask rules (honoured even in auto mode), plan mode, PreToolUse hooks returning "ask", and GitHub Actions gating by write access and human actor

steps.title: Force a human checkpoint on named actions
body: Add permissions.ask entries such as Bash(git push *) and Bash(gh pr create *); an explicit ask rule prompts even when auto mode or an allow rule would otherwise approve.

steps.title: Keep the mode set that asks
body: Set permissions.defaultMode "default" and disable auto and bypass modes so edits and non-read-only commands prompt; Accept Edits still asks outside the working directory and for critical paths.

controls.mechanism: claude.ai Organization settings > Plugins & skills (Inventory with source, version, capabilities and audience; Requests review; organisation marketplaces) enforced in Claude Code by strictKnownMarketplaces and strictPluginOnlyCustomization; MCP servers admitted by allowedMcpServers or managed-mcp.json; the Claude Code capability in Enterprise custom roles

steps.title: Keep the organisation's registry
body: Publish approved plugins and skills through Organization settings > Plugins & skills (Marketplaces tab), review submissions on the Requests tab, and track source and version on the Inventory tab.

steps.title: Make Claude Code consult it
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces to a hostPattern entry matching claude.ai, plus any marketplace you declare in managed settings, so Claude Code refuses plugins from any other source.

steps.title: Refuse unregistered skills, agents, hooks and servers
body: Set strictPluginOnlyCustomization true so skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers can come only from plugins or managed settings.

steps.title: Gate who runs Claude Code
body: On Enterprise, grant the Claude Code capability only through custom roles under Organization settings > Roles.

controls.note: Partial: the registry exists and the client can be forced to consult it for plugins, skills and subagents, but tool servers configured in managed settings or managed-mcp.json have no owner, version or approval record there, the claude.ai host entry also admits the claude.ai default marketplaces, and the Claude Code installations and sessions themselves aren't registry entries — seats, the analytics dashboard and OpenTelemetry attributes are the only inventory of those.

original.mechanism: Seat assignment and per-role Claude Code capability in the claude.ai admin console; disableAgentView, agent teams and cross-session messaging flags; the analytics dashboard lists active users and sessions

steps.title: Gate who may run Claude Code
body: Assign Claude Code access by seat (Organization settings > Organization) and, on Enterprise, by custom role and group under Organization settings > Roles.

steps.title: Control background and peer agents
body: Set disableAgentView true to turn off claude agents, --bg and the supervisor; crossSessionInbound and isolatePeerMachines govern cross-session messaging.

original.note: There is no registry of agents or tool servers with owners and approval state; the analytics dashboard and OpenTelemetry attributes (organization.id, user.account_uuid, session.id) are the inventory.

controls.mechanism: Domain memberships report for verified domains (claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, Domains), with Restrict organization creation, Require SSO and the proxy-injected tenant-restriction header as prevention

steps.title: List the accounts on your verified domains
body: After domain verification, open Domain memberships in the Domains section at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization and download the Claude and Console accounts on your domains as CSV or JSON.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the vendor lists personal and other-organisation accounts on the organisation's verified domains, but doesn't find Claude Code installs on devices, accounts under personal email addresses, or API keys from other organisations — EDR/MDM inventory of the claude binary and ~/.claude, and SSE/CASB, cover those. Prevention, credited here only: Restrict organization creation (Organization and access, Security), Require SSO for Claude, the anthropic-allowed-org-ids tenant-restriction header (Enterprise) and a managed forceLoginOrgUUID.

original.mechanism: Tenant restrictions header (anthropic-allowed-org-ids) injected by the corporate proxy; the analytics dashboard shows who is active; endpoint tooling finds unmanaged installs
original.note: Claude Code does not discover unsanctioned installs; the vendor lever is the proxy-injected tenant-restrictions header that blocks personal-account use, plus IP allowlisting. Pair with EDR/SSE inventory of the claude binary and ~/.claude directories.

steps.title: Block personal accounts on the corporate network
body: Configure the TLS-inspecting proxy to inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your org UUIDs for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com.

controls.mechanism: OpenTelemetry from the managed env block (user_prompt, tool_decision, tool_result, api_request, permission mode, hook and managed-settings events keyed by session.id and user.account_uuid), with the managed endpoint removing developer-set destinations; Compliance API local-session transcripts (Enterprise); admin-console settings changes in the audit log

steps.title: Export every session's events to your collector
body: In the managed env block set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER and OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER to otlp and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; Claude Code removes developer-set endpoints, and a repository's settings can't enable or redirect export.

steps.title: Decide what content is captured
body: Set OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS in managed settings; prompts are redacted and tool parameters omitted by default.

steps.title: Pull transcripts after the fact
body: Enterprise organisations list and retrieve local Claude Code transcripts from /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local with a Compliance Access Key carrying read:compliance_user_data.

steps.title: Audit policy changes
body: Changes to server-managed settings are audit events, with the actor and the previous and new values, in the Compliance API or audit log export.

controls.note: Native: the export is admin-enforced and per-session, and a developer can't turn it off from settings when the variables come from managed settings (a managed env value overrides the shell). Capture is not tamper resistance: durability and non-repudiation belong to the collector. Gaps: server-managed delivery is skipped on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (use MDM there); a modified binary escapes any client-side control; Compliance API transcripts exclude Console API-key, cloud-provider and ZDR sessions; OpenTelemetry tool results are metadata unless content capture is turned on.

original.mechanism: OpenTelemetry events (claude_code.tool_decision, tool_result, user_prompt, api_request) with user.account_uuid and organization.id; Compliance API local-session transcripts (Enterprise); ConfigChange hooks; server-managed settings change audit

steps.title: Export tool decisions fleet-wide
body: In the managed env block set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; developer overrides of the exporter are removed at startup. Add OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 only if the collector may hold commands.

steps.title: Pull transcripts after the fact
body: Enterprise organisations retrieve Claude Code local-session transcripts (prompts, tool calls, results; 6-year retention by default) with a Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope.

steps.title: Audit settings edits
body: Add a ConfigChange hook to log or block user_settings / project_settings changes; policy_settings changes cannot be blocked and server-managed changes are audited through the Compliance API.

original.note: Native event emission and Compliance API transcripts; durability and tamper evidence are the collector's and the archive's. Events carry the user's account id, which is attribution, not a signature — non-repudiation needs the organisation's immutable store.

controls.mechanism: A managed permissions.deny ["*"] delivered to running sessions on the policy refresh; seat or SCIM removal and Sign out everywhere; requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion and forceRemoteSettingsRefresh at startup; disableRemoteControl and disableAgentView

steps.title: Stop tool use fleet-wide
body: Deliver permissions.deny ["*"] as a managed setting; running sessions apply it without a restart on the next policy check (server-managed hourly, MDM or HKLM every 30 minutes, the managed file on change).

steps.title: Cut the member's access
body: Remove the member from the IdP app or SCIM group (Enterprise) or from the organisation's members list.

steps.title: Revoke the member's sessions and devices
body: Use Sign out everywhere in the admin console to revoke every session and enrolled trusted device for that member.

steps.title: Refuse to start outside policy
body: Deliver requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion, and set forceRemoteSettingsRefresh true so clients exit when the server policy can't be fetched.

controls.note: Partial: there is no documented admin stop for a running local session. A managed deny-all halts tool calls within the refresh interval, but the process and its model calls continue; how long a running CLI session keeps working after seat, SCIM or Sign out everywhere revocation is not documented (delay not documented); requiredMinimumVersion and forceRemoteSettingsRefresh act at the next start only. An EDR process kill is the external complement, and local transcripts must be deleted on the device.

original.mechanism: Seat removal / SCIM deprovisioning, /logout revocation, requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh fail-closed startup, and disableRemoteControl / disableAgentView

steps.title: Cut access at the identity layer
body: Remove the seat or SCIM group; Console API keys are deleted in the Console; a gateway sign-in expires within the session lifetime (one hour by default).

steps.title: Refuse to start outside policy
body: Deliver requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion, and set forceRemoteSettingsRefresh true so clients exit when the server policy cannot be fetched.

original.note: Running sessions keep working until credentials expire; there is no server-side "stop all sessions" for local clients. Local transcripts must be deleted on the device.

controls.mechanism: EDR on the host; integration points are processWrapper / CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER (corporate launcher), OpenTelemetry tool events carrying each command, and an in-distro Linux sensor for WSL

evidence.title: Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher
Set up Claude Code for your organization (WSL sensor note)
Monitoring (tool decision and tool result events)

controls.note: External (EDR): Claude Code analyses no process behaviour. Integration points for the sensor: processWrapper or CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER in managed settings starts the background service, agent-view, Remote Control and teammate processes through your launcher (macOS and Linux; ignored on Windows; sessions started in a terminal and a deep link's first process start outside it); OpenTelemetry tool_decision and tool_result events carry each Bash full_command when OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS is set, for correlation in the SIEM; WSL 2 processes are invisible to Windows-side sensors, so run the vendor's Linux sensor in the distribution.

original.mechanism: processWrapper / CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER corporate launcher for every self-spawned process; OTel tool events feed the SIEM; WSL sessions need an in-distro Linux sensor

steps.title: Route every Claude Code process through the corporate launcher
body: Set processWrapper (or env CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER) in managed settings to your launcher's absolute path; it wraps the background service, agent-view sessions and Remote Control processes (not Windows).

steps.title: Cover WSL sessions
body: Windows-side sensors do not see WSL 2 processes; run your EDR vendor's Linux sensor inside the distribution or rely on the identical OTel tool-execution telemetry.

original.note: Sensor scope: the host, where the CLI and its child processes run; the corporate launcher makes every self-spawned process visible to it. WSL sessions need a Linux sensor in the distro. Hooks are not a sensor — they are where the sensor can be consulted before a tool call.

controls.mechanism: sandbox.network.allowedDomains / deniedDomains with strictAllowlist and allowManagedDomainsOnly for sandboxed commands, managed WebFetch(domain:) rules for the fetch tool, and HTTPS_PROXY with the documented host list at the firewall

steps.title: Allowlist sandbox egress from managed settings
body: Deliver sandbox.network.allowedDomains with sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly true (and strictAllowlist), so sandboxed commands reach only listed hosts and others are blocked, not prompted.

steps.title: Restrict the fetch tool
body: Allow only WebFetch(domain:host) rules in managed settings with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, or deny WebFetch outright.

steps.title: Pin the proxy and firewall allowlist
body: Set HTTPS_PROXY and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS in the managed env block and allow only the documented hosts at the firewall, which is what bounds MCP servers and the CLI's own traffic.

controls.note: Partial on the same finding as D3-EI: the allowlist is admin-lockable but doesn't cover every agent-executed command, because sandbox.excludedCommands (no managed lock) lets a developer run named commands outside the sandbox with the host's network. Also outside it: MCP servers and hooks, the CLI's own API traffic, and native Windows. The proxy decides on the client-supplied hostname without TLS inspection (domain fronting is possible), and a configured proxy is routing until direct egress is blocked at the host.

original.mechanism: sandbox.network.allowedDomains / deniedDomains / strictAllowlist / allowManagedDomainsOnly, WebFetch(domain:) rules, permissions.deny for curl/wget, HTTPS_PROXY / NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, and the documented outbound host list

steps.title: Allowlist sandbox egress from managed settings
body: Set sandbox.network.allowedDomains, sandbox.network.strictAllowlist true and sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly true; non-allowed hosts are then blocked instead of prompting, for Bash and its child processes.

steps.title: Restrict the fetch tool and network commands
body: Deny WebFetch or allow only WebFetch(domain:host) entries, and deny Bash(curl *) and Bash(wget *); the docs note deny rules match the command as written, so pair them with the sandbox allowlist.

steps.title: Pin the proxy and firewall allowlist
body: Deliver HTTPS_PROXY and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS in the managed env block and allow only the documented hosts (api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, downloads.claude.ai, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com and so on) at the firewall.

original.note: Sandbox network rules bound sandboxed commands and WebFetch rules bound WebFetch; MCP servers and the CLI's own calls are bounded only by HTTPS_PROXY and host network policy. A configured proxy is routing until direct egress is blocked at the host.

controls.mechanism: Skill and plugin security scanning (Enterprise) of third-party skills and plugins uploaded to the claude.ai organisation, which reach Claude Code as synced plugins or claude.ai marketplaces; plugin archive sha256 pins; the package mirror sits outside, reached through the sandbox domain allowlist

steps.title: Scan uploaded skills and plugins
body: Turn on Skill and plugin security scanning under Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Policy; a fail result blocks the uploaded skill or plugin before anyone in the organisation can use it.

steps.title: Take plugins only through that path
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces to a hostPattern entry for claude.ai so Claude Code installs plugins from your organisation's claude.ai marketplaces.

steps.title: Force dependency installs through your scanning mirror
body: Point package managers at your mirror and allow only its host in sandbox.network.allowedDomains with allowManagedDomainsOnly, so sandboxed installs can't reach public registries directly.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the vendor scans one artifact class — third-party skills and plugins uploaded to the organisation (Enterprise; off by default until 2026-10-02) — and not MCP servers or hooks, skills shared through MCP, items that predate enablement, CMEK, ZDR or HIPAA organisations, or plugins a developer installs from a git marketplace. The archive sha256 pin verifies integrity, not content. Dependencies Claude installs are out of the product's reach: admission scanning at the package mirror or artifact repository is the external control. Claude Code loads no model weights locally.

original.note: Not applicable to the product: Claude Code loads no model artifacts locally; inference is remote on the configured provider. Nothing to scan on the endpoint.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for applicability (2026-09-10)

original.note: The vendor ships pinned versions (requiredMinimumVersion, SDK-bundled binary, plugin archive SHA-256 digests) but no signed manifest of the models, plugins and MCP servers a session composes; the March 2026 npm source-map exposure showed release packaging is not attested. Generate an AI-BOM from managed settings, managed-mcp.json and the plugin marketplace lockfile yourself.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed; no setting for this control (2026-09-10)
