items.title: Enable cloud sessions per role, not per organisation
body: Organization settings > Cowork > "Run Cowork in the cloud" is off by default on Enterprise; grant it through custom roles to the groups that need unattended or device-independent sessions, and leave "Enable for your organization" scoped the same way.

links.title: Use Claude Cowork on Team and Enterprise plans

items.title: Set the network-access policy before the first session
body: Cloud sandboxes inherit the organisation's network-access setting under Organization settings > Capabilities; the Enterprise default is no access. Device keys such as coworkEgressAllowedHosts do not reach cloud sessions.

riskNotes.note: Documents, connector results and browser pages enter an unattended session as instruction; the network-access policy and the connector approval toggles are the containment, and "Automatically approve" removes the per-tool prompt.
Scheduled tasks run with no device and no person present; the Compliance API's list of remote sessions, including agent-owned scheduled runs, is the inventory.
Sessions and their files are saved to the account and retained for years unless deleted; the session can reach a device's folders whenever the desktop app is open there.

controls.mechanism: "Run Cowork in the cloud" at Organization settings > Cowork plus the "Cowork in the cloud (beta)" custom-role capability on Enterprise; only the signed-in account owner starts or steers a session; a trusted-device and recent-sign-in requirement for cloud sessions; the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome toggles govern the reach-back into devices

steps.title: Gate cloud sessions by role
body: On Enterprise turn on "Run Cowork in the cloud" at Organization settings > Cowork and grant the Cowork in the cloud capability to groups through custom roles; on Team it is on by default, so turn it off there deliberately.

steps.title: Require trusted devices for cloud sessions
body: In the organisation's cloud-session controls require trusted-device enrollment and a recent sign-in; it then applies to every cloud session in the organisation.

steps.title: Decide the reach-back into devices
body: Toggle the built-in browser at Organization settings > Cowork and Claude in Chrome at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: enablement is per role on Enterprise (organisation-wide only on Team) and there is no repository, bot or channel trigger, but the trigger condition is fixed by the vendor (the account owner, from any of their devices), scheduled tasks, which start sessions with nobody present, have no switch of their own on standard deployments (scheduledTasksEnabled is a 3P key), and the trusted-device requirement is described without a named toggle. Sessions cannot be shared with other members.

original.mechanism: "Run Cowork in the cloud" per custom role; trusted-device enrolment; SSO at the account layer

steps.title: Gate cloud sessions by role
body: On Enterprise the cloud toggle is off by default and granted through custom roles; Team turns it on by default, so turn it off there deliberately.

controls.mechanism: An isolated, temporary sandbox per session on Anthropic-managed infrastructure, created when the session starts and destroyed when it ends, sharing no state with other sessions or organisations and unable to reach private, internal, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses; always on

steps.title: Record the isolation claim
body: The architecture overview states one sandbox per session, destroyed at the end, with no state shared across sessions or organisations; there is no setting to change.

controls.note: Native by the rule: one sandbox per session, reclaimed after it, documented by the vendor, with assurance through assessment rather than a setting. Outside it: the reach-back to a member's device (local files, the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome run there, only while the desktop app is online and only for connected folders), connector calls and web fetch or web search, which run on Anthropic's servers.

original.mechanism: Per-session ephemeral sandbox on Anthropic servers; always on, no toggle
original.note: Vendor-internal isolation with no administrator setting; the architecture overview is the claim, assurance is the evidence.

steps.title: Read the architecture overview
body: Each cloud session runs in its own ephemeral sandbox with no access to the organisation's network by default; local folders are reachable only through the desktop app's brokered connection.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's network-access policy (Organization settings > Capabilities, Code execution and file creation, "Allow network egress") enforced by a mandatory proxy outside the sandbox that it cannot reconfigure or bypass; no network access by default on Enterprise; applied when a session is created

steps.title: Choose the network-access level
body: At Organization settings > Capabilities keep "Allow network egress" off or choose package managers and specific domains, listing only the hosts sessions need.

steps.title: Confirm cloud sessions inherit it
body: Cloud sessions use the same network-access setting as local Cowork and chat, enforced by the mandatory egress proxy.

controls.note: Native by the rule: an admin-authored allowlist members cannot change, enforced around the sandbox. The setup and agent phases are not separated, every allowlist preset keeps public package managers, and changes reach new sessions only. Outside it: connector calls and web fetch or web search (server side; web search can be turned off at Organization settings > Capabilities), the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome on the member's device, and the inference API. Device egress keys do not apply.

original.mechanism: Organisation network-access policy enforced by a mandatory sandbox proxy
original.note: The policy is set at Organization settings > Capabilities and applies to every cloud session; device egress keys do not apply.

steps.title: Choose the network-access level
body: Enterprise defaults to no access; widen to an allowlist only for the groups whose sessions need the web.

controls.mechanism: Connector authorisation tokens never enter the sandbox and connector calls are made on the server side; the sandbox holds only session-scoped tokens that expire within hours; there is no repository credential

steps.title: Record the credential boundary
body: The architecture overview states the sandbox holds only session-scoped tokens that expire within hours and that connector tokens never enter it; nothing is configured.

steps.title: Narrow what connector grants reach
body: At Organization settings > Connectors set up Managed authorization for supported connectors with chosen Scopes and Applied roles, so the IdP issues and revokes the grant.

controls.note: Native by the rule: the credentials that matter stay outside the sandbox and what is inside is session-scoped and short-lived. What remains in the member's authority: connector calls carry the member's full grant (no on-behalf-of exchange; managed authorisation narrows scopes for the listed connectors, Okta only), a session that reaches the member's desktop acts in their Chrome sessions through Claude in Chrome, and files saved to the account, secrets included, are readable by the model.

original.mechanism: Connector tokens held server-side; never present in the sandbox

steps.title: Confirm connector calls are server-side
body: The architecture overview states connector tokens never enter sandboxes and calls are made server-side; no per-session credential is exposed to the model.

controls.mechanism: Manually approve mode and connector tools capped at "Needs approval" ask the owner before each call; "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" (off by default) and "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" at Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions

steps.title: Force approval on named connector tools
body: Set the tools to Needs approval at Organization settings > Connectors or on a custom role's Connectors tab; members confirm each call and lose the Always allow option.

steps.title: Keep persistent approval and the classifier mode off
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off and turn off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" for sensitive groups under Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the owner approves connector calls before they run and an admin can force that for named tools, but scheduled tasks run with an approval mode chosen at creation and nobody present (runs are reviewed afterwards on the Scheduled page), code in the sandbox is not approved per command, "Skip all approvals" has no documented console switch on Team, and the Automatically approve reviewer is a model that never counts. There is no merge-style gate on output.

original.mechanism: "Automatically approve" and "Always allow for connector tools" toggles
original.note: The toggles govern per-tool prompts in attended sessions; Dispatch and scheduled runs have no prompt to answer, and there is no merge-style gate on their output.

steps.title: Keep connector approvals in the loop
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off and consider turning off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" for sensitive groups.

controls.mechanism: Connector tool policy per tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked), organisation-wide and per custom role, enforced on Anthropic's servers for cloud sessions; the network-access level; code execution, web search, built-in browser and Claude in Chrome toggles; the Automatically approve toggle

steps.title: Scope connector tools by role
body: Set each tool's ceiling at Organization settings > Connectors and narrow it per group on the Connectors tab of each custom role under Organization settings > Roles (Enterprise).

steps.title: Switch off built-in tools a session does not need
body: Turn off web search at Organization settings > Capabilities and the built-in browser at Organization settings > Cowork.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: tools are allowed or denied by name with no argument or resource scoping, "Skip all approvals" has no documented console switch on Team, and device managed settings never reach cloud sessions. No repository token exists, so the branch and repository scoping half of the pin does not apply.

original.mechanism: Connector enablement per organisation; curated plugin marketplaces; built-in browser toggle

steps.title: Curate what a cloud session may call
body: Connectors and plugin marketplaces are admitted at Organization settings > Cowork; the built-in browser can be disabled for the organisation.

controls.mechanism: The Compliance API remote session list, with agent-owned scheduled runs (agent_id, started_by_user); Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Inventory for distributed skills and plugins; owner-added connectors

steps.title: Export the session list
body: Query /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote; agent-owned sessions carry agent_id and started_by_user.

steps.title: Review the plugin and skill inventory
body: Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Inventory lists source, version, capabilities, audience and 30-day use for each governed item.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: there is no admin view of members' scheduled tasks and no way to deny one, runs appear only after they happen, and each task is owned by whoever created it; the inventory covers what the organisation distributes, not what members build for themselves.

original.mechanism: Compliance API listing of remote Cowork sessions, including scheduled runs
original.note: A list of sessions, not a registry with owners and approval; scheduled tasks are owned by whoever created them.

steps.title: Export the session list
body: Remote Cowork sessions, including agent-owned scheduled runs, are available through the Compliance API sessions endpoint.

controls.mechanism: Account memory shared with chat, off by default on Team and Enterprise (Organization settings > Capabilities and the Memory role capability); project memory scoped to each project; sessions and files saved to the account; organisation instructions; admin-curated skills and plugins

steps.title: Decide on memory
body: Leave memory off or turn it on at Organization settings > Capabilities (per role with the Memory capability on Enterprise); members can view, edit and delete entries.

steps.title: Lock instruction sources to reviewed skills and plugins
body: At Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Policy turn off "User-created skills" and set Publishing to "Requires review".

steps.title: Set the retention decision
body: Remote transcripts are kept 6 years unless the member deletes the session, and the Compliance API cannot delete them, so decide the deletion process before enabling cloud sessions.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: memory can be kept off and instruction sources partly locked, but memory writes are not validated (members review and edit their own), project instructions and project memory have no admin control, and projects can be shared under the Share projects capability. Sessions cannot be shared. A deleted task leaves history immediately and backend storage within 30 days.

original.mechanism: Account-level session and file retention; deletion by the user or through the Compliance API
original.note: Retention is administered, not scoped; what a later session may read from an earlier one is not a setting.

steps.title: Set the retention decision
body: Remote transcripts are retained for 6 years unless deleted; decide the deletion policy before enabling cloud sessions.

controls.mechanism: "Run Cowork in the cloud" or "Enable for your organization" off at Organization settings > Cowork, the Cowork in the cloud capability removed from a role (up to 15 minutes), an Inference hooks deny for an account (Enterprise, beta); the owner stops, pauses or deletes their own tasks

steps.title: Disable cloud sessions
body: Turn off "Run Cowork in the cloud", or "Enable for your organization" for the whole product, at Organization settings > Cowork.

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise, beta)
body: With Inference hooks enforcing, have your AI security server deny that user's requests; turning enforcement on or off reaches every Anthropic server in about a minute.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: whether switching cloud sessions off stops a running session or a scheduled task is not documented (delay not documented; role changes take up to 15 minutes; network changes reach new sessions only). Only the owner can stop a task or pause and delete a scheduled one. An Inference hooks deny refuses the next request without terminating the session or cancelling queued runs, and setting a group's pooled budget to $0 freezes its usage on usage-based Enterprise. No EDR complement exists, because the sessions run off every endpoint.

original.mechanism: Turning off "Run Cowork in the cloud" or the organisation toggle
original.note: Prevents new cloud sessions; the delay before a running Dispatch or scheduled task stops is not documented.

steps.title: Disable cloud sessions
body: Organization settings > Cowork > "Run Cowork in the cloud" off, or "Enable for your organization" off for the whole product.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API remote session endpoints (product_surface cowork_remote) return prompts, responses, tool calls and tool results; the OTLP export set at Organization settings > Cowork covers cloud sessions with events correlated by prompt.id and session.id

steps.title: Pull cloud-session transcripts (Enterprise)
body: Use a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data on /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote and its messages endpoint.

steps.title: Stream session events to your collector
body: At Organization settings > Cowork enter the OTLP endpoint, protocol and headers; the stream covers cloud sessions as well as local ones.

controls.note: Native by the rule: programmatic export covering this hosted surface. The OTLP push is the copy the session cannot alter; the Compliance API pull is not, because a member's deletion removes a remote session from it. Tool inputs and results are truncated to 10,000 bytes by default, thinking is left out of the OTLP response event, the OTLP prompt-content default is documented both ways, and Team plans get OTLP only (the Compliance API is Enterprise).

original.mechanism: Compliance API capture of cloud sessions; OTLP session events to the organisation's collector

steps.title: Stream session events
body: Configure the OTLP collector under Organization settings > Cowork; metadata by default, content capture opt-in.

controls.mechanism: Spend limits at Organization settings > Usage (organisation, group per-user, seat tier and individual) and pooled monthly group budgets (Enterprise, beta) that pause every member when exhausted; Team usage-credit spend limits

steps.title: Set group spend limits (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Usage open the "By group/tier" tab, choose "Edit limits" on a group and set a Member limit; individual limits override group limits.

steps.title: Cap a team with a pooled budget (Enterprise, beta)
body: In the same "Edit limits" dialog set a Pooled monthly budget; when it runs out usage pauses for every member of the group, and $0 freezes the group.

steps.title: Cap usage credits (Team and seat-based Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Usage set the organisation-wide monthly spend limit and per-user limits on usage credits.

controls.note: Native by the rule: admin-set spend caps stop use when exhausted ("usage can go slightly over a limit before it pauses"). Not offered: a per-session or per-task budget, session duration or concurrency limits, or a cap on scheduled tasks; the pool is shared with chat and Claude Code, seat usage limits are vendor-fixed, and pooled budgets cannot be managed through the Admin API.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's content classifiers scan untrusted content entering context (no administrator setting); Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) hold each governed prompt and returned tool result, connector calls included, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's AI security server

steps.title: Put an inspector on returned tool content (Enterprise, beta)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on "Allow for your organization", register your AI security server, choose Failure handling and turn on "Enforce verdicts".

steps.title: Know what the vendor screening covers
body: Content classifiers scan all untrusted content entering Claude's context and flag potential injections; there is no setting or event export for them.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal screening that is not admin-configurable, and an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server classifies. Hook verdicts are allow or deny only (no strip or quarantine) and system prompts and tool definitions are never sent. Connector content returning through the organisation's AI gateway on the tunnel path can be classified there as well.

controls.mechanism: The Anthropic Trust Center (SOC 2 Type 2 and CSA STAR L2 report, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certificates, 2025 annual penetration testing reports, SIG Lite and CAIQ questionnaires, Cowork security documents) and the Help Center architecture overview of cloud sessions feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table and resources, read 2026-09-25)
Claude Cowork architecture overview (cloud session architecture)
What Certifications has Anthropic obtained?

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the TPRM platform holds the questionnaire, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger. The Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA and CSA STAR for Claude Enterprise and Claude Team; its Cowork document is the desktop security architecture, so request the cloud-sandbox, egress-proxy and tenant-isolation claims explicitly. Reassess on the moving defaults: cloud sessions on by default for Team and the default execution place where allowed, Cowork not covered by zero data retention, a beta surface.

controls.mechanism: Sessions act under the member's own account and connector grants; scheduled runs are agent-owned sessions with an agent_id (cagt_) and started_by_user in the Compliance API

steps.title: Inventory agent-owned runs
body: Query /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote without user_ids[], since that filter excludes agent-owned sessions, and read agent_id and started_by_user.

steps.title: Revoke through the member
body: Remove the Cowork in the cloud capability from the member's custom role at Organization settings > Roles, or remove the member from the mapped IdP group so the next SCIM sync drops it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the session authenticates as the member and carries attribution only; the agent id on scheduled runs is an identifier in the transcript record with no documented separate issuance, authorisation or revocation, so revoking the agent means removing the member's access or deleting the task. Connector actions appear in the connected service as the member.

controls.mechanism: Session-scoped sandbox tokens that expire within hours; connector tokens held server-side and, under managed authorisation, issued and revoked by the IdP; MCP tunnels (Enterprise research preview) with a rotatable, revocable tunnel token and a CA the organisation holds; no store for secrets a task needs

steps.title: Rotate and revoke the tunnel credentials
body: Revoke the Tunnels API key at Organization settings > Tunnels > Tunnels API after setup, rotate the tunnel token by incrementing tunnel.tokenVersion (Helm) or --token-version (Compose), and archive the tunnel to invalidate its token.

steps.title: Issue connector credentials through the IdP
body: Set up Managed authorization on supported connectors at Organization settings > Connectors so the IdP sets token lifetime and deprovisioning revokes access.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a vendor tunnel exists and its credentials are scoped, rotatable and revocable (outbound-only cloudflared plus proxy, inner TLS with a CA generated in your environment, a server certificate valid 90 days and renewed locally, rotation that does not sever established connections), and sandbox tokens are short-lived, but Cowork offers no encrypted, write-only store for secrets a task needs, so anything a member pastes or saves to the account is readable by the model. Tunnels are an Enterprise research preview by request, with Cloudflare as subprocessor.

summary: Anthropic's chat surfaces: claude.ai in the browser, the mobile apps, and Claude Desktop with its Chat, Cowork and Code tabs. Chat runs on the Anthropic API under the user's organisation login; connectors (MCP) reach Google Drive, Microsoft 365, GitHub, Slack and custom remote servers through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com; desktop extensions (.mcpb) and local MCP servers add device-side tools. Prompts, uploads and connector results go to Anthropic; Team and Enterprise data is not used for training and follows the organisation's retention setting (indefinite by default until a custom period is set).

Team and Enterprise administration is in the claude.ai console: SSO (SAML/OIDC via WorkOS) with domain verification and "Require SSO for Claude", JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping, custom roles and groups gating Claude Code, Cowork, Chrome, connectors, Claude Tag and models, connector enablement and per-tool read/write restrictions, enterprise-managed connector authorisation through the IdP, the desktop extension allowlist, audit logs (180-day export) and the Compliance API (Activity Feed, chats, files, projects, session transcripts, effective settings), custom retention, spend limits, IP allowlisting, CMEK and US-only inference. Enterprise installers deploy via Jamf, Kandji, Intune, SCCM or GPO with device policies in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude covering extensions, local MCP, Claude Code and Cowork tabs, auto-updates and forced org login; device policy overrides the in-console allowlist.

facts.value: Anthropic API; Claude Desktop on 3P routes Chat, Cowork and Code to Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, the Anthropic API or an LLM / Claude apps gateway with local conversation storage.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Commercial plans: no training; chat and project retention indefinite by default, configurable from 30 days at Organization settings > Data and privacy; audit logs 180 days; Compliance API local/remote session transcripts 6 years or the custom period.

items.title: Managed deployment and device policies
body: Device policies live in the macOS configuration-profile domain com.anthropic.claudefordesktop and the Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude registry key (machine-level settings take priority over HKCU when both are configured). The keys that matter for control: isDesktopExtensionEnabled and isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled (kill switches for extensions and the directory), isLocalDevMcpEnabled (local MCP server connections), isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled, secureVmFeaturesEnabled (Cowork access), forceLoginOrgUUID, allowedWorkspaceFolders, effortLevel, disableAutoUpdates and autoUpdaterEnforcementHours. Device-level policy overrides the in-app allowlist.

Claude Desktop on 3P extends the same stores with inferenceProvider and credential keys, disabledBuiltinTools, builtinToolPolicy, disableBypassPermissionsMode, coworkEgressAllowedHosts, managedMcpServers, allowedPluginMarketplaces, userPluginMarketplacesEnabled / userPluginUploadsEnabled, sshHostAllowlist, egressProxyUrl and OTLP telemetry keys; a Linux /etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json uses native JSON.

links.title: Claude Desktop configuration reference (3P managed keys)

items.title: Extension allowlist and managed connector authorization
body: Team and Enterprise Owners can turn on the desktop extension allowlist (Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop). It ships disabled — every extension is available until it is enabled — and enabling it force-deletes existing non-allowlisted installs; custom org-scoped extensions upload in .mcpb format. Enterprise-managed connector authorization (GA) lets admins provision MCP connectors org-wide through the IdP (Okta today), assign them by role and scope the permissions Claude may request; Owners can also restrict each connector's tools to read-only and block verified-domain services from connecting to outside accounts.

items.title: Identity, audit and compliance for the organisation
body: SSO via WorkOS (Okta, Entra ID, Google, OneLogin, JumpCloud, Duo SAML) with "Require SSO for Claude", JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping and automatic removal; Enterprise custom roles and groups; IP allowlisting (CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support); tenant restrictions via the proxy-injected anthropic-allowed-org-ids header.

Audit logs (Enterprise, 180 days, emailed download link) from Organization settings > Data and privacy; the Compliance API for the Activity Feed, chats, files, projects, directory, effective settings and Cowork / Claude Code / M365 session transcripts; custom data retention from 30 days; Inference hooks (beta) for inline allow/deny of every governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code.

links.title: Set up JIT or SCIM provisioning

riskNotes.note: Chat and project retention is indefinite until an Owner sets a period; uploads, connector results and artifacts persist with the chat. Custom retention and the Compliance API delete endpoints are the levers.

Custom remote MCP connectors and desktop extensions are user-addable by default; the extension allowlist ships disabled and Anthropic reviews Directory connectors against listing criteria without auditing them.

Connectors act with the user's granted scopes; org-wide tool restrictions (read vs write) and managed authorisation scoping keep Claude from sending mail or writing tickets when only reading is intended.
Personal accounts on the corporate network are blocked only by tenant restrictions or IP allowlisting; domain capture and SSO enforcement pull verified-domain users into the organisation.

controls.mechanism: "Require SSO for Claude" (claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, Authentication) sends every interactive web, desktop and mobile sign-in through the IdP, whose MFA policy applies; "Shortened session length" (Enterprise) forces a fresh sign-in; forceLoginOrgUUID pins Claude Desktop to the organisation; Enterprise domain capture ("Migrate accounts using your domain") leaves no personal account on a verified domain

steps.title: Require SSO so the IdP's MFA governs every login
body: After verifying your domains at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, set up SSO through WorkOS, turn on Require SSO for Claude in the Authentication section, and enforce MFA on the Claude app in your IdP.

steps.title: Bound how long a sign-in lasts (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Organization and access > Session security click Enable next to Shortened session length and choose 1, 7, 14 or 28 days; older sessions expire at once.

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude; login fails for any account outside the listed organisations.

steps.title: Pull personal accounts on your domain into the tenant (Enterprise)
body: With Restrict organization creation, SSO enforcement and JIT or SCIM in place, turn on Migrate accounts using your domain under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security.

controls.note: Partial on the MFA rule applied to every vendor: Claude documents no second-factor requirement of its own, so the factor is whatever the IdP enforces behind Require SSO. Paths that skip a fresh challenge: a signed-in web, desktop or mobile session stays active while the user stays active unless Shortened session length is set (Enterprise only); Compliance Access Keys, which never expire on their own, and Admin API keys; personal accounts on other addresses, which only the tenant-restriction header blocks; and Team plans, which can verify a domain and Restrict organization creation but not claim existing accounts or shorten sessions. Claude Desktop on 3P has no Anthropic identity; sign-in is the inference provider's or the organisation's IdP.

original.mechanism: SSO (SAML/OIDC) with Require SSO for Claude, domain verification and capture, JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping, custom roles and groups (Enterprise)

steps.title: Enforce SSO
body: Verify domains at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, configure the IdP through WorkOS, then toggle "Require SSO for Claude" in Authentication settings.

steps.title: Provision and deprovision from the directory
body: Enable SCIM with group-to-role mapping (Enterprise / Console); users removed from all mapped groups are removed at the next sync.

steps.title: Gate features by role
body: Create custom roles and groups at Organization settings > Roles and Groups to gate Claude Code, Cowork, Chrome, connectors, Claude Tag, models and admin scopes.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom roles and groups (Organization settings > Roles, Groups) grant capabilities, each connector and connector tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked) and admin permissions, with "View effective role"; target-tenant consent for the connector apps is documented: Microsoft Entra admin consent for the two Microsoft 365 connector apps (client IDs 08ad6f98-a4f8-4635-bb8d-f1a3044760f0 and 07c030f6-5743-41b7-ba00-0a6e85f37c17) and Google Workspace API controls trust for Claude

steps.title: Authorise features and connectors by role
body: At Organization settings > Roles create custom roles, choose their groups, toggle capabilities and set each connector or tool on the Connectors tab; check a member with View effective role.

steps.title: Decide in Microsoft Entra whether the connector may be granted
body: A Global Administrator grants admin consent through the adminconsent URLs for both client IDs, requires assignment on the M365 MCP Server for Claude and M365 MCP Client for Claude enterprise apps, and revokes Graph permissions the organisation does not want.

steps.title: Decide in Google Workspace
body: In admin.google.com under Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage third-party app access, set Claude to Trusted, or leave it blocked.

controls.note: Native on Enterprise by the rule: the console administers role and group authorisation over connectors, tools and features, enforced on Anthropic's servers and failing toward deny, and the vendor documents the target-tenant consent path with the app IDs. Team plans have organisation-wide connector and tool policy only, which is partial. Connector permissions apply only to members on the Custom role (User, Admin and Owner see every organisation connector under the organisation-wide policy), grants are additive across roles, and role changes take up to 15 minutes. The consent itself is the target tenant's control, not Anthropic's.

original.mechanism: SSO (SAML/OIDC) with Require SSO for Claude, domain verification and capture, JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping, custom roles and groups (Enterprise)

steps.title: Enforce SSO
body: Verify domains at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, configure the IdP through WorkOS, then toggle "Require SSO for Claude" in Authentication settings.

steps.title: Provision and deprovision from the directory
body: Enable SCIM with group-to-role mapping (Enterprise / Console); users removed from all mapped groups are removed at the next sync.

steps.title: Gate features by role
body: Create custom roles and groups at Organization settings > Roles and Groups to gate Claude Code, Cowork, Chrome, connectors, Claude Tag, models and admin scopes.

original.mechanism: Connectors retrieve as the authenticated user (OAuth) or as the scoped managed authorisation; verified-domain restriction stops org services connecting to outside accounts

steps.title: Keep retrieval per user
body: Prefer user OAuth or role-scoped managed authorisation over shared service accounts and turn on the verified-domain connector restriction on Enterprise.

original.note: Delegated when the connector runs as the user (the source system enforces the user's permissions, oversharing included); service-owned when enterprise-managed authorisation is used, in which case the managed scope, not the user's entitlements, bounds retrieval for everyone.

controls.mechanism: anthropic-allowed-org-ids tenant-restriction header (Enterprise and Console) injected by the organisation's TLS-inspecting proxy and enforced by Anthropic for claude.ai web, desktop, API-key and OAuth traffic; IP allowlisting (Enterprise, CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support); the code execution sandbox's own egress set at Organization settings > Capabilities

steps.title: Block other tenants at the proxy
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your organisation UUIDs (numbered continuation headers, up to 500 UUIDs) for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com, overwriting the header on every request.

steps.title: Restrict where your tenant can be used from (Enterprise)
body: Send Anthropic support your office and VPN CIDR ranges; every authenticated request from another address is then denied.

steps.title: Set the sandbox's own egress
body: At Organization settings > Capabilities under Code execution and file creation, leave Allow network egress off or limit it to package managers and named domains.

controls.note: Partial on the D3-OTF rule: Anthropic honours a documented tenant-restriction header that the organisation's SSE injects (TLS inspection required; other organisations get a 403 tenant_restriction_violation), so personal and foreign tenants are blocked on managed networks. A customer proxy does not control the vendor's own egress: remote connectors reach MCP servers from Anthropic's cloud, web search runs on Anthropic's servers, and the code execution sandbox is governed only by the Capabilities network setting (off for new Enterprise organisations, package managers only on Team; connector traffic stays possible whatever it says). Off-network and unmanaged devices bypass the header; IP allowlisting gates only the organisation's own tenant. Local MCP servers in Claude Desktop use the device's network.

original.mechanism: IP allowlisting (Enterprise, CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support) and tenant restrictions (anthropic-allowed-org-ids header injected by a TLS-inspecting proxy)

steps.title: Restrict where Claude can be used from
body: Compile CIDR ranges and have Anthropic enable IP allowlisting; every authenticated request outside the ranges is denied (Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions then need an exemption).

steps.title: Block other tenants at the proxy
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your org UUIDs for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com (up to 500 UUIDs across numbered headers).

original.note: IP allowlisting is enforced by Anthropic; the tenant-restriction header is enforced by a TLS-inspecting proxy the organisation operates. Neither is an SSE service: inline inspection of prompts and uploads is the customer's SSE, and its completeness depends on which paths it sees.

original.mechanism: Documented host allowlist for Claude Desktop and claude.ai; egressProxyUrl / PAC keys on 3P; connector traffic through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com; custom connectors reachable only via allowlisted Anthropic IPs

steps.title: Allowlist the documented hosts
body: Permit anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com, platform.claude.com, downloads.claude.ai, *.claudeusercontent.com and *.claudemcpcontent.com (plus optional CDN hosts for artifacts) and route through egressProxyUrl on managed devices.

original.note: The product documents its destinations and offers proxy keys; it enforces no destination policy of its own. Connector traffic egresses from Anthropic's MCP proxy, outside the organisation's network.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) hold every governed claude.ai request on web, desktop and mobile, with its tool calls, tool results and extracted attachment text, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's DLP or AI security server; the Compliance API supports detection after the fact

steps.title: Put your DLP inline (Enterprise, beta)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on Allow for your organization, register the endpoint and signing secret, set Failure handling to Block the request, Requests inspected to 100 and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Scan stored content after the fact
body: Give your DLP or DSPM product a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data to page through /v1/compliance/apps/chats, messages and files, and delete:compliance_user_data only on a separate key.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: an inline hook that hands prompts to the organisation's DLP with a block verdict is an attach point, and Claude classifies nothing itself. The hook allows or denies only (no masking or redaction), never receives image bytes (a screenshot of a document is not inspected), has no response-side event yet, skips voice mode, members of excluded custom roles and requests outside the rollout percentage, and falls back to the failure-handling choice when the server errs or the circuit breaker trips. A blocked message stays in the conversation. It is not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud, nor on Team plans. Blocking connector write tools and custom retention are minimisation and lifecycle, not detection; Compliance API scanning finds content after it reached Anthropic.

original.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) route every governed prompt to your AI security server for allow/deny; connector tool restrictions limit outbound actions; no built-in content classifier

steps.title: Enable Inference hooks
body: Configure the AI security server endpoint and signing secret, run shadow mode, then enforce; denied requests never reach the model and are recorded in the Activity Feed. Not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud.

original.note: Inference hooks route governed prompts to the organisation's scanner; the product itself classifies nothing, and uploads, connector results and outputs are outside the hook unless the hook contract says otherwise.

original.mechanism: claude.ai is a browser SaaS; paste and upload inspection is the organisation's browser-security tooling
original.note: Anthropic offers no in-page inspection; pair the tenant-restriction header with browser D&R or SSE inline controls.

steps.title: Instrument the browser session
body: Apply your browser-security policy to claude.ai and *.claudeusercontent.com and use the tenant-restriction header to keep sessions in the corporate tenant.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's model-layer defenses against injected instructions (no administrator setting); Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) hand each governed request, including connector tool calls and the results they return, to the organisation's AI security server before the next inference step

steps.title: Put a screen on returned connector content (Enterprise, beta)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks register an AI security server that classifies tool results for injection, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Know what the vendor screening covers
body: The connector verification page tells members to stay aware of prompt injection "even though Claude has built-in protections"; Verified and Community labels are not a security audit of what a connector returns.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal defenses documented only in general terms (no setting, threshold, quarantine or event an administrator can see), plus an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server does the classifying. The hook returns allow or deny (no strip or quarantine), never receives system prompts or tool definitions, so a poisoned connector description is not seen, and ignores images. Claude.ai has no action classifier to lean on; restricting write tools limits what an injection can do, which is AML.M0028, not screening.

original.mechanism: Anthropic model-side safeguards and web-fetch isolation; connector tool restrictions; Inference hooks for inline policy

steps.title: Limit what an injected instruction can do
body: Restrict connectors to read-only tools and enable only vetted connectors; use Inference hooks to deny prompts carrying policy-violating content.

original.note: No admin-configurable injection classifier is exposed for chat.

controls.mechanism: The Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table, SOC 2 Type 2 and CSA STAR L2 report, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certificates, HIPAA reports, SIG Lite, CAIQ, VSA and HECVAT questionnaires, infrastructure diagram, security advisories) and the Compliance API effective-settings endpoint feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table and resources, read 2026-09-25)
Compliance API — organizations, users, roles, groups and effective settings

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the questionnaire, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform. The Trust Center scope table lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, HIPAA and NIST 800-171 for Claude Enterprise, and all but HIPAA for Claude Team; the reports and questionnaires sit behind Request access, and it publishes CVE-2026-22561 for the Claude for Windows installer. Re-assess the tenant on a clock by reading each organisation's effective settings through the Compliance API (Enterprise); a readback is evidence for the assessment, not the assessment.

original.mechanism: Trust Center artifacts (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA implementation guide, architecture overviews) feed the buyer's TPRM platform

steps.title: Collect artifacts
body: Request the Trust Center resources referenced across the docs, including the Cowork desktop security architecture overview and the M365 architecture diagrams.

original.mechanism: Compliance API directory and settings endpoints, Enterprise Analytics API and usage exports feed the organisation's governance platform

steps.title: Mirror organisation state
body: Pull organizations, users, roles, groups and effective settings from the Compliance API and per-user engagement from the Enterprise Analytics API.

original.mechanism: Compliance API effective-settings and Activity Feed endpoints, audit log export, and admin console readback let posture tooling verify training opt-out, retention, connectors and roles

steps.title: Evidence configuration continuously
body: Poll each organisation's effective settings and the Activity Feed with a Compliance Access Key; use the audit log export (180 days) for point-in-time evidence.

original.note: The Compliance API effective-settings and Activity Feed endpoints are the readback an SSPM product polls; nothing in the product compares settings to a baseline, detects drift or remediates. The same rule applies to every vendor with a readback API.

controls.mechanism: Connector tool policy per connector and tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked) at Organization settings > Connectors and, on Enterprise, on each custom role's Connectors tab; a Needs approval ceiling makes Claude ask before each call and removes the member's "Always allow"; device keys remove local MCP servers and desktop extensions

steps.title: Cap write tools at Needs approval
body: Set send, create, update and delete tools to Needs approval (or Blocked) in the organisation-wide tool policy at Organization settings > Connectors and on each role's Connectors tab; members then confirm every call and cannot choose Always allow.

steps.title: Remove the tools the policy does not reach
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false, or isDesktopExtensionEnabled false, in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude where local tools are not wanted.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a present person approves each call of an organisation connector's tool and an administrator can force that per tool, non-overridably and enforced on Anthropic's servers for web, desktop and mobile, but the docs do not say the prompt shows the tool's arguments, so approval bound to the exact action is not documented. Outside the policy: local MCP servers and desktop extensions, whose prompts the user can set to always allow unless the device keys remove them; code execution with network egress, which acts without per-action approval; and roles or organisations left at Always allow, where members keep persistent approval. Team plans set the policy organisation-wide only.

original.mechanism: Connector tool calls prompt per tool unless the user chooses always allow; Owners can set connector tools to ask or blocked org-wide; no approval workflow for chat outputs

steps.title: Force approval on connector actions
body: At Organization settings > Connectors set tools that write (send message, create issue) to ask or remove them; these settings are enforced in Claude Code and Cowork sessions too.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise-managed authorisation (Organization settings > Connectors > connector > Configuration > Managed authorization) issues connector grants from the IdP by role and removes them on IdP deprovisioning; the Activity Feed records integration_user_connected, integration_user_disconnected and mcp_server_managed_auth_token_exchanged per member; member removal ends access immediately

steps.title: Issue connector grants from the IdP
body: On a supported connector click Set up next to Managed authorization, confirm the Okta connection, choose the roles and the scopes Claude may request, then Save & turn on.

steps.title: Inventory grants from the Activity Feed (Enterprise)
body: Query /v1/compliance/activities with activity_types[] integration_user_connected and integration_user_disconnected to keep a per-member register of connector grants.

steps.title: End grants with the person
body: Use SCIM directory sync so members removed from the IdP app are removed from the organisation, which ends their access immediately.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: no console page or API lists each member's live connector grants with a revoke action, so the register is the organisation's, rebuilt from Activity Feed events; per-grant revocation is the member's (Customize > Connectors) or the source's (Entra, Google), and Owners can only remove a connector for everyone. Managed authorisation binds grants to the IdP lifecycle, with token lifetime set by the connector's authorisation server, but covers ten listed connectors and Okta only; individually authorised grants live as long as the source allows (Microsoft 365 refresh tokens lapse after 90 days of inactivity by default). Chat has no agent identity of its own: connector actions carry the member's.

original.mechanism: Compliance Access Keys and Admin API keys with scopes; connector service identities via enterprise-managed authorisation; no per-agent identity for chat

steps.title: Scope machine credentials
body: Create a Compliance Access Key with only the scopes needed (read:compliance_activities, read:compliance_user_data) rather than an Owner's session.

original.note: The scoped API keys identify automation reading the organisation, not an agent acting for users; connector service identities are the vendor's; chat actions carry the user's identity.

controls.mechanism: The Compliance API enumerates every chat, file, project and project attachment, and chat messages name the integration and MCP server behind each tool call; Organization settings > Connectors lists the organisation's connectors; the Activity Feed records which member connected which integration

steps.title: Enumerate what Claude holds (Enterprise)
body: Page /v1/compliance/apps/chats with order_by=updated_at, then each chat's messages, files and artifacts, and the projects and project attachments, with a read:compliance_user_data key.

steps.title: List the sources behind the connectors
body: Export the connectors at Organization settings > Connectors and the integration_user_connected events, then run your data-classification tooling over those sources before enabling them.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the product lists what it stores and which sources are connected, without classification or an oversharing report on the drives, mailboxes, sites and channels behind the connectors (the Microsoft 365 connector retrieves on demand and caches no file content, so there is no index to inspect). Custom retention and deletion are lifecycle controls, not inventory. Knowing what the connectors reach is a DSPM or data-classification product, which can consume the Compliance API.

original.mechanism: Custom data retention (30 days to indefinite) for chats and projects, Compliance API retrieve and delete for chats, files and projects, organisation data export

steps.title: Set retention and delete on demand
body: Configure retention at Organization settings > Data and privacy (Owner) and use the Compliance API content endpoints to retrieve or delete chats, files and projects.

original.note: Retention, deletion and export are data lifecycle controls. They do not discover or classify sensitive content in chats, files or projects, nor assess exposure; a DSPM product consumes the Compliance API content endpoints to do that.

controls.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens encrypted in Anthropic's backend and never shown to the model, their lifetime set by the source or, under managed authorisation, the IdP; MCP tunnels (Enterprise research preview) with a tunnel token rotated by re-running setup and revoked by archiving; Compliance Access Keys scoped at creation and deleted at Organization settings > API

steps.title: Rotate and revoke the tunnel credentials
body: Revoke the Tunnels API key at Organization settings > Tunnels > Tunnels API after every setup run, rotate the tunnel token by incrementing tunnel.tokenVersion (Helm) or --token-version (Compose) and re-running setup, and archive a tunnel to invalidate it.

steps.title: Scope and rotate compliance keys
body: Create separate read and delete Compliance Access Keys at Organization settings > API and rotate them yourself; they never expire and a deleted key fails on the next request.

steps.title: Issue connector credentials through the IdP
body: Set up Managed authorization on supported connectors so the IdP and the connector's authorisation server set token lifetime and deprovisioning revokes access.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a vendor tunnel exists and its credentials are scoped and revocable, but rotating the tunnel token means re-running setup and restarting cloudflared (a redeploy of the tunnel stack), the token and TLS private keys are stored in your environment (Helm release Secrets are not encrypted at rest by default), and the preview carries no uptime or support commitment. Compliance Access Keys do not expire, and individually authorised connector tokens live as long as the source allows. Custody of the desktop app's own sign-in token is not documented for standard deployments.

original.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens held by the platform; enterprise-managed authorisation replaces per-user grants; API and compliance keys are scoped and revocable in the console

steps.title: Centralise connector credentials
body: Use enterprise-managed authorisation so connector access is inherited from IdP roles on first login instead of users pasting tokens.

original.note: Connector tokens are held by the platform and never shown to the model; the API and compliance keys are long-lived until rotated in the console. Enterprise-managed authorisation replaces per-user grants — it does not make the underlying credential ephemeral.

controls.mechanism: Only Owners add connectors (Organization settings > Connectors) and members can connect only those; per-tool Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked as an organisation-wide ceiling and, on Enterprise, per custom role, enforced on Anthropic's servers; isLocalDevMcpEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled and the desktop extension allowlist on the device

steps.title: Set the organisation-wide tool policy
body: At Organization settings > Connectors open each connector's tool permissions and set every tool or category to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked; members cannot widen it.

steps.title: Narrow it per group (Enterprise)
body: On each custom role's Connectors tab under Organization settings > Roles set All connectors, each connector or each tool; new roles default to Needs approval, and the stricter of role and organisation policy applies.

steps.title: Lock down device-side tools
body: Turn on the allowlist at Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop and set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false in device policy where local MCP servers are not wanted.

controls.note: Native on Enterprise by the rule: an administrator allowlist of connectors plus per-tool (read versus write) scoping per group, locked against members and enforced outside the model; when permissions cannot load, access fails toward deny. Boundaries: no argument or resource scoping (which folder, which channel) beyond the source system's own permissions; Team plans scope organisation-wide only; members on built-in roles get every organisation connector under the organisation-wide policy; local MCP servers and desktop extensions are outside the tool policy (device keys and the extension allowlist only, and the allowlist does not guard against tampering with installed files).

original.mechanism: Connector enablement per organisation, per-tool read/write restrictions, role-based connector access, desktop extension allowlist, isLocalDevMcpEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled

steps.title: Enable and scope connectors
body: Enable connectors at Organization settings > Connectors > Browse connectors and restrict each connector's tools (for example search but not send) for the whole organisation.

steps.title: Lock down device-side tools
body: Turn on the desktop extension allowlist and set isLocalDevMcpEnabled or isDesktopExtensionEnabled false in device policy where local tools are not wanted.

original.note: Connector enablement and per-tool read/write restrictions hide or limit connector tools org-wide; there is no argument-level scoping (which folder, which channel) beyond what the connector's own authorisation grants.

controls.mechanism: Connectors retrieve with each member's own permissions at the source (per-user OAuth, or the IdP's assertion under managed authorisation); administrators choose which connectors and tools exist, narrow Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra, and stop verified-domain services connecting to outside Claude accounts; no site, drive or mailbox scoping in Claude

steps.title: Keep retrieval on the member's own entitlements
body: Add only the connectors you govern at Organization settings > Connectors; each member then authenticates individually and reaches only what their source account can.

steps.title: Narrow what the Microsoft 365 connector may read
body: In Entra under Enterprise applications > M365 MCP Server for Claude > Permissions revoke Graph permissions such as Sites.Read.All or Mail.Read that the organisation does not want reached.

steps.title: Keep work data out of personal Claude accounts (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Organization and access > Connector domain restriction turn on Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: retrieval runs with the requesting member's entitlements, so the source enforces them (oversharing included, and Microsoft 365 DLP applies to delegated calls), but administrators can only include or exclude whole connectors, tools or Graph permission scopes, not choose which sites, drives or mailboxes the assistant may search; the Ask Your Org enterprise search project uses the same per-member connectors. Under managed authorisation the Owner-chosen scopes bound every member of the roles selected. Oversharing remediation is the source's.

original.mechanism: Connectors retrieve as the authenticated user (OAuth) or as the scoped managed authorisation; verified-domain restriction stops org services connecting to outside accounts

steps.title: Keep retrieval per user
body: Prefer user OAuth or role-scoped managed authorisation over shared service accounts and turn on the verified-domain connector restriction on Enterprise.

original.note: Delegated when the connector runs as the user (the source system enforces the user's permissions, oversharing included); service-owned when enterprise-managed authorisation is used, in which case the managed scope, not the user's entitlements, bounds retrieval for everyone.

controls.mechanism: Organization settings > Connectors lists every organisation connector (only Owners add them, members connect only those); the desktop extension allowlist at Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop; Organization settings > Plugins & skills Inventory and Requests tabs list governed plugins and skills and the approval queue for member submissions

steps.title: Treat the connector list as the enforced register
body: Keep custom connectors Owner-added at Organization settings > Connectors and remove any that have no owner in your inventory.

steps.title: Turn on the desktop extension allowlist
body: Toggle Allowlist on under Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop; unlisted extensions are force-deleted and new installs come only from the sanctioned registry.

steps.title: Approve plugins and skills before they spread
body: Review the Inventory and approve or deny member submissions on the Requests tab of Organization settings > Plugins & skills.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the connector list and extension allowlist are enforced registers, but they carry no owner or approval record per connector, the allowlist ships off, local MCP servers configured in claude_desktop_config.json appear nowhere unless isLocalDevMcpEnabled removes them, and members with the Create skills capability add their own skills. Reconciliation against actual use is the organisation's inventory.

original.mechanism: Organisation connector catalogue, extension allowlist and role assignments in the console; Compliance API session listings for Cowork and Claude Code

steps.title: Treat the connector catalogue as the registry
body: Only Owner-enabled connectors and allowlisted extensions are available to members; review them under Organization settings > Connectors.

original.note: The connector catalogue and extension allowlist are approved configuration; session listings are use. There is no owner or approval record per connector and no reconciliation — the organisation's inventory holds those.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise domain claiming lists every personal Free, Pro and Max account on a verified domain (email, plan, created, last active; CSV export) and "Migrate accounts using your domain" moves or closes them; Restrict organization creation, the anthropic-allowed-org-ids header and forceLoginOrgUUID prevent new personal use

steps.title: Review personal accounts on your domain (Enterprise)
body: After domain verification, SSO enforcement and JIT or SCIM, review and export the personal accounts on the domain, then turn on Migrate accounts using your domain under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security.

steps.title: Stop new personal organisations on the domain
body: Turn on Restrict organization creation under Security on the Organization and access page once the domain shows Verified.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the vendor lists personal accounts on the verified domains, not what they do, accounts on personal addresses, Claude on unmanaged devices, or connectors members attach, which remain for SSE/CASB and endpoint inventory. Domain capture is one-way and has a fixed 30-day window; Team plans can verify a domain and block new personal accounts but not list or claim existing ones. The header and forceLoginOrgUUID prevent rather than discover.

original.mechanism: Domain capture pulls verified-domain accounts into the organisation; tenant restrictions and IP allowlisting block personal accounts on corporate networks

steps.title: Capture and block
body: Verify domains for account claiming and deploy the tenant-restriction header so personal claude.ai use from managed networks is refused.

original.note: Domain capture is a genuine discovery signal: it finds personal accounts on verified domains and pulls them into the organisation. Its scope is accounts on your domains — personal accounts on other addresses and unmanaged devices are found by proxy or endpoint inventory.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API (Enterprise): /v1/compliance/apps/chats and each chat's messages return prompts, responses and tool_use blocks (tool name, JSON input, integration name, mcp_server_url) with tool_result text, files and artifacts; /v1/compliance/activities returns control-plane and connector events such as integration_user_connected, mcp_tool_policy_updated and inference_hooks_request_denied; a 180-day audit-log CSV export

steps.title: Create a Compliance Access Key (Enterprise)
body: The primary owner enables the Compliance API at Organization settings > API and creates a key with read:compliance_activities and read:compliance_user_data only.

steps.title: Pull conversations with their tool calls
body: Walk /v1/compliance/apps/chats with order_by=updated_at and fetch each chat's messages with tool_result_max_chars and tool_use_input_max_chars set to -1 so inputs and results are not cut at 10,000 characters.

steps.title: Stream the Activity Feed to the SIEM
body: Poll /v1/compliance/activities from the last saved cursor and correlate its events with your gateway's records.

controls.note: Native by the rule: an administrator exports conversation content with each connector call's tool, arguments, server and result, plus connector and policy events, programmatically. Boundaries: Enterprise only (Team has neither the API nor audit logs); pull-based, so a chat a member deletes before the next poll comes back with deleted_at and no content, and retention deletions are final; non-text tool results are omitted; transcripts of Cowork and Claude Code sessions are separate endpoints; integrity and retention beyond Anthropic's are the SIEM's. Inference hooks can push each governed transcript in real time as an archival alternative.

original.mechanism: Enterprise audit logs (30+ event types, 180-day export) and the Compliance API Activity Feed with actor, IP, user agent and device; session transcripts for Cowork, Claude Code, M365 and Science

steps.title: Export or stream audit events
body: Owners export logs from Organization settings > Data and privacy, or query GET /v1/compliance/activities continuously into the SIEM.

original.note: Vendor-held audit log with a 180-day export window and the Activity Feed; durable retention and tamper evidence beyond that window are the organisation's archive. Events are attributed, not signed.

controls.mechanism: Member removal (Organization settings > Members > Remove from team, or SCIM) ends access immediately; an Owner removes a connector for everyone at Organization settings > Connectors or sets its tools to Blocked; the Chat capability off on custom roles (up to 15 minutes); an Inference hooks deny for an account (Enterprise, beta); isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled false on devices

steps.title: Cut a member off
body: Select Remove from team at Organization settings > Members, or remove the person from the IdP app with SCIM; they lose access to the organisation immediately.

steps.title: Remove a connector for everyone
body: At Organization settings > Connectors click Remove (or the three dots) on the connector, or set all of its tools to Blocked, then revoke the app's grant at the source (Entra, Google, your IdP).

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise, beta)
body: With Enforce verdicts on, have your AI security server deny that member's requests; turning enforcement on or off reaches every Anthropic server in about a minute.

steps.title: Remove device-side tools
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled false in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: there is no organisation-wide switch for claude.ai chat (the Chat capability can be turned off only on custom roles, and built-in roles keep it); removing a connector disables it for every member, but revocation of the grants at the source is not documented, so revoke them there; and the effect of either on a research run or tool loop already in progress is not documented (delay not documented; role changes up to 15 minutes). Member removal is documented as immediate. An Inference hooks deny refuses the next inference request, which halts a running tool loop at its next step, but only on Enterprise and only while the hook is enforcing.

original.mechanism: SCIM deprovisioning, member removal, connector disable (revokes for all), extension allowlist force-delete, device keys (isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled, secureVmFeaturesEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled), Compliance API delete

steps.title: Cut access and remove data
body: Remove the member or SCIM group, disable the connector at Organization settings > Connectors, and delete chats, files or projects through the Compliance API.

original.note: Seat removal and connector disable apply at the next request; a connector call in flight completes. The docs state no propagation delay, so measure it.

summary: Office add-ins served from pivot.claude.ai inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook that read and write the open file or mail thread, with connectors, skills and an optional cross-app mode. Users sign in with their Claude account (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) and requests go to Anthropic, or the add-in is pointed at the organisation's Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or gateway endpoint. Chat history, uploaded skills, connector registrations and the sign-in credential live in the Office webview's browser storage on each device; Anthropic deletes inputs and outputs from its backend within 30 days.

Admins deploy and gate the add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and toggle "Let Claude work across apps" at Organization settings > Office agents. Governance gaps are explicit in the docs: the add-ins do not inherit custom data retention and activity is not in Enterprise audit logs or data exports. Enterprise organisations with the Compliance API get add-in session transcripts (office_agents/* local sessions), which the add-in pages label public beta and the Compliance API reference calls stable. A custom OpenTelemetry collector receives the full unfiltered audit trail (prompts, tool inputs and outputs, document references) from each user's browser and must support CORS.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Backend inputs and outputs deleted within 30 days per the add-in pages, but Enterprise organisations with the Compliance API have add-in session transcripts held 6 years by default (Compliance API reference); local history keeps the 50 most recent conversations per user, organisation and app with no admin retention window; commercial terms, no training.

riskNotes.note: A gateway token or API key configured centrally is distributed unencrypted to every user's browser profile and included in data exports; shared OS accounts share uploaded skills and connector registrations.

The add-in sends the open document, workbook or thread content the user asks about; Outlook requires Graph consent, and cross-app mode links context across Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook sessions.
History is keyed to a Claude account or a hashed Entra object ID; Office builds without nested app authentication fall back to a per-installation identifier shared by everyone on the device.
Add-ins can be installed from AppSource by users unless the M365 Admin Center restricts them; activity is absent from Enterprise audit logs and exports.

controls.mechanism: Require SSO for Claude (claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, Authentication) governs the add-in's claude.ai sign-in and Migrate accounts using your domain sends new domain accounts through SSO; the Outlook Graph token and the Entra-based third-party paths sign in with Microsoft Entra ID through nested app authentication, governed by Conditional Access on the Claude for Office enterprise app or on your own app registration (graph_client_id)

steps.title: Require SSO so the IdP's MFA governs the add-in sign-in
body: After verifying your domain, turn on Require SSO for Claude in the Authentication section at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization and enforce MFA on the Claude application in your IdP; the add-in's Log in button completes that claude.ai sign-in in a browser window.

steps.title: Consolidate accounts on your domain
body: On Enterprise, turn on Migrate accounts using your domain under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security, so new accounts on the domain go straight through SSO into the workspace instead of becoming personal accounts.

steps.title: Put Conditional Access on the Entra sign-in
body: Target an MFA Conditional Access policy at the Claude for Office enterprise application (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266), or at your own single-tenant app set with graph_client_id, which governs the Outlook Graph token and Entra sign-in on Bedrock direct, keyless Foundry and gateway_auth_source=entra deployments.

controls.note: Partial on the MFA rule applied to every vendor: Anthropic has no organisation "require 2FA" switch of its own, so the second factor is whatever the IdP enforces — behind Require SSO on the Claude-account path, and Entra Conditional Access for the Graph token and the Entra-based third-party paths. Paths with no interactive factor: a static gateway token or Foundry API key delivered in the manifest, Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap response authenticates inference with no login, and Vertex AI direct relies on the user's Google account. The Claude-account access and refresh tokens sit in the webview's localStorage; no session lifetime is documented, so a sign-in lasts until the user signs out or the profile's storage is cleared. Personal Pro and Max accounts can sign in to the same AppSource add-in: domain capture covers only verified domains, and the tenant-restriction header at the proxy is the network-side backstop.

original.mechanism: Claude account sign-in (SSO/SCIM at the organisation) plus Microsoft 365 Admin Center add-in assignment; Entra ID identity in third-party mode

steps.title: Assign the add-ins to users
body: Manage member access to the Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and grant the one-time Microsoft Graph consent for Outlook.

steps.title: Enforce the Claude organisation
body: Require SSO for Claude and use domain capture so the add-in sign-in lands in the managed organisation.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 admin center Settings > Integrated apps assigns the add-ins to everyone, users or groups, with self-install closed by Let users access the Office Store (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the My Marketplace Apps / My Custom Apps / My ReadWriteMailbox Apps user roles (Outlook); a documented tenant-wide Microsoft Graph admin consent to Anthropic's Claude for Office Entra app (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266) or your own single-tenant app via graph_client_id; per-user disabled_features / access_policies through Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap endpoint in custom-manifest deployments; claude.ai Organization settings > Office agents is org-wide only

steps.title: Assign the add-ins to groups
body: In the Microsoft 365 admin center go to Settings > Integrated apps > Add-ins > Deploy Add-in, choose the Claude listing or upload the manifest, and assign Specific users/groups; group membership then grants and removes access.

steps.title: Close the self-install paths
body: Clear Let users access the Office Store at Settings > Org settings > Services > User owned apps and services, and for Outlook remove My Marketplace Apps, My Custom Apps and My ReadWriteMailbox Apps from the default role assignment policy in the Exchange admin center.

steps.title: Decide the Graph consent
body: Have a Global Administrator open the documented admin-consent link for Claude for Office (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, User.Read, offline_access), or register a single-tenant app with those delegated permissions and set graph_client_id on the manifest URL instead.

steps.title: Set per-user feature policy
body: In custom-manifest deployments deliver disabled_features (comma-separated) through Entra ID extension attributes, or access_policies statements through the manifest or a bootstrap endpoint, so features vary by user.

controls.note: Native by the rule, with the add-in's authorization plane split across two consoles. The Microsoft side decides who may run the add-in (group assignment; unassigned users are blocked only once the Office Store setting and the Exchange add-in user roles, both on by default, are closed) and whether the Graph grant exists at all: Anthropic documents the consent URL, the app ID, the verified publisher (Anthropic, PBC), the redirect URIs and the delegated scopes, plus a single-tenant alternative whose approval and Conditional Access the organisation owns (the setup plugin's manifest command also lists People.Read for that app; the Outlook page lists four scopes). That consent is the Microsoft 365 tenant's own control. The claude.ai side is coarse: Organization settings > Office agents switches cross-app mode for everyone, Enterprise custom roles do not list the add-ins, and model access follows the member's role. Per-user feature policy exists only where configuration keys are delivered, which the docs describe for third-party-platform deployments.

original.mechanism: Claude account sign-in (SSO/SCIM at the organisation) plus Microsoft 365 Admin Center add-in assignment; Entra ID identity in third-party mode

steps.title: Assign the add-ins to users

steps.title: Enforce the Claude organisation
