original.mechanism: The add-in reads only the currently open file or the open email; Outlook access is bounded by the Graph consent granted by the admin

steps.title: Scope Graph consent
body: Grant only the Microsoft Graph permissions the Outlook add-in documents during the one-time admin consent.

original.note: Delegated: the open document is what the user already has; Outlook retrieval carries the Graph consent the admin granted, so that consent, not the user's mailbox permissions, is the ceiling.

controls.mechanism: The anthropic-allowed-org-ids tenant-restriction header, injected by the organisation's proxy on claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com (Enterprise), covers the add-in's Claude-account sign-in and inference; the per-path domain allowlist; disabled_features web_search removes Anthropic-served web search and fetch in custom-manifest deployments

steps.title: Inject the tenant-restriction header
body: Have your proxy add anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your organisation UUIDs on claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com; a request for any other organisation fails with 403 tenant_restriction_violation.

steps.title: Allow only the documented destinations
body: Permit pivot.claude.ai, claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, appsforoffice.microsoft.com and, when used, login.microsoftonline.com, graph.microsoft.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com and bridge.claudeusercontent.com (Claude account), or your gateway and cloud endpoints (third-party platform).

steps.title: Keep web search inside your network
body: In custom-manifest deployments set disabled_features=web_search and attach an in-network search tool with mcp_servers, so search queries stop going to Anthropic's search provider.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: Anthropic enforces the tenant block server-side and the organisation's SSE injects the header. The header article lists web, desktop, API-key and OAuth-token access but does not name the Office add-ins, so confirm with a personal-organisation sign-in through the proxy. A customer proxy does not control egress Anthropic performs for the add-in: built-in web search and web fetch (Anthropic's search provider), code-execution containers and MCP connector calls through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com leave from Anthropic's cloud. On third-party platforms inference goes only to the organisation's gateway or cloud endpoint, so the header is moot there and the gateway is the egress point.

original.mechanism: pivot.claude.ai and the model endpoint are ordinary HTTPS from the Office webview; tenant-restriction header and IP allowlisting apply to claude.ai traffic

steps.title: Keep add-in traffic in the corporate tenant
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids at the proxy for claude.ai and api.anthropic.com so the add-in cannot sign in to a personal organisation.

original.note: The add-in itself offers nothing; the vendor-side tenant restriction is credited on the Claude chat entity, and the proxy that enforces the header is the organisation's SSE. Confirm the Office webview honours the proxy before relying on it.

original.mechanism: Only pivot.claude.ai, the model endpoint, the identity provider and the configured OTel collector are contacted; third-party mode keeps content inside your endpoint

steps.title: Allowlist the documented destinations
body: Permit pivot.claude.ai plus your model endpoint and collector; in third-party mode conversation content goes only to your Vertex, Bedrock, Azure or gateway endpoint.

original.note: The add-in documents a small fixed destination set; it enforces no policy of its own, and the Office webview's traffic must be bounded by the proxy or SSE.

controls.mechanism: access_policies statements that deny addin.access on an open document, or file.upload of an attached file, by Microsoft Purview sensitivity label GUID (mip_label_guid), label name or file path, with an allow-list mode and fail-closed handling of unreadable labels (manifest or bootstrap); Microsoft's Allow programmatic access = false label option keeps Outlook add-ins off encrypted mail; no content detection, and Inference hooks do not cover the add-ins

steps.title: Block the add-in on labelled content
body: Add access_policies deny statements for addin.access with an open_file resource matching your restricted sublabel GUIDs, and for file.upload with an uploaded_file resource on the same labels, and deliver the array in the manifest or bootstrap response.

steps.title: Keep Outlook add-ins off encrypted mail
body: For sensitivity labels that encrypt mail, set the Allow programmatic access custom policy option to false; Outlook add-ins do not activate on those items.

steps.title: Scan transcripts after the fact
body: Pull office_agents/* local session transcripts from the Compliance API into your DLP scanner; this detects after the prompt was sent and cannot block it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: label-based restriction without content detection. access_policies reads the label, not the content — an unlabelled document carrying card numbers passes unless labels are allow-listed (the first allow flips that scope to default-deny, and exists: false refuses unlabelled files). It gates only the open document and uploaded attachments: text the user types or pastes, mail read through Graph (thread retrieval, search, attachments read inline), connector results and cross-app context are not documented as label-checked, and the key is documented for manifest and bootstrap delivery, not the AppSource install with Claude sign-in. Microsoft Purview lists DLP and sensitivity labels as unsupported for Anthropic Claude interactions, Anthropic's Inference hooks govern claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Code and Claude Tag but not the add-ins, and the OpenTelemetry collector and Compliance API see prompts only after they were sent. Preventive inspection of typed content is the endpoint DLP or SSE product's.

original.mechanism: Custom OpenTelemetry collector receives prompts and document references for detection; no inline blocking; Inference hooks are documented for claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code, not M365

steps.title: Route the audit trail to your DLP pipeline
body: Configure a custom collector endpoint (CORS-enabled, forwarding to your backend) so spans with prompt content and tool inputs reach your inspection tooling.

original.note: The telemetry collector sees prompts after the fact; it cannot block. Preventive DLP on document and mail content is the endpoint DLP or SSE product, and Inference hooks are not documented for the add-ins.

original.mechanism: The add-in is a web page in the Office webview (WebView2 / macOS container); browser and endpoint tooling see it as pivot.claude.ai traffic
original.note: No vendor inspection point; Office on the web places the add-in in a third-party frame that browsers partition.

steps.title: Treat pivot.claude.ai as a governed SaaS origin
body: Apply your web-content policy to https://pivot.claude.ai and the configured model endpoint.

controls.mechanism: Nothing in the product: no documented screening of document, mail, attachment or connector content, and Inference hooks do not cover the add-ins; on third-party platforms every model request passes the organisation's LLM gateway (gateway_url, or azure_base_url for Foundry), the inline point for an AI gateway's injection classifier

controls.note: External by the rule: nothing in the product screens returned content. An AI gateway placed on the third-party gateway path sees every /v1/messages request — open-document content, email bodies and tool results included — and can block it; the Claude-account path goes straight to api.anthropic.com with no inspection point the organisation runs. The Excel, PowerPoint and Word pages say risky operations ask for confirmation and the Outlook page tells users to review drafts from untrusted senders; confirmation gates the action, not the input, and is credited under human approval. Turning off Let Claude work across apps (Organization settings > Office agents) stops an email's instructions steering an edit in another app — containment, not screening.

original.note: No admin-tunable detector; the vendor documents no add-in-specific injection controls.

steps.title: Limit exposure through connectors and scope
body: Enable only vetted connectors and skills for the add-ins and keep cross-app mode off where email content should not steer spreadsheet edits.

The Trust Center resources page lists the two add-in architecture overviews and a Microsoft 365 connector data-flow document; no Outlook-specific overview is listed. Re-assess when the documented gaps move: add-in activity is excluded from Enterprise audit logs and data exports, custom retention is not inherited, Outlook is beta, and the Compliance API coverage label differs between pages. steps.title: Attach the architecture diagrams
body: Download the deployment-mode architecture overview from the Trust Center resources linked on the enterprise-readiness page.

original.mechanism: Enterprise Analytics API per-user and per-surface aggregates and usage CSV exports feed the governance system

steps.title: Pull usage into your platform
body: Use the Claude Enterprise Analytics API for per-surface aggregates and the admin console usage CSV for per-seat spend.

original.mechanism: Organisation settings readable through the console and Compliance API; Trust Center architecture diagrams per deployment mode; add-in activity absent from audit logs

steps.title: Record the documented gaps
body: Note in posture checks that the add-ins ignore custom retention and are excluded from Enterprise audit logs and data exports; use the Trust Center diagrams for the deployment mode.

original.note: Readback only, and incomplete: add-in activity is absent from audit logs and exports, so an SSPM product cannot evidence add-in use from the vendor's streams.

controls.mechanism: The add-in asks the user to confirm an operation it judges risky before it runs, and Outlook drafts and invites land unsent (no Mail.Send scope); OpenTelemetry records each tool call's tool.accept_decision (manual, auto_accept standing approval, deferred); connector Tool permissions (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked) are set org-wide on claude.ai; no add-in setting forces per-action approval

steps.title: Set connector write tools to Needs approval
body: As an Owner, open each connector's Tool permissions under Customize > Connectors and set write/delete tools to Needs approval or Blocked; the restriction applies org-wide and users can't override it.

steps.title: Audit how each action was approved
body: Configure the custom collector and alert on agent.tool_execution spans with tool.read_write write and tool.accept_decision auto_accept.

steps.title: Keep sending with the user
body: Rely on the Outlook add-in's scope set (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, User.Read, offline_access, no Mail.Send): every draft and invite lands unsent for the user to send.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a present human confirms, but the administrator cannot require it and users can hold a standing approval (auto_accept). The add-in decides which operations count as risky; Word's tracked-changes mode is one the user enters, not a policy; Outlook's move and flag operations run through Graph under Mail.ReadWrite and whether they prompt is not documented. Connector Tool permissions are documented for claude.ai connectors; the add-in pages say connectors are enabled in Claude settings but do not state that Needs approval is enforced in the add-ins. On third-party platforms connectors are "coming soon" and admin-attached mcp_servers carry no approval setting.

original.mechanism: Word edits land as tracked changes and comments for review; Outlook drafts are left unsent; no admin-configurable approval gates

steps.title: Keep humans on the output
body: Rely on tracked changes in Word and draft-only mail in Outlook; there is no org-level approval setting for add-in actions.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft Graph access runs on one tenant-wide admin-consented delegated grant to the Claude for Office enterprise app (or your own app), listed and revocable at Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications > Claude for Office > Permissions, with per-user tokens issued by Entra through nested app authentication; MCP connector authorisations are per user and per device, held in the add-in's browser storage, with no admin listing or revoke

steps.title: Review and revoke the Graph grant
body: In Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications open Claude for Office (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266), review Permissions > Admin consent, and revoke there or with Remove-MgOauth2PermissionGrant.

steps.title: Issue connector credentials from your own endpoint
body: In custom-manifest deployments provision connectors per user with mcp_servers from a bootstrap endpoint, so the credential is one your endpoint issues and expires rather than a user's OAuth grant on the device.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the Graph grant is inventoried and revocable in Entra and new tokens stop when the Entra account is disabled, but it is one grant for every user, and a revoke stops new token issuance only — access tokens already cached in each user's MSAL store run to their expiry. Connector grants are the gap: the add-in keeps connector client registrations (claude-mcp-gateways, scoped to the connector's address rather than the user, so shared by anyone on the same OS account) and their tokens in local storage on each device; nothing in the claude.ai console or the Compliance API lists them, only the user (or the connector's own IdP) can revoke them, no expiry is documented, and removing a Claude seat leaves them on disk.

original.note: The add-in runs entirely as the signed-in user; there is no workload or agent identity to govern.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed; no setting for this control (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: No inventory or classification in the product: the add-in keeps no index and reaches the open file, the user's own mailbox and calendar through Graph (Outlook) and user-connected connectors; OpenTelemetry document.url per turn and Compliance API transcripts record which documents were sent, and the data-storage page maps the device-side stores

controls.note: External: inventory and oversharing discovery of the SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content the add-in can reach belong to the DSPM / data-classification product (Microsoft Purview DSPM, for example); the add-in reaches whatever the user opens or their delegated Graph scope allows. It contributes a use record, not an inventory: document.url on every agent.query span, and file contents in Compliance API transcripts (Enterprise). Purview's Anthropic Claude connector (preview) imports the activity feed and chat conversations through the Compliance API; session transcripts, where add-in activity sits, are not among its listed data types. The device-side stores (claude-chat-history holds attached file contents) are an endpoint data store for the organisation's own inventory; the 30-day backend deletion and the 50-conversation cap are retention, not inventory.

original.mechanism: Backend deletion within 30 days; local store bounded to 50 conversations per user/org/app; users can delete all history; export scripts before reimaging; no admin retention setting

steps.title: Manage the device-side store
body: Use the claude-for-msft-365-install plugin export scripts before rebuilds and treat exports as secrets (they contain credentials); control lifetime through profile cleanup rather than an add-in setting.

original.note: Lifecycle only: nothing here discovers or classifies sensitive content in the local store; that is the endpoint DLP or DSPM product's job.

controls.mechanism: Graph and cloud-provider tokens are obtained and used on the device and never reach Anthropic or the model; Claude sign-in, connector and gateway credentials sit unencrypted in the webview's localStorage; keyless options (gateway_auth_source=entra, Bedrock via Entra-to-STS, keyless Foundry) and a bootstrap_url that re-issues the gateway token about five minutes before its declared expiry let the administrator bound credential lifetime; no tunnel

steps.title: Replace static keys with Entra-issued tokens
body: Set entra_sso=1, graph_client_id, entra_scope and gateway_auth_source=entra so the add-in sends each user's short-lived Entra access token to your gateway or Foundry resource and ignores any gateway_token or azure_api_key.

steps.title: Issue gateway tokens from a bootstrap endpoint
body: Serve the gateway token from bootstrap_url with an expiry; the add-in calls the endpoint again about five minutes before expiry and once on a 401, so tokens rotate without users signing out.

steps.title: Keep secrets out of the manifest query string
body: Put gateway_token, azure_api_key, google_client_secret, otlp_headers, inference_headers and mcp_servers after # in the manifest URL; the add-in ignores them in the query string from October 19, 2026.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the administrator can bound lifetime and rotation for the gateway credential (Entra or bootstrap), but the Claude-account access and refresh tokens and MCP connector tokens are held unencrypted in the add-in's localStorage — the OS account is the only boundary — with no admin lifetime or rotation setting, and a static gateway token or API key is a shared secret on every device, held until changed and copied into data exports. Custody is otherwise sound where documented: the Graph token stays in the MSAL cache and goes only to graph.microsoft.com, and the redirect through pivot.claude.ai carries only a code or a consent outcome. Anthropic offers no tunnel for the add-ins; admin-attached mcp_servers are called directly from the user's browser.

original.mechanism: Cloud-provider sign-ins use short-lived tokens renewed on device; a centrally issued gateway token or API key is a shared secret on every device

steps.title: Prefer per-user sign-in over a shared key
body: Use Entra ID / cloud-provider sign-in in third-party mode instead of distributing a gateway API key in the manifest.

original.note: Cloud sign-ins are short-lived; a centrally issued gateway token or API key is a long-lived shared secret on every device, readable from the add-in's local storage by anyone with the user's OS session.

controls.mechanism: Organization settings > Connectors enablement and per-tool Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked on claude.ai (enforcement in the add-ins not stated); Organization settings > Office agents "Let Claude work across apps" plus the per-device "Let Claude work across files"; disabled_features (web_search, file.upload, skills.authoring) and admin-provisioned mcp_servers in custom-manifest deployments; a fixed Graph scope set for Outlook

steps.title: Enable only vetted connectors
body: An Owner adds connectors at Organization settings > Connectors and sets each connector's Tool permissions; the add-ins offer only connectors enabled in Claude settings.

steps.title: Turn cross-app mode off where it is not needed
body: At Organization settings > Office agents turn off Let Claude work across apps; the per-device Let Claude work across files setting is off by default on Team and Enterprise.

steps.title: Remove tools in custom-manifest deployments
body: Set disabled_features (or access_policies deny statements) for web_search, file.upload and skills.authoring, and give each user only the in-network servers listed in mcp_servers.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: connector-level admission and feature switches exist, but no per-tool or read/write scoping per group is documented for the add-ins. Tool permissions are documented for claude.ai connectors, and Enterprise custom roles gate connectors per tool, yet neither page names the Office add-ins. The built-in Office tools (cell and document writes, execute_office_js) have no admin scoping, and Outlook's Graph scope is a fixed delegated set (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, User.Read, offline_access), all-or-nothing at consent. disabled_features applies per user through Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap endpoint; access_policies only through the manifest or bootstrap.

original.mechanism: "Let Claude work across apps" org toggle at Organization settings > Office agents (no published default); a separate per-add-in, per-device "Let Claude work across files" setting is on by default for Pro/Max and off by default for Team/Enterprise; connector and skill availability follows organisation connector settings; Graph consent scopes for Outlook

steps.title: Turn cross-app mode on or off
body: At Organization settings > Office agents toggle "Let Claude work across apps"; each user's add-in also has its own "Let Claude work across files" setting in Settings, on by default on Pro/Max and off by default on Team/Enterprise.

controls.mechanism: Retrieval runs as the user: Office.js reads only the open file or the open mail item, and Outlook's Graph calls use the user's own delegated token; access_policies addin.access statements keyed on sensitivity label or file path restrict which open documents the add-in will run on (manifest or bootstrap); no admin scoping of mailboxes, folders or connector corpora

steps.title: Restrict the add-in to approved documents
body: Add an access_policies allow statement for addin.access listing your General and Public label GUIDs (default-deny for everything else), or deny statements for restricted labels and file_path prefixes such as a restricted share.

steps.title: Own the Graph application
body: Register a single-tenant app with the delegated Graph permissions and set graph_client_id, so approval and Conditional Access for mailbox access sit under your own application.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: identity-scoped retrieval holds — the open document is one the user already opened, and Graph delegated access is bounded by both the consented scopes and the user's own mailbox and calendar permissions, so whatever the user can already reach, oversharing included, is reachable. The admin restriction covers only the open document (label or path), is documented for manifest and bootstrap delivery, and does not scope mailbox search, thread retrieval or connectors. Oversharing analysis of SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange is the DSPM product's.

original.mechanism: The add-in reads only the currently open file or the open email; Outlook access is bounded by the Graph consent granted by the admin

steps.title: Scope Graph consent
body: Grant only the Microsoft Graph permissions the Outlook add-in documents during the one-time admin consent.

original.note: Delegated: the open document is what the user already has; Outlook retrieval carries the Graph consent the admin granted, so that consent, not the user's mailbox permissions, is the ceiling.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 admin center Integrated apps lists the add-ins the organisation deployed, and closing the Office Store and the Exchange add-in user roles blocks others; Organization settings > Connectors is the approved connector catalogue; Compliance API local sessions (product_surface office_agents/*) record use

steps.title: Hold the deployment record in Integrated apps
body: Deploy the Claude add-ins from Settings > Integrated apps and clear Let users access the Office Store, so users run only centrally deployed add-ins.

steps.title: Close Outlook self-install
body: Remove My Marketplace Apps, My Custom Apps and My ReadWriteMailbox Apps from the default role assignment policy under Roles > User roles in the Exchange admin center.

steps.title: Reconcile use against the record
body: List local sessions whose product_surface is office_agents/excel, office_agents/powerpoint, office_agents/word or office_agents/outlook from the Compliance API.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: enforcement exists (only deployed add-ins once self-install is closed; only Owner-enabled connectors) but there is no owner or approval record per add-in or connector. Integrated apps shows what administrators deployed, not copies users installed from AppSource while the store was open or a third-party manifest pointing the add-in at another gateway; connectors a user authorised live only on that user's device. Compliance API session listings cover Claude-account Enterprise use only.

original.mechanism: Microsoft 365 Admin Center integrated-apps inventory of deployed Claude add-ins; Compliance API local sessions with office_agents/* product_surface (beta)

steps.title: Inventory deployments and sessions
body: List deployed add-ins in the M365 Admin Center and, on Enterprise, query local sessions with product_surface office_agents/excel and similar.

original.note: The Admin Center inventory records deployment, not ownership or approval of what the add-ins may do; treat it as an input to the organisation's inventory.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise domain claiming (Organization settings > Organization and access > Security, Migrate accounts using your domain) lists personal Free, Pro and Max accounts on verified domains with plan and last-active date and a CSV export; the add-ins' Claude-account sign-in uses those same accounts

steps.title: Review personal accounts on your domains
body: Turn on Migrate accounts using your domain and review the list of existing personal accounts (email, plan, creation and last active dates), exported as CSV, before claiming them.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the domain-claim list is a genuine discovery signal for personal Claude accounts on verified domains — the accounts a user would sign in to the add-in with — though not for which of them used the add-in. Personal accounts on other addresses, add-ins users installed themselves (Integrated apps does not list them) and third-party manifests pointed at an unsanctioned gateway are found by SSE, CASB or endpoint inventory. The tenant-restriction header and closing the Office Store are prevention, credited here only in this note.

original.mechanism: M365 Admin Center controls whether users can acquire AppSource add-ins; tenant restrictions block personal Claude organisations

steps.title: Control add-in acquisition
body: Manage which users can install the Claude add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and enforce the tenant-restriction header for claude.ai.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API local session endpoints (GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local and /{session_id}/messages, product_surface office_agents/*, scope read:compliance_user_data) return Enterprise add-in transcripts with prompts, responses, tool calls and results; a custom OpenTelemetry collector (otlp_endpoint and otlp_headers at Organization settings > Office agents, or the same keys in the manifest, Entra attributes or bootstrap) receives agent.query, agent.stream and agent.tool_execution spans

steps.title: Pull add-in transcripts from the Compliance API
body: With a Compliance Access Key holding read:compliance_user_data, list GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local with updated_at.gte, keep sessions whose product_surface starts with office_agents, and fetch each session's /messages transcript.

steps.title: Stream spans to a collector you run
body: Set otlp_endpoint (and otlp_headers) at Organization settings > Office agents on Enterprise, or as a configuration key on third-party platforms, pointing at an OpenTelemetry Collector with a CORS-enabled OTLP/HTTP receiver; raise otlp_attr_max_chars if 4,000-character truncation loses evidence.

controls.note: Native by the rule: programmatic export of conversation content and tool events. Boundaries: the Compliance API covers Claude-account Enterprise sign-in only (the add-in pages call this coverage public beta, the Compliance API reference calls it stable), not Pro, Max, Team or third-party-platform deployments, and HIPAA-ready or ZDR organisations capture no local sessions. Add-in activity is not in Enterprise audit logs or data exports, and deleting a conversation in the add-in does not remove the session. OpenTelemetry spans are posted from each user's browser, so a user who controls the client can suppress them — telemetry, not tamper resistance; they omit assistant response text, record connector tools as mcp_tool, and on third-party platforms carry no user identity (correlate session.id with Entra or gateway logs). On the third-party path the organisation's gateway log is the record to fuse with.

original.mechanism: Custom OpenTelemetry collector receives the full span trail per user (CORS required); Compliance API M365 session transcripts (beta); excluded from Enterprise audit logs and data exports

steps.title: Configure a custom collector
body: Point the add-in at an OpenTelemetry Collector you run with a CORS-enabled OTLP HTTP receiver; the collector, not the browser, authenticates to your backend.

controls.mechanism: Remove the add-in (or its assignment) in Integrated apps; deny addin.access through access_policies or disabled_features ("Kill switch: the add-in refuses to run") in custom-manifest or bootstrap deployments; disable the Claude for Office enterprise app (Enabled for users to sign-in? = No) and revoke its admin consent in Entra; no claude.ai setting disables the add-ins

steps.title: Remove the add-in deployment
body: In Settings > Integrated apps select the Claude add-in and remove it (or remove users under Users); a removed add-in is not accessible to any user.

steps.title: Make the add-in refuse to run
body: Deliver disabled_features=addin.access, or an access_policies deny for addin.access, through the manifest, Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap endpoint; the add-in reads it when it loads.

steps.title: Stop token issuance in Entra
body: In Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Claude for Office > Properties set Enabled for users to sign-in? to No, which prevents all tokens being issued for the app, and revoke its admin-consented permissions.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: each stop blocks the next load or the next token, not a task pane already running, and the delay is not documented (Microsoft gives 24 to 72 hours for deployments to appear; removal timing is not stated). Configuration keys are read when the add-in loads — only served settings, which are re-read while it runs, are documented as applying mid-session, and they are preview. Disabling the Entra app stops new tokens; cached Graph access tokens run to expiry. Connector grants on each device cannot be revoked in bulk, and copies users installed themselves from AppSource are not removed by Integrated apps. No claude.ai control disables the add-ins; removing a member's seat or revoking the gateway token at your gateway is the practical stop for inference, though the add-in pages do not document its effect. Local history, skills and credentials persist until the device profile is wiped.

original.mechanism: Remove the add-in deployment in the M365 Admin Center, disable cross-app mode, remove the user's Claude seat; local data persists until the profile is wiped

steps.title: Withdraw the add-in
body: Remove or block the add-ins in the M365 Admin Center and turn off "Let Claude work across apps"; wipe the device profile to remove local history and credentials.

original.note: Withdrawing the add-in applies at the client's next add-in catalogue refresh, and seat removal at the next request; the docs state no delay, so measure it.
