tools.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

variants.name: AgentCore harness (config-only managed loop; CreateHarness / InvokeHarness)
variants.note: GA June 2026. AWS runs the Strands-based loop in a microVM per session; model, prompt, tools, skills, memory and limits are configuration. Built-in shell and file_operations tools are on unless allowedTools restricts them.

variants.name: AgentCore Runtime (bring-your-own agent code on microVMs; InvokeAgentRuntime)
variants.note: The escape hatch: AWS supplies the microVM, identity and endpoints, the loop is your code, and it gets Memory, Gateway, Identity and guardrails only where the code calls them.

variants.name: AgentCore Runtime on Instances (capacity providers; EC2 managed instances in your account)
variants.note: Sessions of up to 14 days on one EC2 instance per session; several agents can share an instance and are not isolated from each other. Data and EBS volumes stay in your account and VPC.

summary: AWS's decomposed agent platform: Runtime (a Firecracker microVM per session, bring-your-own code or the config-only managed harness), Memory (short- and long-term, scoped by actor and session), Gateway (tools from Lambda, OpenAPI, Smithy and MCP servers behind one MCP endpoint with inbound and outbound auth), Identity (a workload identity per agent and a token vault for OAuth tokens and API keys), Policy (Cedar policy engines and Bedrock Guardrails checks evaluated at the gateway), Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability (CloudWatch and X-Ray in your account) and Evaluations, each billed separately and driven over the bedrock-agentcore(-control) APIs with IAM SigV4 or a JWT from your IdP. Inference is Amazon Bedrock by default; the harness can also call OpenAI, Gemini or any LiteLLM provider directly.

Governance is IAM-native: condition keys on the control plane (subnets and security groups, gateway authorizer type, policy engine and mode, target and credential-provider types, memory actor and namespace) let an organisation set floors by SCP that a builder cannot lower, and the Cedar engine is default-deny per tool call. The gaps are boundaries rather than missing features: only traffic through a Gateway is policy-evaluated and guardrail-screened, InvokeHarness callers can override tools, skills, prompt and model per call, the harness runs on the public network with managed memory on (API default) unless configured otherwise, and session IDs are not bound to the caller.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pay per AgentCore service used (Runtime per-second vCPU and memory, Memory events, records and retrievals, Gateway calls, Browser and Code Interpreter sessions, CloudWatch ingestion); the harness itself has no separate charge. GA; harness GA June 2026.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Harness: Amazon Bedrock (Converse Stream, or Responses / Chat Completions via Bedrock Mantle), OpenAI, Google Gemini or any LiteLLM-compatible provider, switchable per turn and overridable per InvokeHarness call; model fields (modelId, apiBase, additionalParams) pass through unvalidated. Runtime: whatever model the customer's code calls.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Everything runs in AWS: prompts, tool inputs and outputs and session files in the microVM (public network unless VPC mode), memory in AgentCore Memory, traces and logs in your CloudWatch. Memory extraction, Policy and Evaluations use cross-region inference inside the geography; a harness configured for OpenAI, Gemini or LiteLLM sends the conversation to that provider.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: MicroVM state is ephemeral and memory-sanitized at session end (idle 900 s, max 8 h by default); session storage persists per runtimeSessionId until the runtime is deleted; Memory events expire per eventExpiryDuration (3–365 days), long-term records until deleted; traces follow your CloudWatch retention. Bedrock content is not used to improve base models or shared with model providers; third-party providers' terms apply to their calls.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide (harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Policy, tools)

facts.label: Compliance scope
facts.value: HIPAA eligible; FedRAMP (Class C and D), SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 and CSA STAR per the developer guide (the AgentCore FAQ still says FedRAMP is being pursued); reports in AWS Artifact.

facts.label: Network modes
facts.value: networkMode PUBLIC (default) or VPC (ENIs in your subnets via AWSServiceRoleForBedrockAgentCoreNetwork) for harness, Runtime, Code Interpreter and Browser; Code Interpreter also offers SANDBOX. Inbound API calls can use a PrivateLink interface endpoint; private MCP targets are reached via VPC Lattice.

facts.label: Predecessor
facts.value: Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic closed to new customers on 2026-07-30 (maintenance mode, model catalog frozen); AWS recommends migrating to the AgentCore harness.

items.title: Strip the InvokeHarness override surface in the front end
body: InvokeHarness accepts tools, allowedTools, skills, systemPrompt, model, actorId and limits per call, and the harness does not validate additionalParams, apiBase or modelId. Forward only the user's message and derive actorId and runtimeSessionId server-side; lifecycle hooks are the one setting a caller cannot override.

items.title: Set organisation floors by SCP
body: Deny CreateAgentRuntime / UpdateAgentRuntime / CreateCodeInterpreter / CreateBrowser without bedrock-agentcore:subnets, and CreateGateway / UpdateGateway unless bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode is ENFORCE; restrict CreateGatewayTarget by McpTargetConfigurationType and CredentialProviderType.

riskNotes.note: CreateHarness through the API provisions managed memory when memory is omitted (the CLI defaults to none), and actorId is whatever the caller passes; spans carry model payloads and tool request and response data into CloudWatch, where CVE-2026-15737 showed raw prompts landing in span attributes.

Skills fetched from S3 or Git are injected as trusted input, and callers can override skills per invocation. Bedrock Guardrails' prompt-attack filter does not evaluate toolResult content on the Converse path, so only guardrail policies at the Gateway screen what tools return.

SigV4 callers carry no per-user identity into downstream tools, the gateway service role is shared by every GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE target, and GetWorkloadAccessTokenForUserId trusts a caller-supplied userId.

Token passthrough forwards the caller's inbound token to a gateway target unmodified, and invocation is authorised against the runtime ARN, not the session: a shared backend principal can route one user's request into another user's runtimeSessionId, and the credentials it holds, unless the application binds them.

shell and file_operations are available in every harness session unless allowedTools removes them, commands run as root in the microVM, and InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand executes commands without the model at a higher privilege level.
AWS Agent Registry auto-detection catalogs AgentCore Runtimes and Gateways across AWS Organizations member accounts; agents built on other services or outside AWS are registered by hand.

remote_mcp tools are declared by URL in the harness and fetched live; Gateway MCP targets cache the tool catalog until SynchronizeGatewayTargets or pin it with mcpToolSchema, which is the re-gating point for definition changes.

controls.mechanism: IAM Identity Center MFA (Settings > Authentication > Multi-factor authentication, "Every time they sign in (always-on)") for the people who reach the AgentCore console and control plane; aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent in role trust policies or on bedrock-agentcore write actions for IAM users

steps.title: Require MFA at every workforce sign-in
body: In the IAM Identity Center console choose Settings > Authentication > Multi-factor authentication > Configure and set Prompt users for MFA to Every time they sign in (always-on), the default.

steps.title: Refuse definition changes without MFA
body: Require aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent true in the trust policy of the role that holds CreateHarness, UpdateHarness, UpdateAgentRuntime, UpdateGateway and credential-provider actions, or deny those actions to IAM users with BoolIfExists false, which also refuses long-term access keys (they never carry the key).

controls.note: Rated on console and account access that can change harness, runtime, gateway, policy and credential definitions, per the architecture rule. Native where the identity source is the Identity Center directory, AWS Managed Microsoft AD or AD Connector; with an external IdP the MFA section is not available and MFA is the IdP's, so an organisation federating that way is at partial. Workloads call InvokeHarness and InvokeAgentRuntime with SigV4 role credentials or a JWT from the configured discovery URL; end-user MFA is the deployer's front end or the IdP behind CUSTOM_JWT.

controls.mechanism: ListHarnesses / ListHarnessVersions / ListAgentRuntimes / ListGateways / ListWorkloadIdentities with tags; AWS Agent Registry records (DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED via UpdateRegistryRecordStatus) with AWS Organizations auto-detection of Runtimes and Gateways; IAM and SCPs on the create and update actions

steps.title: Turn on organisation-wide auto-detection
body: Enable auto-detection on an organization-scoped registry from the delegated administrator so every AgentCore Runtime and Gateway in member accounts becomes a record with a DETECTED_FROM provenance entry naming its ARN.

steps.title: Curate records through approval
body: Records move DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED; route the EventBridge submit event to your review workflow and approve or reject with UpdateRegistryRecordStatus (turn auto-approval off).

steps.title: Restrict who can deploy a definition
body: Grant CreateHarness, UpdateHarness, CreateAgentRuntime, UpdateAgentRuntime and CreateGatewayTarget only to the delivery pipeline's role; the harness actions also require the matching AgentRuntime action on the same ARN.

controls.note: The listable inventory is native (every harness, runtime, version, gateway and workload identity) and the tenant gates creation by IAM and SCP. Registry approval gates discovery, not execution: nothing consults it before InvokeHarness, so "unregistered means denied" is IAM's job. Auto-detection covers Runtimes and Gateways; the docs do not say whether harnesses (Runtimes underneath) appear as their own records. The public-preview registry namespace (bedrock-agentcore) ends on 2026-10-30.

controls.mechanism: Immutable versions created on every UpdateHarness / UpdateAgentRuntime; named endpoints pinned by CreateHarnessEndpoint / UpdateHarnessEndpoint targetVersion (UpdateAgentRuntimeEndpoint for Runtime); A/B tests through an AgentCore Gateway with control and treatment weights scored by online evaluation, then promote or stop

steps.title: Pin production to an endpoint and roll back by pointer
body: Create a production endpoint with targetVersion; DEFAULT follows every update, the named endpoint does not until UpdateHarnessEndpoint moves it, and moving it back to the prior version is the rollback.

steps.title: Canary through an A/B test
body: Run agentcore run ab-test with --control-weight 90 --treatment-weight 10 and a per-variant online evaluation; stop reverts all traffic to control, promote writes the treatment into agentcore.json for the next deploy.

steps.title: Score each version before it moves
body: Attach online evaluation configurations (sampling rate, built-in evaluators such as Builtin.GoalSuccessRate and Builtin.ToolSelectionAccuracy, or custom ones) to the endpoints under test.

controls.note: Versioning, one-step rollback and progressive traffic are native; the evaluation in the promotion path scores but does not block (a person runs promote), evaluators measure quality and safety rather than adversarial behaviour, and no automated rollback on regression is documented. The traffic split applies only to requests routed through a Gateway (one running test per gateway, sticky by session ID); A/B walkthroughs use Runtime endpoints, and a front end that calls InvokeHarness on DEFAULT gets every update at once. Rated native on the architecture rule because versions, endpoints, weighted traffic and an evaluation step all exist, which the first-party runtimes do not offer.

controls.mechanism: A workload identity minted per agent by Runtime and Gateway (arn ...:workload-identity-directory/default/ workload-identity/<name>, harness_<agentName>-* for harnesses), listed by ListWorkloadIdentities and removed by DeleteWorkloadIdentity; a per-agent IAM execution role; workload access tokens binding user and agent (GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT)

steps.title: Inventory the agent identity directory
body: Run aws bedrock-agentcore-control list-workload-identities and review creation source, owner tags and unused identities; the directory is one per account and Region.

steps.title: Give each agent its own role and providers
body: Create one execution role per agent whose GetResourceOauth2Token / GetResourceApiKey statements name only that workload identity's ARN and its credential providers, never "*".

steps.title: Refuse unverifiable user binding
body: Deny bedrock-agentcore:GetWorkloadAccessTokenForUserId where a JWT is available so every workload token is minted by GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT from a verified issuer and subject.

controls.note: The platform mints and inventories a principal per agent, which the pin says to select for. Separation is IAM's: the service enforces no binding between workload identities and credential providers in the same account, so agents sharing an execution role share reach. Runtime- and Gateway-managed identities cannot fetch workload tokens directly. The workload identity authenticates to AgentCore services only; a third-party tool sees whatever credential the provider issued.

controls.mechanism: AgentCore Gateway outbound authorization per target — OAuth client credentials, authorization code (tokens keyed to user and workload), on-behalf-of token exchange, API key, gateway IAM role or caller IAM credentials — injected by the gateway; SCP keys bedrock-agentcore:CredentialProviderType and CredentialProviderScope on CreateGatewayTarget / UpdateGatewayTarget

steps.title: Put tools behind a gateway with per-target credentials
body: Register each MCP, OpenAPI or Lambda tool as a gateway target with its own credential provider; prefer the token exchange (on-behalf-of) grant so the downstream token carries both user and agent.

steps.title: Authenticate callers with a JWT, not SigV4
body: Set authorizerConfiguration customJWTAuthorizer (discoveryUrl, allowedClients) on the harness; with SigV4 callers the harness propagates no per-user identity and user-scoped vault tokens and on-behalf-of exchange are unavailable.

steps.title: Constrain credential types organisation-wide
body: Deny CreateGatewayTarget and UpdateGatewayTarget unless bedrock-agentcore:CredentialProviderType is on your approved list, keeping JWT_PASSTHROUGH off targets outside the trust boundary.

controls.note: Held outside the agent and injected per destination with per-user scoping on the Gateway path, which meets the architecture rule. Paths outside it: remote_mcp headers on the harness (plain text, or a ${arn:...} token-vault reference the harness resolves at invocation) and Runtime code calling GetResourceOauth2Token or GetResourceApiKey both put the credential inside the session process. The gateway service role is shared by every GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE target and is the upper bound for any caller, and token passthrough forwards the inbound token unmodified.

controls.mechanism: Policy in AgentCore: a Cedar (Dogwood-compatible) policy engine attached to a gateway as policyEngineConfiguration {arn, mode ENFORCE | LOG_ONLY}, default-deny and forbid-wins on every tools/call over principal, tool and context.input, with temporal session rules; SCP keys bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineArn and PolicyEngineMode; harness before_tool_call Lambda hooks

steps.title: Attach a policy engine in ENFORCE
body: Create a policy engine and set policyEngineConfiguration arn and mode on CreateGateway or UpdateGateway; run LOG_ONLY first, then ENFORCE, in which anything not permitted is denied.

steps.title: Write per-tool rules over the arguments
body: Permit named actions such as AgentCore::Action::"RefundTool___process_refund" for a principal only when a context.input condition holds (amount < 500), and forbid the rest.

steps.title: Make ENFORCE a floor builders cannot lower
body: By SCP, deny CreateGateway and UpdateGateway unless bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode is ENFORCE and bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineArn is an approved engine.

steps.title: Cover tools the gateway does not see
body: Configure a before_tool_call hook with a Lambda target and failureMode deny; it receives toolName, toolType and toolInput for built-in, remote MCP, gateway and inline tools and can skip the call.

controls.note: Two AWS pages disagree: policy-enforcement-modes says no condition key protects the mode beyond UpdateGateway, while the Gateway condition-keys page and the service authorization reference list bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode for CreateGateway and UpdateGateway; set the SCP and test that a LOG_ONLY or null update is refused. The deterministic engine sees only gateway traffic: harness shell and file_operations, Browser, Code Interpreter and direct remote_mcp tools are outside it, the before_tool_call hook is the deployer's own Lambda logic, inline_function (custom) tools return to the application, InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand bypasses the loop (IAM is its only gate), and Runtime code reaches the engine only if it routes tools through a gateway.

controls.mechanism: Memory events scoped by actorId + sessionId, long-term namespaces such as /strategy/{memoryStrategyId}/actor/{actorId}/, IAM condition keys bedrock-agentcore:actorId, sessionId and namespace, Cedar FGAC through the Memory gateway connector, eventExpiryDuration, DeleteEvent and DeleteMemoryRecord; harness memory disabled | managedMemoryConfiguration | agentCoreMemoryConfiguration

steps.title: Decide memory on every harness
body: The API provisions managed memory when memory is omitted; set memory {"disabled": {}} or attach a BYO memory (agentCoreMemoryConfiguration) with a customer-managed key and eventExpiryDuration.

steps.title: Scope long-term namespaces per actor
body: Use namespace templates ending in /actor/{actorId}/ with a trailing slash, and restrict callers with the bedrock-agentcore:actorId and namespace condition keys.

steps.title: Bind actorId to the signed-in user
body: Front Memory with a gateway Memory connector and a Cedar policy that permits event access only when the request's actorId equals the JWT sub.

steps.title: Expire and delete
body: Set eventExpiryDuration (3–365 days) and remove poisoned or personal records with DeleteEvent and DeleteMemoryRecord.

controls.note: Scope, disable, expire and delete are all settable. On the harness actorId is an InvokeHarness field, so isolation holds only if the front end derives it from the authenticated user, and the documented execution-role policy grants memory actions with no actor condition. Contents are not validated: AWS puts memory-poisoning prevention on the customer (sanitise with guardrails before CreateEvent). Long-term extraction runs cross-region inside the geography. The CLI creates harnesses without memory; the API does not.

controls.mechanism: AWS Artifact audit reports and the AgentCore compliance-validation page feed the buyer's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Compliance validation for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
AWS Artifact
AWS services in scope by compliance program

controls.note: A TPRM platform holds the assessment; AWS supplies the evidence. AgentCore is HIPAA eligible and listed for FedRAMP Class C and D, SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 and CSA STAR on the developer guide, while the AgentCore FAQ still says FedRAMP is being pursued — confirm on services-in-scope. There is no zero data retention mode: retention is what you configure. Memory, Policy and Evaluations use cross-region inference inside the geography, and a harness pointed at OpenAI, Gemini or LiteLLM adds that provider as a subprocessor to assess separately. Re-assess on the 2026 bulletins.

controls.mechanism: A dedicated Firecracker microVM per runtimeSessionId (harness and Runtime) with isolated CPU, memory and filesystem, terminated and memory-sanitized at session end (lifecycleConfiguration idleRuntimeSessionTimeout default 900 s, maxLifetime default 28800 s); Code Interpreter and Browser run their own sessions; Instances run one EC2 instance per session

steps.title: One session ID per user conversation
body: Generate runtimeSessionId server-side from the authenticated user (33+ characters) and never accept it from the client; AgentCore does not enforce session-to-user mapping.

steps.title: Bound the microVM's life
body: Set lifecycleConfiguration idleRuntimeSessionTimeout and maxLifetime on CreateAgentRuntime or UpdateAgentRuntime (harness: idle and lifetime limits) so compute is reclaimed promptly.

steps.title: Keep untrusted agents off shared Instances
body: On the Instances compute type the session, not the agent, is the isolation unit; give agents that are not mutually trusted separate sessions or separate capacity providers.

controls.note: Inside the microVM: shell, file_operations, a custom container and, on Runtime, the customer's whole agent loop. Outside: inference, Gateway, Memory, and Browser and Code Interpreter sessions (their own sandboxes). Commands run as root in the microVM and InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand at a higher privilege; a caller allowed to invoke the runtime ARN can route into any session ID it knows. On Instances the boundary is an EC2 instance in your account shared by co-located agents. Unit 42 showed Code Interpreter SANDBOX mode leaking DNS in 2026; AWS remediated it.

controls.mechanism: networkConfiguration.networkMode PUBLIC (default) | VPC with subnets and security groups on the harness, Runtime, Code Interpreter and Browser; Code Interpreter SANDBOX mode; IAM keys bedrock-agentcore:subnets and securityGroups to force VPC mode; host allowlisting only by the VPC's own firewall and DNS controls

steps.title: Run sessions in VPC mode
body: Create the harness with environment agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration networkMode VPC and private subnets and security groups; add VPC endpoints for ECR, S3 and bedrock-runtime instead of a NAT route.

steps.title: Force VPC mode by SCP
body: Deny CreateAgentRuntime, UpdateAgentRuntime, CreateCodeInterpreter and CreateBrowser when bedrock-agentcore:subnets or securityGroups is null or not on the approved list.

steps.title: Close the code interpreter
body: Under AgentCore > Built-in Tools > Code Interpreter > Create, choose Network settings Sandbox (limited external network access) or VPC rather than Public network.

controls.note: Partial on the architecture rule: AgentCore offers a network mode, not a provider-enforced host list. Exact-host allowlisting is the VPC's firewall and DNS filtering — ours to run, as for a self-hosted worker. The harness defaults to the public network, and CreateHarness / UpdateHarness are not among the operations documented to evaluate the subnet condition keys. Paths the mode does not govern: model inference, Gateway targets (egress from the gateway, with its own private endpoints) and the Web Search connector, which is served inside AWS.

controls.mechanism: allowedTools patterns on the harness (@builtin/shell, @server/tool, globs; all tools when omitted); per-target tools at the gateway with Cedar rules over tool and arguments; MCP targets in DEFAULT listing mode cache the catalog until SynchronizeGatewayTargets, or pin it with mcpToolSchema; SCP key bedrock-agentcore:McpTargetConfigurationType

steps.title: Name the tools the agent may select
body: Set allowedTools to the specific entries the agent needs (for example "@builtin/file_operations", "@crm/read_*"), leaving shell out unless required.

steps.title: Admit MCP servers through gateway targets
body: Register servers as gateway targets with a static mcpToolSchema, or review the diff before each SynchronizeGatewayTargets, so a server's new tools stay unavailable until re-approved.

steps.title: Remove direct command execution
body: Grant bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand to nobody who fronts users; allowedTools does not govern it.

controls.note: Per-tool enablement and argument-level permission at the gateway meet the rule. InvokeHarness accepts tools, allowedTools and skills per call and no condition key restricts those fields, so any principal with InvokeHarness can widen the set unless the front end strips them; the next UpdateHarness can undo it unless IAM restricts that action. remote_mcp servers declared by URL are admitted as declared and nothing verifies what they serve; the gateway's cached or static catalog is the only re-gating on definition change.

controls.mechanism: Token vault for OAuth tokens, client credentials and API keys encrypted with an AWS owned or customer managed KMS key; client secrets in Secrets Manager; Private Key JWT client authentication with the key in KMS; SigV4 with short-lived STS role credentials or a JWT for the API; no tunnel — PrivateLink inbound and VPC ENIs or VPC Lattice outbound, authorised by IAM

steps.title: Encrypt the token vault with your key
body: Configure a single-Region symmetric customer managed KMS key (by ARN) for the token vault, and a CMK on the credential providers' Secrets Manager secrets.

steps.title: Replace shared client secrets with Private Key JWT
body: On a CustomOauth2 credential provider, choose Private Key JWT and give the ARN of an asymmetric KMS signing key, so AgentCore Identity signs client assertions in KMS instead of holding a secret.

steps.title: Scope who can read a credential
body: Name exact provider ARNs in GetResourceOauth2Token, GetResourceApiKey and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue statements, and prefer gateway-injected credentials to remote_mcp headers or code retrieval.

controls.note: Partial: the store is encrypted and the API runs on short-lived credentials, but the vault is not write-only. GetResourceOauth2Token and GetResourceApiKey return values to any workload whose role allows them, and the documented harness execution-role policy grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the credential's secret; only gateway-injected credentials never reach the agent's process (the harness docs say agent code never sees model API keys, without saying whether its shell can). Tunnel story: AWS offers no outbound-only tunnel; private MCP servers are reached through VPC mode or gateway private endpoints on VPC Lattice, so there is no tunnel token to rotate.

controls.mechanism: inline_function tools pause the loop (stopReason tool_use) and hand toolUseId and the model's input to the caller, which must return the matching toolResult on the same runtimeSessionId; the harness rejects caller-supplied toolUse blocks; before_tool_call Lambda hooks (allow or deny, timeoutSeconds up to 900); temporal Cedar rules requiring a prior approval action

steps.title: Route consequential actions through inline functions
body: Define the action as an inline_function tool, show the pending toolUseId and input to a person, and send the toolResult only after they approve.

steps.title: Require a recorded approval at the gateway
body: Write a temporal policy that permits the action only if an approval action's response (output approved true) was recorded formerly within 1h in the same policy session for the same resource.

controls.note: Partial: a pause bound to the exact call exists only for inline functions, which the application executes anyway. Built-in, remote MCP and gateway tools have no per-call ask mode; the before_tool_call hook and the temporal policy make the approval the deployer's own Lambda or approval tool, and an after_tool_call event confirms the harness processed a client result, not that the action happened. CVE-2026-18830 (fixed) let a caller dispatch configured tools without the model.

controls.mechanism: Guardrails in Policy in AgentCore at the gateway: BedrockGuardrails::PromptAttack, ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation checks in a when guardrails block — forbid over context.input, suppressOutput over context.output of MCP, HTTP runtime and inference targets — scored by bedrock:InvokeGuardrailChecks with the decision logged

steps.title: Screen what tools return
body: Add a suppressOutput policy whose when guardrails block runs BedrockGuardrails checks over the target response's context.output fields, and a forbid policy with PromptAttack(["PROMPT_INJECTION"]) over context.input.

steps.title: Grant the check and calibrate
body: Give the gateway execution role bedrock:InvokeGuardrailChecks, run the engine in LOG_ONLY to read the scores, then set thresholds (defaults 0.4 prompt attack, 0.2 content and sensitive data).

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: the gateway can classify returned tool content with a block and a logged decision, but the documented output-side checks are ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation; PromptAttack is documented over context.input (what the agent sends), and injection screening of what a tool returns is not shown, so it is not credited until a LOG_ONLY test proves it. It covers gateway targets only, in the Regions the guardrails table lists (not all AgentCore Regions); the docs' output examples use ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation, so test PromptAttack over context.output in LOG_ONLY before relying on it. Not screened: harness built-in tools, direct remote_mcp results, Browser pages, Code Interpreter output and memory retrieval. A guardrailConfig on the model does not help: on Converse it does not evaluate toolResult blocks.

controls.mechanism: AgentCore Observability: harness invocations emit traces, logs and metrics (model calls, tool invocations with payloads, memory operations, shell commands) to CloudWatch and X-Ray in your account, spans in /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<id>-<endpoint> (UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED, default for agents created from 2026-07-20) or aws/spans; Runtime via ADOT; CloudTrail management and data events

steps.title: Turn on Transaction Search
body: Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search once per account (CloudWatch > Application Signals > Transaction search); harness traces then flow with no further configuration.

steps.title: Instrument Runtime code
body: Add ADOT with AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true and AWS_GENAI_CONTENT_EXTRACTION_OPT_OUT=true to keep tool request and response data on spans; without instrumentation a Runtime agent emits no steps.

steps.title: Record data events off-account
body: Create a trail with advanced event selectors for AgentCore data events into an S3 bucket in a separate logging account.

controls.note: Every step lands in our own account, so retention, KMS and SIEM subscription are ours. Not tamper-evident by itself: principals with CloudWatch Logs permissions can alter or delete log groups, so ship to a separate account for non-repudiation. Spans carry prompts and tool data (CVE-2026-15737 was the SDK writing raw prompts to span attributes). Correlation IDs propagate from the harness to Gateway, Memory, Code Interpreter and Browser; a Runtime agent's trace is only as complete as its instrumentation.

controls.mechanism: StopRuntimeSession (terminates the session and its streaming responses at once), StopCodeInterpreterSession / StopBrowserSession; a resource-based policy Deny on the runtime or DeleteHarness / DeleteAgentRuntime; credential revocation by deleting credential providers, Revoke active sessions on the execution role, and a gateway rate limit of 0 for a caller

steps.title: Stop the running session
body: Call StopRuntimeSession with the runtime ARN (for a harness, GetHarness environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.agentRuntimeArn), qualifier and runtimeSessionId; retry on 409 RetryableConflictException.

steps.title: Refuse new sessions
body: Attach a resource-based policy denying InvokeAgentRuntime on the runtime and its endpoints, or delete the harness (pass deleteManagedMemory=false to keep memory for forensics).

steps.title: Revoke what it held
body: In the IAM console choose the execution role > Revoke sessions > Revoke active sessions, delete its OAuth2 and API key credential providers, and set a rate of 0 on the gateway for its caller (propagates within 30 seconds).

controls.note: Stop, block and revoke are each documented: StopRuntimeSession "instantly terminates" the session and its streaming, and Revoke active sessions denies the role's current credentials immediately. The harness pages do not name StopRuntimeSession; the harness API returns the underlying agentRuntimeArn it takes, so rehearse it on a harness. Deleting a credential provider has no stated propagation time, gateway rate limits fail open on transient errors, ENIs can persist 8 hours after deletion, and nothing cancels work the agent handed to other agents.

tools.name: Cline

variants.name: Cline for VS Code and its forks (Marketplace / Open VSX saoudrizwan.claude-dev, v4.1.21 2026-09-24)
Cline for JetBrains IDEs
Cline CLI (npm cline, v3.0.65), with the TUI, ACP mode, Kanban and chat connectors

summary: Cline's open-source (Apache-2.0) coding agent — the IDE-extension harness class: a loop over file, shell, search, web-fetch and browser tools, MCP servers, rules, skills and hooks, driven by a present developer in VS Code, its forks or JetBrains, and from the same core as a CLI with a TUI, an ACP mode, a local hub daemon, a Kanban board and chat connectors. The developer brings the model: a pasted provider key (30+ providers, local runtimes included) or the Cline provider billed in Cline credits.

Prompts, file contents and tool output go straight to the chosen provider, or through Cline when the Cline provider is used. Task history, checkpoints (a shadow Git repository) and provider credentials stay under ~/.cline on the device. Anonymous usage telemetry goes to Cline when the Cline Telemetry toggle is on.

The Open Source tier ships no organisation control plane. Cline Enterprise adds one: SSO through WorkOS AuthKit, Owner / Admin / Member roles, and a remote configuration held at app.cline.bot that the client applies to members signed in to the organisation — provider and model pinning, yoloModeAllowed, MCP server policy (allowedMCPServers, remoteMCPServers, blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers, mcpMarketplaceEnabled), telemetry, OpenTelemetry export and Prompt Storage to the organisation's bucket. It holds no per-tool rules, sandbox or egress policy, and the docs describe no device-side key that forces the organisation sign-in.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Open Source (free; bring your own key, the pay-as-you-go Cline provider, or ClinePass at $9.99/month) and Enterprise (custom: SSO, role-based access control, centralised billing, config management, provider limits, authentication logs, the JetBrains extension; the FAQ adds VPC deployment, SCIM, OIDC and OpenTelemetry). No separate Teams tier is listed.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Direct from the device to the configured provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex, Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, LiteLLM, Ollama, LM Studio and others), or through the Cline provider. Enterprise remote configuration can pin the provider and its base URL (openAiBaseUrl, LiteLLM baseUrl, Anthropic baseUrl, awsBedrockEndpoint); members signed in to the organisation cannot select another provider or switch to a personal account.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, rules, file contents and tool results to the model endpoint; anonymous feature, task and error events to Cline while Cline Telemetry is on (the docs call it opt-in; remote-config telemetryEnabled sets a default a user can still turn off); on Enterprise, optional OTLP export to the organisation's collector and Prompt Storage of each task's full conversation to its S3 or R2 bucket.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: With the developer's own key Cline states it does not collect the request; with Cline-provided keys it collects the request to forward it, the upstream provider's terms apply, and some providers may train on it unless opted out. The privacy policy (updated 2025-09-24) states no retention period; the Enterprise page says code and prompts aren't used for training.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: docs.cline.bot/llms.txt — Config, Auto Approve, Rules, Skills, Plugins, MCP, Checkpoints, CLI reference, Connectors, Kanban remote access, Networking and proxies, and the Enterprise section (remote configuration, YOLO and MCP controls, SSO, members, telemetry, OpenTelemetry, Prompt Storage).

facts.label: Distribution & updates
facts.value: VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX (extension id saoudrizwan.claude-dev), JetBrains Marketplace (plugin 28247), npm (cline; Kanban as the kanban package). The extension updates under the editor's own auto-update policy; the CLI checks for and installs a new release at startup unless CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 (source only). npm releases have been published with OIDC provenance since the 2026-02 token compromise.

facts.label: Listening ports
facts.value: Hub daemon on 127.0.0.1:25463 (CLINE_HUB_ADDRESS), Kanban on 127.0.0.1:3484 (--host or KANBAN_RUNTIME_HOST widens it), connector webhook listeners on the port passed with --port.

items.title: Enterprise remote configuration
body: Admins edit the organisation's settings at app.cline.bot (Settings → Cline Settings, Enable settings) and signed-in members download and apply them. Documented fields: provider settings with allowed models and base URLs, yoloModeAllowed, telemetryEnabled, mcpMarketplaceEnabled, allowedMCPServers, remoteMCPServers (name, url, headers, alwaysEnabled), blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers, the openTelemetry* export fields and enterpriseTelemetry.promptUploading. The schema in the source also carries globalRules, globalWorkflows and globalSkills (alwaysEnabled) and kanbanEnabled. The YOLO page says the policy cannot be overridden by users; the OpenTelemetry override page says environment variables win over it.

items.title: Local configuration
body: Global state lives in ~/.cline (data/settings/providers.json for provider keys, global-settings.json, cline_mcp_settings.json, plus rules, hooks, skills, agents, plugins and cron specs) and ~/Documents/Cline; project configuration in .cline/ and .clinerules/ travels with the repository. Workspace rules win over global ones on conflict. CLINE_DATA_DIR, --config and --data-dir relocate the store, and CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS carries the only rule language for shell commands.

riskNotes.note: Repository rules (.clinerules/, .cline/rules/, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, AGENTS.md), files, fetch_web results and MCP output enter context with no vendor screening. Embrace The Red (2025-08) exfiltrated .env contents through a markdown image rendered in the chat after an indirect injection, unfixed at publication; Clinejection (2026-02) used the same class against Cline's own issue-triage bot and reached its publish tokens.

The CLI starts with --auto-approve true, "Execute safe commands" trusts the model's own requires_approval flag (CVE-2026-52024 bypassed it, and CVE-2026-52025 ran an OS command from a URL tile without the dialog), and an Enterprise administrator can withdraw only YOLO, not the per-category auto-approve toggles.

The harness itself arrives from npm, the VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX and the JetBrains Marketplace: a leaked npm token published cline@2.3.0 with a postinstall that installed openclaw globally (GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7). CLI plugins install from any npm package, git repository or HTTPS file URL, and MCP servers commonly launch through npx, with no allowlist for either outside Enterprise MCP policy.

MCP server definitions and workspace hooks are plain files the developer, the agent or a cloned repository can change; the dashboard WebSocket flaw (CVE-2026-59723) let any web page add a stdio MCP server to the settings file. Enterprise remoteMCPServers with blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers and mcpMarketplaceEnabled false is the only organisation-held server list.

Provider keys sit in ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json and MCP tokens in the MCP settings file. Prompt Storage copies every file the agent read and every command output into the organisation's bucket, so that bucket needs source-code-level access control.
The extension has no turn or spend cap and the CLI's --timeout defaults to 0; hub-hosted sessions and scheduled agents keep running with no client attached.

controls.mechanism: None on the remote surfaces: the Kanban board (127.0.0.1:3484, widened with --host or KANBAN_RUNTIME_HOST) has no login of its own; CLI chat connectors (cline connect) admit by platform identity (--allowed-user-id for Telegram) or an admission script (--hook-command); Cline Enterprise SSO (WorkOS AuthKit to the IdP) covers the account sign-in only

evidence.title: Kanban remote access (tunnels, VPNs, no built-in authentication)
CLI connectors (--allowed-user-id, --hook-command)
Cline Enterprise SSO setup (WorkOS AuthKit)
GHSA-5c57-rqjx-35g2 — Kanban server cross-origin WebSocket hijack

controls.note: External: nothing in Cline binds a remote surface to a named user, let alone with MFA. The Kanban board — the surface the vendor documents for phones and remote access — listens on 127.0.0.1:3484 without a login, and its Remote Access page says anyone with an ngrok URL can use it; CVE-2026-44211 showed any web page could drive it over WebSocket. Chat connectors admit anyone who reaches the bot unless started with a Telegram user-ID allowlist or a --hook-command script; platform identity is admission, not MFA. The dashboard's ROOM_SECRET (known from GHSA-3cj3-hqcr-g934, not the docs) is a shared secret left unset on local binds. Enterprise SSO applies the IdP's MFA to the developer's account sign-in, not to these surfaces. Put a zero-trust tunnel tied to the directory (Cloudflare Tunnel with Access, a tailnet under device posture) in front of the Kanban port and block unmanaged connectors with device management; integration points are --host / KANBAN_RUNTIME_HOST, cline connect --allowed-user-id / --hook-command and cline connect --stop. ACP is stdio from the launching editor and exposes no port.

controls.mechanism: CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS (JSON allow / deny globs and allowRedirects over shell commands, deny wins), the per-category Auto Approve toggles, PreToolUse hook scripts that cancel a call, and the Enterprise remote-config yoloModeAllowed false; remote steering admitted by cline connect --allowed-user-id or --hook-command

steps.title: Restrict shell commands by pattern
body: Set CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS in the environment that launches the editor or CLI (for example the MDM-managed login environment) to a policy such as {"allow": ["npm *", "git *"], "deny": ["rm -rf *", "sudo *"]}; deny overrides allow, commands matching no allow pattern are refused, and shell redirects are refused unless allowRedirects is true.

steps.title: Forbid YOLO mode organisation-wide
body: In the app.cline.bot remote configuration set yoloModeAllowed to false (Cline Enterprise); the YOLO toggle is disabled for every signed-in member and cannot be re-enabled in local settings.

steps.title: Add a blocking PreToolUse hook
body: Install an executable PreToolUse script in ~/Documents/Cline/Hooks (extension) or ~/.cline/hooks (CLI) and check Enable Hooks; returning {"cancel": true, "errorMessage": "..."} stops the tool call before it runs.

steps.title: Gate remote steering messages
body: Start chat connectors only with --allowed-user-id (Telegram) or a --hook-command script that returns {"action": "deny"} for every sender but the owner; without either, every message is run.

controls.note: Partial on the tier rule: Cline evaluates deterministic rules before a call for one tool class only, and none of them can be delivered where the developer cannot change it. CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS covers shell commands by glob over the command string (a script or interpreter that runs the same thing is not matched) and is an environment variable the developer can unset; Auto Approve is per-category user settings; hooks are user or workspace files behind a user toggle, and a repository can ship its own in .clinerules/hooks. The Enterprise remote configuration, applied to members signed in to the organisation, carries yoloModeAllowed and MCP server policy but no per-tool or per-argument rules. File edits, MCP tools and fetches have no rule language beyond approve or auto-approve. Remote instructions: connectors admit what --allowed-user-id or --hook-command allows and everything by default; the Kanban port admits any local client; ACP takes instructions over stdio from the editor that launched it.

controls.mechanism: PreToolUse hook scripts that can cancel a tool call whose arguments carry a secret (an attach point at user or workspace level); CLI and SDK plugin hooks.beforeModel for request mutation; the Enterprise remote-config provider base URL to send inference through an inspecting AI gateway

steps.title: Route inference through the organisation's gateway
body: In app.cline.bot under Settings → Cline Settings enable settings, choose LiteLLM (or OpenAI Compatible) as the API Provider and set its Base URL to the AI gateway that runs DLP; signed-in members cannot select another provider.

steps.title: Block tool calls that carry secrets
body: Deploy a PreToolUse hook (extension: ~/Documents/Cline/Hooks/PreToolUse; CLI: ~/.cline/hooks) that passes the tool name and parameters to the organisation's detector and returns cancel true on a hit, then check Enable Hooks.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: Cline ships no detector, but its hooks can block a tool call on an organisation-written check, and the provider base URL hands the inference path to a gateway that can inspect and mask. In the extension the documented blocking hook sees tool arguments before execution, not prompts or responses, and a cancel stops the whole task rather than masking the span; hooks are user or workspace files behind a user toggle. CLI and SDK plugins add hooks.beforeModel, which can rewrite the request, but plugins do not run in the VS Code or JetBrains extension. .clineignore is minimisation and is being deprecated — the vendor says it is not an access-control boundary. The base URL holds only for members signed in under remote configuration.

controls.mechanism: CLI -t / --timeout <seconds> (default 0, no timeout) and --retries <count> (consecutive mistakes before halting) per run; no token, turn or cost budget; token and cost counts observable in the OpenTelemetry task.tokens event

steps.title: Bound unattended CLI runs
body: Launch CLI runs from the organisation's wrapper or scheduled-job definition with --timeout and --retries so a looping run halts on time or repeated failure.

steps.title: Put the spend ceiling in the gateway
body: Pin the organisation's provider to LiteLLM (Base URL of your proxy) in remote configuration and set the per-key budgets in the proxy, since Cline itself enforces none.

controls.note: Partial: one kind of limit on one surface — the CLI's wall-clock timeout and mistake count, set per invocation by whoever launches it. The IDE extension documents no request, turn or spend cap, and neither surface has a token or cost budget or a stop for subagents, hub sessions and scheduled runs. Cline Enterprise reports usage and cost (task.tokens, the organisation metrics endpoints) but sets no limit. The ceiling is the gateway's budget behind the remote-config base URL, or the provider invoice.

controls.mechanism: Auto Approve toggles split by scope (Read / Edit project files versus all files, Execute safe versus all commands, Use the browser, Use MCP servers), Plan mode (no edits or commands), per-server MCP autoApprove and disabled, CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS for shell commands, and the Enterprise MCP policy (mcpMarketplaceEnabled, allowedMCPServers, blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers)

steps.title: Keep auto-approval inside the working tree
body: In Cline Settings → Auto Approve leave Read all files, Edit all files, Execute all commands, Use the browser and Use MCP servers off, so anything outside the workspace or beyond reads needs a click.

steps.title: Limit the MCP tool set organisation-wide
body: In remote configuration set allowedMCPServers to the approved server ids and blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers to true (Cline Enterprise).

steps.title: Restrict shell commands
body: Deliver CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS with the allow patterns the task needs; commands matching no allow pattern are refused.

controls.note: Partial on the tier rule: the workspace boundary is real but governs auto-approval, not access — a call outside the working tree still runs once the developer approves it — and every toggle is a user setting the organisation cannot lock (remote configuration reaches only YOLO and MCP servers). The extension has no per-tool deny that removes a built-in tool; toolPolicies enabled false exists only in the SDK. The decision is made by the harness outside the model, but every grant is the developer's own OS authority, and the CLI starts with --auto-approve true.

controls.mechanism: None in product: commands run in the editor's terminal or the CLI's shell as the user; CLINE_SANDBOX and --data-dir isolate only Cline's state directory; Kanban's git worktrees separate working copies, not processes

evidence.title: CLI reference (CLINE_SANDBOX, CLINE_SANDBOX_DATA_DIR)
CLI source — configureSandboxEnvironment redirects data directories only
Tools reference (bash, editor, fetch_web built-ins)

controls.note: External: Cline has no OS or container sandbox the organisation could require. CLINE_SANDBOX ("Enable sandbox mode" in the CLI reference) points Cline's data directory at $CLINE_SANDBOX_DATA_DIR or /tmp/cline-sandbox — state isolation, not execution isolation — and Kanban worktrees separate branches, not processes. Isolation comes from a VM or dev container the organisation supplies: run the extension in a VS Code Dev Container or remote workspace, or the CLI inside a container. Shell commands, stdio MCP servers, hooks and plugins otherwise run with the developer's full authority.

controls.mechanism: None that keeps credentials out of reach: reads outside the workspace need an approval unless Read all files is on, and a PreToolUse guard hook can refuse file and shell tool calls whose arguments match listed paths; a dev container or secretless credential broker is the boundary

evidence.title: .clineignore and the PreToolUse guard hook
Deprecations (.clineignore is not an access-control boundary)
Auto Approve (Read all files)

controls.note: External on the rule applied to every vendor, where only an OS-enforced scope earns partial: Cline has no sandbox and no environment scrub, so an approved command reads ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, the git credential helper, cloud CLI configuration and browser profiles as the developer. Credited contributions: the approval gate for reads outside the workspace, and the vendor's PreToolUse_ClineignoreGuard.sh, which cancels read_files, editor, apply_patch and shell calls whose path arguments match .clineignore patterns — a pattern match on arguments that a command reaching the file indirectly passes, living in user or workspace files behind a user toggle. MCP servers receive tokens from their env and headers entries; organisation headers in remoteMCPServers go only to that server's URL. Keep credentials outside the agent's filesystem with a dev container or a credential broker.

controls.mechanism: Per-rule and per-skill toggles, Enterprise remote-config globalRules / globalSkills with alwaysEnabled (source schema), Checkpoints (a shadow-Git snapshot after every tool use), edit approval for writes to rule and memory-bank files, and the Enable Hooks switch that keeps workspace hooks from running

steps.title: Keep workspace hooks from running
body: Leave Enable Hooks unchecked in Cline's feature settings unless the organisation supplies the hooks; when checked, scripts in the repository's .clinerules/hooks run as code.

steps.title: Review repository rules before they load
body: In the Rules panel toggle off workspace rules (.clinerules/, .cline/rules/, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, AGENTS.md) that did not come from a trusted author.

steps.title: Keep writes gated and revertible
body: Leave Enable Checkpoints on (the default) and Edit project files off in Auto Approve, so every write to a rule or memory-bank file is approved and can be restored.

steps.title: Push always-on organisation rules
body: On Cline Enterprise add globalRules entries with alwaysEnabled true to the remote configuration; the schema says members cannot turn them off (the field is in the source, not yet in the docs).

controls.note: Partial: the agent's writes to memory and rule files are gated by edit approval and revertible through checkpoints, and an Enterprise organisation can add always-on rules, but no instruction source can be locked out. Cline auto-loads repository rules and global ones, workspace rules win over global rules on conflict, and each is only a user toggle; the docs describe no trust prompt for a newly opened repository. Memory Bank is a convention written into a rules file, not a product memory store, so there is nothing to switch off beyond that rule. Workspace hooks execute once the developer enables hooks. Checkpoints are local snapshots, not integrity protection, and auto-approved edits skip the gate.

controls.mechanism: Extension hook scripts (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and task events) returning cancel, and CLI / SDK plugin hooks.beforeModel, as attach points for an organisation classifier; no vendor injection screening

steps.title: Enable hooks and install the organisation's scripts
body: Place the organisation's hook scripts in ~/Documents/Cline/Hooks (extension, named exactly after the event, executable) or ~/.cline/hooks (CLI) and check Enable Hooks in Cline's feature settings.

steps.title: Screen tool results in PostToolUse
body: Have the PostToolUse script send the tool result to the injection classifier and return {"cancel": true, "errorMessage": "..."} on a hit, which aborts the task before the model continues.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: Cline does no injection screening of its own, and hooks are attach points the organisation must fill. A cancel aborts the task rather than stripping the flagged block, contextModification only adds text, and the hooks are user or workspace files behind a user toggle; the PostToolUse and UserPromptSubmit event names come from the extension source, as the docs now document only PreToolUse. No documented hook covers rule files or MCP tool descriptions. CLI and SDK plugins add hooks.beforeModel, which can rewrite the request before inference. Beyond that, screening belongs to the AI gateway behind the remote-config base URL.

controls.mechanism: Provider credentials in ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json; short-lived options through a Bedrock AWS CLI profile (SSO), Vertex application default credentials, Azure identity authentication (azureIdentity) and the Cline provider's OAuth sign-in; Enterprise remote configuration pins the provider so members cannot choose another

steps.title: Pin the organisation's provider
body: In app.cline.bot remote configuration select the provider (LiteLLM, OpenAI Compatible, Bedrock, Vertex or Anthropic) and its base URL; signed-in members cannot select other providers or switch to personal Cline accounts.

steps.title: Use short-lived cloud credentials
body: For Bedrock have members select the AWS Profile option with an SSO profile (aws sso login --profile <name>) instead of an API key or IAM access keys.

controls.note: Partial: short-lived paths exist and an Enterprise organisation can pin the provider, but storage is not hardened and a pasted key cannot be forbidden. The Config page places API keys in ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json with no keychain or encryption documented (the LiteLLM member page says keys are "stored locally in VS Code"); the CLI also takes -k / --key and ACP CLINE_API_KEY. Under remote configuration members still supply their own credential for Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and keyed LiteLLM providers, and a LiteLLM Master Key set in the console is one long-lived key used by every member's client. MCP tokens sit in plain env and headers entries. The drawing's control — the key vaulted in the gateway, the developer holding a short-lived gateway token — is external, reached through the remote-config base URL.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise remote configuration mcpMarketplaceEnabled false (all locally configured servers blocked), allowedMCPServers (local servers admitted by id), remoteMCPServers pushed by URL with alwaysEnabled, and blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers; no version or hash pinning; the CLI self-updates at startup unless CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1

steps.title: Admit only organisation-defined servers
body: On Cline Enterprise set mcpMarketplaceEnabled false, list the approved servers in remoteMCPServers (name, url, headers, alwaysEnabled) and set blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers true.

steps.title: Stop the CLI updating itself
body: Set CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 in the CLI's environment so the startup check installs nothing, and install pinned versions from the organisation's package mirror.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the organisation can admit servers, but nothing pins what they serve. allowedMCPServers matches the server name in the member's own mcpServers entry, so the command behind an approved name is the developer's (the schema comment calls the id the server's GitHub URL, the docs page the local name); remote servers are admitted by URL with no version or hash, and nothing scans tool descriptions or re-approves a changed tool list. Harness integrity: the extension updates through the Marketplace or Open VSX under the editor's own auto-update and allowed-extensions policy, not a Cline key; the CLI installs updates at startup unless CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 (source only). The compromised cline@2.3.0 npm release went out through that channel; releases now carry npm OIDC provenance.

controls.mechanism: Approval prompts on every file edit and command in the IDE extension by default, the Auto Approve toggles, and the Enterprise remote-config yoloModeAllowed false; the CLI starts with --auto-approve true, ACP with approval on

steps.title: Forbid YOLO mode
body: Set yoloModeAllowed to false in the app.cline.bot remote configuration (Cline Enterprise).

steps.title: Keep writes and commands on approval
body: Leave Edit project files, Execute safe commands and Execute all commands off in Cline Settings → Auto Approve, so each edit and command shows its diff or command line for approval.

steps.title: Turn CLI auto-approval off
body: Launch the CLI with --auto-approve false (it defaults to true) from the organisation's wrapper, and leave the Auto-approve tools toggle off in ACP clients.

controls.note: Partial on the tier rule: a present developer approves each edit and command with its current arguments in the extension, but the organisation can remove only YOLO. The per-category toggles — Edit all files and Execute all commands together approximate YOLO — stay user settings, and Execute safe commands lets the model's own requires_approval flag decide (CVE-2026-52024 bypassed it). The CLI auto-approves by default and the docs do not say whether it honours yoloModeAllowed; scheduled runs, connectors (the /yolo command) and Kanban tasks run with whatever approval the launcher set. Approval is per call with no expiry or identity binding; checkpoints revert, they do not approve.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise remote configuration held at app.cline.bot: remoteMCPServers (organisation-pushed servers, alwaysEnabled), allowedMCPServers (also filters the MCP marketplace), blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers and mcpMarketplaceEnabled

steps.title: Publish the approved server set
body: List the organisation's servers in remoteMCPServers with alwaysEnabled where they must stay on, and set blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers true so no other remote server can be added.

steps.title: Restrict local servers and the marketplace
body: Set allowedMCPServers to the approved ids; unlisted local servers are blocked and unlisted marketplace entries are hidden.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the list is held in the vendor console and enforced by the client for signed-in members, not in the config file it governs, but it carries no owner, version or approval record, admits local servers by name, and covers neither CLI plugins, hooks and skills nor the agent installs themselves (the member list is the only inventory, and only of members who sign in). Nothing reconciles discovered servers against it.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise remote-config OpenTelemetry export (openTelemetryEnabled, OTLP endpoint, protocol, headers; events such as task.tool_used with auto_approved, task.mcp_tool_called, task.terminal_execution, hooks.execution and task.yolo_mode_toggled) and Prompt Storage (enterpriseTelemetry.promptUploading) syncing each task's api_conversation_history.json to the organisation's S3 or R2 bucket; CLINE_OTEL_* environment variables override the OpenTelemetry settings

steps.title: Turn on OpenTelemetry from the dashboard
body: In app.cline.bot organisation settings enable OpenTelemetry with the collector's OTLP endpoint, protocol and authentication headers, and enable logs as well as metrics.

steps.title: Upload full task transcripts
body: Under Settings → Enterprise Telemetry enable Prompt Uploading to an S3 or R2 bucket (intervalMs, batchSize, backfillEnabled) so each task's conversation, with tool inputs and outputs, reaches the organisation's store.

controls.note: Partial on the same rule as Gemini CLI: the export is admin-configured, but the OpenTelemetry override page says environment variables take priority over remote configuration, so a developer can repoint or disable it (CLINE_OTEL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED, CLINE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT). OTel events carry tool name, success and auto_approved but no arguments (terminal commands only as a hash). Prompt Storage carries the full content with no documented user opt-out, but it syncs from the local task file every 30 seconds, evicts beyond maxQueueSize and drops failed items after seven days, and the page describes only the extension's storage path. Both apply only to members signed in under remote configuration. Capture only: tamper resistance belongs to the collector and the bucket.

steps.title: Remove the member
body: In app.cline.bot open Members, choose Remove from Organization; the user loses access to the organisation immediately, and removal in the IdP revokes access at the next sign-in attempt.

body: Set mcpMarketplaceEnabled false and blockPersonalRemoteMCPServers true, and remove remoteMCPServers entries; the page says these take effect immediately for all team members.

controls.note: Partial: an Enterprise administrator can revoke organisation access and cut MCP for connected clients, but nothing documented stops a running local session. Removal withdraws organisation resources (the Cline provider, remote configuration); a session on the developer's own provider key keeps working, and whether a running task on the organisation's provider stops is not documented (delay not documented). Background work outlives the editor: hub sessions keep executing when a client disconnects and scheduled agents run with no client attached, so the stop is cline hub stop or cline connect --stop on the device, an EDR process kill, and revocation of the brokered credential at the gateway.

controls.mechanism: None in product: no domain allowlist or network sandbox; the extension follows the editor's proxy settings (VS Code proxy, JetBrains HTTP Proxy) and the CLI honours https_proxy / http_proxy and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS

evidence.title: Networking and proxies
Tools reference (bash, fetch_web)

controls.note: External: Cline cannot restrict where its tools connect. Proxy settings route Cline's own provider traffic but enforce nothing — shell commands, stdio MCP servers, the browser tool and fetch_web reach whatever the host network allows, and the CLI supports only plain HTTP proxies (no PAC or SOCKS). There is not even a documented on/off for the network tools — Use the browser in Auto Approve decides approval, not availability, and a "Cline web tools" setting appears only as a telemetry event. The remote-config provider base URL fixes where inference goes, not where tools go. The endpoint egress allowlist enforced by device management or an SSE agent is the control: admit the AI gateway, the package mirror and the named services an approved server calls.
