body: Filter the Audit Log by the Grok Bot application and stream it to your SIEM for Bot, routine, Team Setup and computer changes.

controls.note: Native on the hosted rule: an admin-enabled, server-side export off Cursor of every Bot tool call, who decided it (a person, Auto-review, a hook or no gate), its outcome and duration, correlated per turn and per tool call, plus the turn's model calls and, if opted in, prompts and final responses; it is not only control-plane audit. Boundary: by design the export never carries tool arguments or results, file paths or message bodies (shell commands are exported secret-scrubbed, browser URLs without query strings), so what a Bot read cannot be reconstructed from it; rows with client provenance are reported best-effort by the Bot's own computer, and only server-provenance rows cannot be skipped. Enterprise only; the internal store keeps 90 days and there is no backfill.

original.mechanism: Action Recording (Enterprise, off by default) plus OpenTelemetry Export tagged cursor.surface=grok_bot

steps.title: Record Bot actions
body: Turn on Action Recording on the Grok Bot page to capture Bot actions including scrubbed shell commands, then enable OpenTelemetry Export so shell, browser, tool-call and computer-use events reach your collector.

steps.title: Export the events
body: Configure Team Settings → OpenTelemetry Export; Grok Bot actions arrive as logs with no prompt content.

original.note: Action Recording captures what the Bot did on its computer; OTel export carries lifecycle and tool events. Neither is detection — the recordings and events feed a tool the organisation runs.

original.mechanism: Enterprise audit log covering Grok Bot control-plane events; SIEM streaming

steps.title: Stream Grok Bot audit events
body: Audit logs cover admin, security and authentication events plus Bot creation, member access changes, Team Setup manifests, MCP authentication, Slack account links and routines.

original.note: Control-plane events only — Bot actions are in Action Recording, not the audit log. Retention and tamper evidence are not stated; the SIEM stream is the durable record.

controls.mechanism: Bot memory persists by design with no admin switch; Team Rules and Group Rules always required; Grok Bot Computers Delete VMs and Data (organisation admins, Enterprise)

steps.title: Lock the instruction sources
body: Add Team Rules on the Grok Bot page scoped to Grok Bot; rules applied to Grok Bot are always required and members cannot turn them off.

steps.title: Wipe a member's state when needed
body: Under Grok Bot Computers → Manage → Manage selected, Delete VMs and Data removes the computer and its durable data; Terminate VMs and Recreate VMs keep the disk.

controls.note: Partial on the rule. Admins can lock instruction sources (Team Rules and Group Rules) and wipe a member's computer, but no admin setting disables or scopes Bot memory, memory writes are not validated and Auto Review does not review them, and the shared durable disk (files, browser sessions, logins) persists across sessions for every Bot the member runs. Deleting a Bot removes its profile, conversation and routines, not files or sign-ins on the computer; a shared Bot template carries identity, description, skills and routines.

original.mechanism: Per-user microVM; admin computer termination; separate user accounts for separate credentials

steps.title: Terminate a computer to reset state
body: Organisation admins can terminate any member's computer; provision separate Cursor user accounts where workloads must not share memory, files or browser sessions.

original.note: Memory persists by design and Auto-review does not evaluate memory writes; there is no validation, expiry or rollback.

controls.mechanism: Cursor account On-demand monthly limit (Spending → Monthly Limit) and Enterprise member spend limits; weekly included usage per plan; no separate Grok Bot spend cap; 50 routines per Bot

steps.title: Cap on-demand usage
body: Set Monthly Limit under Spending on cursor.com/dashboard (shown in Grok Bot as On-demand monthly limit), or turn on-demand off so Grok Bot stops when weekly usage runs out.

steps.title: Lock the setting and set member limits
body: Enable Only Admins Can Edit Usage Settings under Permissions in the Spending tab and, on Enterprise, set member or group overrides.

controls.note: Partial on the hosted rule. The only lever is the Cursor account's on-demand limit and Enterprise member limits: the teams page says a separate Grok Bot spend cap is not available, and the plans page says the limit is not a hard stop in the middle of a run (a Bot already working can finish past it). Weekly included usage and the 50-routines-per-Bot cap are vendor-fixed, and no admin-set routine frequency, action count, duration or concurrency limit is documented.

original.mechanism: Weekly usage allowances per plan; Cursor team spend limits

steps.title: Cap spend through the team
body: Grok Bot usage draws on plan allowances that reset weekly with on-demand billing beyond them; team and per-member spend limits in the Cursor dashboard bound the cost.

original.note: No limit on routine frequency, action count or task duration is documented.

controls.mechanism: Grok Bot Computers → Terminate VMs (organisation admins, Enterprise); Manage Group Access or Enable Grok Bot off (/grok-bot/disable); member removal; identity-provider session revocation

steps.title: Stop running work
body: Open Grok Bot Computers → Manage, select members, and choose Manage selected → Terminate VMs; running work stops, the operation runs on Cursor's side, and a progress card reports each member as complete, skipped or failed.

steps.title: Keep it stopped
body: Terminating does not remove access, so turn the member's group off in Manage Group Access or turn Enable Grok Bot off, remove the member from the team, and revoke their identity-provider sessions.

controls.note: Native on the hosted rule: an organisation admin (team admin rights are not enough; Enterprise only) can stop running Bots for any member, in bulk, from the vendor control plane, and the dashboard reports each stop as complete or failed. Delay: no time bound is published (members are processed in batches and large operations take a while), so the per-member result is the evidence. A terminated computer restarts on the member's next message on the same durable disk, and the enable switch and group removal block future work without saying whether they stop a running turn, so pair terminate with access removal. Stopping does not undo completed actions; grok_bot_vm and grok_bot_vm_bulk audit events record the kill.

original.mechanism: Organisation-wide switch; Manage Group Access; computer termination by admins; SCIM deprovisioning

steps.title: Stop a Bot or the whole feature
body: Terminate the member's computer from computer management, remove the group in Manage Group Access, or flip the organisation-wide switch off.

original.note: Terminating a member's computer stops active work on it; the organisation-wide switch and group removal block future work and the docs state no propagation delay, so measure it.

controls.mechanism: Firecracker microVM per member (own kernel, memory and virtual devices) shared by all of that member's Bots; durable disk across sessions; Execution on Local Computer ceiling; Recreate, Terminate and Delete VMs and Data for organisation admins

steps.title: Treat the computer as the member's boundary
body: One member cannot reach another's computer, but every Bot a member runs shares one; give a workload that needs its own computer and credential set its own Cursor user.

steps.title: Keep execution off members' machines
body: Set Execution on Local Computer to Never allow on the Grok Bot page.

steps.title: Reclaim idle computers
body: Turn on Terminate Inactive Computers under Grok Bot Computers so computers unused for 30 days are terminated.

controls.note: Partial on the hosted rule: a shared machine across sessions and agents. Isolation between members is a dedicated, hardware-separated Firecracker microVM, but it is one persistent computer per member shared by every Bot that member runs (files, browser sessions and command-line credentials are shared, and each Bot's screen is a work surface, not a boundary), and the durable disk outlives sessions (terminate and recreate keep it). Local execution runs outside the microVM on the member's own machine unless set to Never allow; delegated Cloud Agents run in their own per-agent VMs.

original.mechanism: Firecracker microVM per member with its own kernel, memory and virtual devices; all of a member's Bots share that computer; durable disk across sessions; admin termination from computer management

steps.title: Treat the computer as the member's boundary
body: One member cannot reach another member's computer, but every Bot a member runs shares one; Bots isolate personalities and workspaces, not compute, so give separate people separate accounts rather than sharing a member login.

steps.title: Terminate a computer to reset it
body: Local files, browser sessions and anything saved in the browser persist on the disk across sessions; an admin terminates the computer from the dashboard and the next session starts fresh.

original.note: Per member, not per Bot, and persistent, not ephemeral. Execution on the member's own machine (Execution on Local Computer) runs outside the microVM entirely; set it to Never allow if the boundary must hold.

controls.mechanism: Network Controls (Enterprise) with No policy, Allow all network access, Defaults plus team allowlist and Team allowlist only, domains and IP ranges with ports, directory-group policies and a lock; /grok-bot/network (egressMode, locked); Allow Local Egress

steps.title: Set Team allowlist only and lock it
body: In Network Controls on the Grok Bot page choose Team allowlist only, list the domains and IP ranges Bots need, and lock the team policy so group policies cannot replace it; running computers apply changes within about a minute.

steps.title: Keep desktop routes and networking clients inside the policy
body: Turn Allow Local Egress off unless members need Route egress through this desktop, and add a Team Setup networking client's coordination servers, relays and gateways to the allowlist.

steps.title: Manage the policy as code
body: PUT /grok-bot/network with egressMode network_settings_only and locked true.

controls.note: Native on the hosted rule: an admin-authored allowlist, lockable over directory-group policies, enforced by Cursor on all traffic from the Bot computer and applied to running computers within about a minute. Enterprise only; teams without a policy allow all destinations. Bypasses: connector calls run from Cursor's connector backend outside the computer's policy (blocking a plugin and blocking its website are separate controls), delegated Cloud Agents follow Cloud Agent network settings, and inference is outside. Traffic leaves from static ranges shared across Grok Bot customers unless routed through a member's desktop or your networking client.

original.mechanism: Network Controls (Enterprise): No policy, Allow all, Defaults plus team allowlist, Team allowlist only, with domains and IP ranges with ports; directory-group policies with a lock; private networks through desktop routing or Team Setup networking clients

steps.title: Set Team allowlist only and lock it
body: Pick Team allowlist only on the Grok Bot page, list the domains and IP ranges Bots need, and lock the policy so directory groups cannot override it; the policy applies when a computer is created or recreated.

steps.title: Keep private-network routes inside the allowlist
body: Desktop routing and Team Setup clients (Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel) give reach into private networks but do not replace the destination allowlist; add coordination servers, relays and gateways to it.

original.note: Enterprise only; teams without a policy allow all destinations. Covers all traffic from the Bot computer, which egresses through Cursor's shared static ranges unless routed through a member's desktop. Connector calls run from Cursor's backend, outside the computer's policy.

controls.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens held on Cursor's connector backend; per-Bot Secrets and the secure secret card (write-only, never shown to the Bot); Team Secrets present only in Team Setup script environments

steps.title: Route service access through connectors
body: Connect services as plugins so OAuth tokens stay on Cursor's connector backend and Bots invoke tools without receiving them; tokens are never stored on the computer.

steps.title: Enter credentials through the secure secret card
body: Save API keys with the secure secret card or a Bot's Secrets section; values are write-only and never shown to the Bot, even in Shell.

steps.title: Keep setup credentials in Team Secrets
body: Store credentials Team Setup scripts need as Team Secrets (Enterprise); they exist only in the script's environment and script output is redacted before it is logged.

controls.note: Partial on the hosted rule. Connector tokens stay outside the computer and saved secrets are never shown to the Bot, but the browser sessions and logins a member signs the Bot into live on the computer's durable disk, usable by every Bot that member runs until someone signs out or wipes the disk, and a setup script can write a Team Secret somewhere persistent. There is no repository credential: coding is delegated to Cloud Agents under their own controls. A Bot acts as its member, with no on-behalf-of exchange.

original.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens stay on Cursor's backend and are never stored on the computer; Bots invoke tools without receiving tokens; a secure secret request masks an entered value and keeps it out of the transcript

steps.title: Keep credentials off the computer
body: Connect tools through connectors so tokens stay on the backend, and enter one-off secrets through the secure secret request rather than in chat.

original.note: Covers connector tokens. The member's logged-in browser sessions on the durable disk are inside the boundary — a Bot acts with them — so web credentials are isolated only by terminating the computer. A Bot acts as its owner; there is no on-behalf-of exchange.

original.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens held on Cursor's backend, never on the computer; login, 2FA and payment handed to the member

steps.title: Rely on backend-held connector tokens
body: Bots invoke connector tools without receiving OAuth tokens and tokens are never stored on the computer; credentials typed during browser sessions are outside this model, so hand those steps to the member.

original.note: No vault or just-in-time issuance for secrets the Bot uses inside its shell or browser sessions.

controls.mechanism: Team Secrets (Enterprise; encrypted, never shown again after saving, admin-managed, up to 100 per team); write-only per-Bot Secrets; connector OAuth tokens on Cursor's backend; no vendor tunnel (the organisation's own networking client through Team Setup)

steps.title: Store fleet credentials as Team Secrets
body: Add each credential under Team Secrets on the Grok Bot page as a name and value; Cursor stores it encrypted, never shows it again, and Replace rotates it on the next script run.

steps.title: Roll a rotation out now
body: Run Recreate VMs from Grok Bot Computers so Team Setup re-runs with the rotated value instead of waiting for the periodic refresh.

steps.title: Scope the networking-client credential
body: Prefer interactive login in the computer's browser; a reusable tagged Tailscale auth key stored as a Team Secret joins every team computer under the same tags, so scope its ACLs and revoke computers from your own admin console.

controls.note: Partial on the hosted rule. Team Secrets and per-Bot secrets are encrypted and write-only, and Team Secrets are admin-scoped to setup scripts with output redaction, but a rotation reaches computers only when scripts re-run, a Team Secret spans the whole team (there are no group-level secrets), and the credentials a Bot actually uses in the browser are long-lived web sessions on the durable disk rather than short-lived issued tokens. Tunnel: Grok Bot has no vendor tunnel or connector; private reach is a member's desktop route or the organisation's own networking client installed by Team Setup, whose key is issued, rotated and revoked in that vendor's console, not Cursor's. Team Secrets are dashboard-only (not in the Admin API).

tools.name: GitHub Copilot Chat on github.com

variants.name: Copilot Chat on github.com (immersive and panel)
Copilot Chat in GitHub Mobile
Copilot Spaces (curated context, organisation-owned or personal)

summary: Copilot Chat on github.com and Mobile answers over repositories, issues and PRs the user can see, attaches images and PDFs, searches the web when the policy allows, and calls a fixed GitHub MCP server to do a limited set of tasks (branches, merges) on request; a chat can hand off into a cloud agent session. Spaces bundle repositories, files, issues and uploads as reusable context.

Inference runs on the Copilot API with enterprise-enabled models; retrieval runs with the user's own permissions (viewers of a Space only see sources they can access). Conversations are stored by GitHub: today 100 conversations with 28-day message retention, moving to life-of-account no earlier than 2026-09-28 when chat, Mobile chat and the cloud agent merge under one policy. Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training.

Admin levers are the "Copilot in GitHub.com" policy (soon the unified policy), the web search and models policies, content exclusion, and, for Enterprise Managed Users, the enterprise access-restriction header. Spaces have no dedicated policy on the pages fetched; the MCP and Memory policies do not apply to Chat in GitHub.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All plans; Business and Enterprise gate it with Copilot in GitHub.com and, no earlier than 2026-09-28, a single policy (set under "Copilot cloud agent (coming soon)") shared with Mobile chat and the cloud agent.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API; models selectable per conversation within the enterprise Configure models policy; enterprise BYOK custom models appear in Chat; data-resident routing under the data residency policy.

facts.label: Data leaving the browser
facts.value: Prompts, attached files, repository context and (when enabled) web search results to the Copilot API; nothing runs on the device.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Up to 100 recent conversations, messages kept 28 days — changing to retention for the life of the account no earlier than 2026-09-28; Business and Enterprise data is not used for training.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Copilot Chat concepts and Spaces.

items.title: Policies that reach chat on github.com
body: Copilot in GitHub.com (feature toggle; opt-in preview features and feedback collection hang off it), Copilot can search the web, Configure models and Configure custom models, content exclusion — all honoured by Chat in GitHub per the supported-surfaces table. MCP servers in Copilot, the registry restriction and Copilot Memory are not: chat's GitHub MCP server is fixed, and Memory is used by the cloud agent, code review, the CLI and agentic autofix. Across a user's organisations the least restrictive setting wins for most policies, including web search and Copilot in GitHub.com; public-code matching is among the exceptions that follow the most restrictive.

items.title: The unified Copilot experience (no earlier than 2026-09-28)
body: GitHub relaunches Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in GitHub Mobile and the cloud agent as one experience under one policy, set under "Copilot cloud agent (coming soon)" in Copilot settings; chat retention becomes life-of-account, and administrators who opt out lose Copilot on github.com and Mobile for their users.

links.title: Upcoming changes to Copilot policies and billing

riskNotes.note: CamoLeak (2025) turned hidden PR-description comments into silent exfiltration through GitHub's own Camo image proxy; the fix was to stop rendering images in chat. Chat still reads every issue and PR the user can see, and can now act through the GitHub MCP server.
Retention moves from 28 days to life-of-account no earlier than 2026-09-28; Spaces accept uploads and free text that are then shareable to organisation members or publicly.
Web search and image/PDF attachments widen the inference input beyond repository data; both are policy-controlled (web search) or user-controlled (attachments) rather than inspected.

Spaces and the repositories themselves are the retrieval stores (a repository is indexed automatically once a chat has its context); anyone with editor access to an organisation Space, or push access to a repository, can shape what the model reads.

controls.mechanism: GitHub's own second-factor requirement (Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security > "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations", optionally "Only allow secure two-factor methods"); with Enterprise Managed Users the IdP's MFA instead (OIDC with Entra ID Conditional Access)

steps.title: Require two-factor authentication for every organization
body: Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security: select "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations" and "Only allow secure two-factor methods" (passkeys, security keys, authenticator apps, GitHub Mobile); members without it cannot reach organization resources until they enable it.

steps.title: With Enterprise Managed Users, put MFA in Entra ID
body: The 2FA policy is not available to managed users; use OIDC SSO so GitHub applies the Entra ID Conditional Access Policy, knowing GitHub enforces its IP conditions but MFA only at IdP sign-in.

controls.note: Native by the D3-MFA rule applied to every vendor on this drawing: GitHub's identity layer requires a second factor for every organization member, enforced server-side, and the same account signs in to Chat on github.com and GitHub Mobile. Boundary: the requirement covers organization members, billing managers and outside collaborators; the page does not say whether it binds a user licensed directly by the enterprise (user or enterprise-team assignment) who belongs to no organization. It is unavailable under Enterprise Managed Users, where MFA is the IdP's and, per GitHub, enforced only at IdP sign-in (CAP IP conditions are re-checked on web use and token authentication, web-session protection in preview; device compliance is not enforced). What skips a fresh second factor: a signed-in session — SAML SSO re-authentication is every 24 hours unless the IdP sets otherwise, and the GitHub Mobile session lifetime is not documented on the pages fetched. A personal account is not an organization member, so personal-plan Copilot is outside the requirement; keeping people in the corporate account is the D3-OTF header's job.

original.mechanism: Copilot seat assignment (enterprise teams, IdP-synced under EMU), Copilot in GitHub.com policy, SAML SSO

steps.title: Assign seats and enable the feature
body: Grant licences from Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot (users, enterprise teams or organisations); enable Copilot in GitHub.com under AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients.

steps.title: Confirm the unified policy before 2026-09-28
body: Review the single policy replacing Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in Mobile and the cloud agent; opting out removes chat on github.com and Mobile.

controls.mechanism: Copilot licences by user, enterprise team (IdP-synced under Enterprise Managed Users) or organization; enterprise Copilot policies set once or delegated to organizations (AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients); no connector apps of its own — OAuth app access restrictions and GitHub App installation are GitHub's target-tenant path for other products' GitHub connectors

steps.title: Assign licences by group
body: Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot > Manage > Enterprise Teams > Assign licenses; with Enterprise Managed Users sync the team to an IdP group so joining or leaving the group grants or removes Copilot.

steps.title: Set feature policies at enterprise level
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients: enable or disable each policy for the enterprise instead of letting organizations decide, because a user seated by several organizations gets the least restrictive setting.

steps.title: As the target tenant, gate other vendors' GitHub connectors
body: Keep OAuth app access restrictions enabled on each organization (the default for new organizations) and approve OAuth apps and GitHub App installations one by one, which decides whether another chat product's GitHub connector can reach organization data.

controls.note: Partial by the D3-APA rule on this drawing: GitHub administers group-based authorization over the chat feature (licences by user, enterprise team or organization; policies per enterprise or delegated per organization, enforced server-side), but Chat on github.com has no connector apps whose consent a target tenant grants — its one connector is GitHub's own MCP server acting within the user's permissions — and inside the product authorization is feature on/off per organization, not per group or per tool. The consent path GitHub does document runs the other way: as the target tenant for other vendors' GitHub connectors (OAuth app access restrictions, bypassed by privileged OAuth apps; GitHub App installation with selected repositories; fine-grained token approval) — the other products' control seen from their side. No documented setting lets an organization refuse Chat on github.com to someone licensed elsewhere who can read its repositories. Policy configuration is not the runtime decision; the decision is GitHub's server-side check of licence and policy on each request.

original.mechanism: Copilot seat assignment (enterprise teams, IdP-synced under EMU), Copilot in GitHub.com policy, SAML SSO

steps.title: Assign seats and enable the feature
body: Grant licences from Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot (users, enterprise teams or organisations); enable Copilot in GitHub.com under AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients.

steps.title: Confirm the unified policy before 2026-09-28
body: Review the single policy replacing Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in Mobile and the cloud agent; opting out removes chat on github.com and Mobile.

original.mechanism: Retrieval runs as the user; Space viewers only see sources they have access to; no remediation of over-shared repositories

steps.title: Rely on repository permissions and Space visibility
body: Organisation-owned Spaces grant admin / editor / viewer or No access; viewers only see sources they can already access — fix repository over-sharing first.

original.note: Delegated: retrieval carries the user's own repository permissions, so an over-shared repository is retrievable by everyone who can already see it; nothing here narrows scope below the user's entitlements.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise access restrictions: the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header, injected by the organisation's break-and-inspect proxy on github.com, api.github.com and *.githubcopilot.com, makes GitHub refuse accounts outside the enterprise (Enterprise Managed Users only); Copilot subscription-based network routing by plan endpoint; the web-search policy for GitHub's own egress

steps.title: Enable enterprise access restrictions
body: Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security > Enterprise access restrictions: select "Enable enterprise access restrictions" and copy the header value shown for the enterprise.

steps.title: Inject the header at the proxy
body: Have the TLS-inspecting proxy overwrite sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise: ENTERPRISE-ID (up to 20 IDs) on all traffic to github.com/*, api.github.com/* and *.githubcopilot.com; other accounts get a 403 and the audit log records business.proxy_security_header_unsatisfied.

steps.title: Route Copilot by plan
body: Allow *.business.githubcopilot.com and/or *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com and block *.individual.githubcopilot.com; GitHub lists Copilot Chat on GitHub and GitHub Mobile among the features this routing affects.

steps.title: Turn web search off where exfiltration risk matters
body: Set Copilot can search the web to disabled at enterprise level; it applies to Chat in GitHub, and across a user's organizations the least restrictive setting wins.

controls.note: Partial by the D3-OTF rule on this drawing: GitHub honours a documented tenant-restriction header that the organisation's proxy injects and enforces the block server-side (web sign-in, API and OAuth or GitHub App tokens, Copilot endpoints); the organisation's SSE does the injection. Boundary: Enterprise Managed Users only (data-residency enterprises are already separated by their GHE.com subdomain); it needs a break-and-inspect proxy on every path, so devices off the proxy are not covered. Enterprises with personal accounts have no header, only the plan-based endpoint routing, which blocks personal Copilot plans but not a personal GitHub account. A customer proxy does not control GitHub's own egress: web search queries go to Bing from GitHub's side, and a cloud agent session started from chat egresses from GitHub-hosted runners under its own firewall (toolCopilotCloudAgent); keeping web search off is the only chat-side lever.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; github.com chat traffic is ordinary HTTPS to github.com
original.note: An SSE or CASB can only see the browser session; the model traffic originates from GitHub's side. Tenancy enforcement must rely on SSO and seat assignment.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

original.mechanism: Web-search policy; image rendering disabled in chat (post-CamoLeak); GitHub MCP server limited to a fixed task set
original.note: The model's reach is GitHub data plus web search; there is no domain allowlist for chat, and the vendor's remaining lever is to keep web search off.

steps.title: Turn web search off where exfiltration risk matters
body: Disable Copilot can search the web; it applies to IDEs and Chat in GitHub.

controls.mechanism: No content inspection in the product; content exclusion (path filter) and the web-search policy are data minimisation; an SSE or browser security product inspecting the github.com and *.githubcopilot.com session is the integration point

evidence.title: Content exclusion for GitHub Copilot (website and Mobile support, public preview)
Asking Copilot questions in GitHub (attachments on by default, no policy)
Copilot network routing (plan endpoints an SSE can see)
Audit log events for agents (Copilot API usage records, EMU and data residency, preview)

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor on this drawing: GitHub detects nothing in chat prompts, attachments, Space uploads or answers, offers no inline hook, and applies no sensitivity labels. Content exclusion (Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion; public preview on the website and Mobile) keeps named paths out of Copilot's context, and the web-search policy limits what leaves in search queries — path and feature minimisation, not detection. Image and PDF attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC, HEIF) are on for every plan with no policy to turn them off. Integration point: an SSE or browser security product that TLS-inspects the github.com and *.githubcopilot.com session and blocks pastes and uploads before they leave. Copilot Usage Records (request and response bodies, Enterprise Managed Users and data-residency enterprises, preview) would allow detection after the fact, but its documented client list does not name Chat on github.com.

original.mechanism: Content exclusion (honoured by Chat on GitHub and Mobile) and the web-search policy; no inspection of prompts or uploads

steps.title: Exclude sensitive paths at enterprise scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion: fnmatch patterns per repository or "*" — applied to chat on the GitHub website and Mobile, not to third-party agents.

steps.title: Decide on web search
body: Set Copilot can search the web at enterprise level; across a user's organisations it resolves to the least restrictive organisation setting, so an enterprise-level lockdown is the only way to guarantee it is off.

original.note: Content exclusion is a context filter on what the model may read; nothing inspects the prompt, the uploads or the answer for sensitive content.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; paste and upload controls belong to a browser security product
original.note: Chat accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC and HEIF attachments; only a browser control can stop uploads of classified documents.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: No documented screening of the content Chat on github.com reads; GitHub-side content filters on prompts and outputs cover harmful content, and image rendering was disabled after CamoLeak

evidence.title: Application card — Copilot Chat (content filtering; context sources on GitHub.com)
Risks and mitigations (hidden-character filtering is for the cloud agent)
CamoLeak write-up (image rendering disabled in Copilot Chat, 2025-08-14)

controls.note: None by the input-screening rule on this drawing: GitHub documents no injection screening of the repository files, issues, pull requests, Space sources, attachments or web results that Chat on github.com reads, nothing an administrator can switch on or tune, and no event. What exists is adjacent: prompts and outputs pass GitHub's content filters for harmful, offensive or off-topic content (a harm filter, not injection classification); hidden characters and HTML comments are filtered only before input reaches the Copilot cloud agent; and disabling image rendering in chat on 2025-08-14 closed the CamoLeak exfiltration channel on the output side. No product class can sit on GitHub's internal retrieval path. What stands in: web search off, the Allow confirmation and rulesets for writes, and GitHub's defences questioned in the vendor assessment.

original.mechanism: Vendor-side mitigations (image rendering disabled after CamoLeak; hidden-character filtering for agent hand-offs); no customer configuration

steps.title: Know what the vendor changed
body: Image rendering in Copilot Chat was disabled on 2025-08-14 to close the Camo exfiltration channel; hidden HTML comments in issues and PRs are filtered before agent prompts.

original.note: Vendor-operated mitigations on specific input paths (rendered images, hidden characters in hand-offs); nothing the customer can tune, and repository content the chat reads is not classified.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot CLI

variants.name: Copilot CLI (GA 2026-02-25)
GitHub Copilot app (desktop, GA 2026-06-17; same managed-settings plane, own policy since 2026-07-27)
Copilot in Windows Terminal (Canary; governed by the Copilot CLI policy)

summary: Copilot CLI is the terminal-native coding agent (plan mode, autopilot, built-in Explore / Task / Code Review / Plan agents, /fleet parallel sessions, hooks, plugins, MCP) and the runtime behind the GitHub Copilot desktop app, the SDK and JetBrains agent mode. It runs on the developer's machine with the developer's GitHub identity; inference goes to the Copilot API by plan, or straight to a provider under local BYOK.

Prompts, file contents and tool output leave the device for the Copilot API; session data (prompts, responses, tools, files changed) is written to ~/.copilot/session-state and synced to the user's GitHub account only where the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy is at least "View from cloud" (unconfigured keeps it local for Business and Enterprise seats). Remote steering exposes the session to github.com and GitHub Mobile. Nothing reaches the organisation's audit log except policy changes.

The admin plane is managed-settings.json: server-managed from the .github-private repository (copilot/managed-settings.json, with team overrides), MDM (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot, com.github.copilot) or a root-owned file. It carries deny / ask / allow permissions with Shell, Read, Edit and Domain selectors (GA 2026-09-09), disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, plugin marketplaces, the MXC local sandbox policy, OpenTelemetry export and remote-control mode.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise gate it with the Copilot CLI policy (Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Clients), and the desktop app with its own GitHub Copilot app policy.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API per plan; enterprise-enabled models only; local BYOK (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Ollama) bypasses GitHub; enterprise BYOK models are served by the Copilot API.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts and tool output to the Copilot API; session data synced to the GitHub account only where the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy allows it and remoteExport is not false; OTLP telemetry only where the enterprise configures it; remote-steering traffic to github.com.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training; model providers run under ZDR except Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 (retain by default, exemption available through end-2026).

facts.label: Sandboxes
facts.value: Local sandbox uses Microsoft eXecution Container (MXC: Seatbelt on macOS 15+, bubblewrap on Linux, BaseContainer on Windows 11); cloud sandbox runs on Azure Container Apps Sandboxes behind the Cloud sandbox access policy (off by default). Both public preview.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Copilot CLI how-tos (install, authenticate, allowing tools, hooks, MCP, plugins, administer for your enterprise).

items.title: Managed settings — delivery and precedence
body: Server-managed: an organisation in the enterprise hosts .github-private with copilot/managed-settings.json (legacy .github/copilot/settings.json still read); copilot/team-mappings.json and copilot/teams/*.json let named teams relax keys the enterprise marks { "overridable": ... }. Clients refresh within about an hour, or on restart. MDM and local-file delivery exist for machines that must not depend on the server channel; the CLI falls back to its cached copy when a fetch fails.

Keys the CLI honours: permissions.deny / ask / allow, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, model, enabledPlugins / extraKnownMarketplaces / strictKnownMarketplaces, allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, telemetry.*, remoteControl and sandbox.* — sandbox applies to the CLI and the app (not VS Code), the app ignores telemetry, the cloud agent honours only model and plugin keys.

items.title: Permission model and its escape hatches
body: Read-only operations run without asking; edits, destructive shell commands and URL fetches prompt. Per-repo approvals persist in ~/.copilot/permissions-config.json and allowed URLs in ~/.copilot/settings.json. --allow-all / --yolo, /allow-all, --allow-all-tools and autopilot remove the prompts; deny rules still win. The managed file removes these options with disableBypassPermissionsMode and pins its own deny / ask / allow.

Policy hooks — root-owned, machine-wide, immune to disableAllHooks — run preToolUse (fail-closed on error, fail-open on timeout) and permissionRequest with a permissionDecision of allow, deny or ask; HTTP hooks for those events must be https.

items.title: Local sandbox policy
body: Deny-by-default filesystem: read/write, read-only and denied paths, with automatic grants for the working directory, PATH toolchains and package caches that managed settings can switch off (addCurrentWorkingDirectory, allowDevToolAccess). Network allowOutbound / allowLocalNetwork and an HTTP proxy; auth.git / auth.gh credential injection (formerly gitAuth / ghAuth) and macOS keychainAccess are separate switches. Managed values combine in the most restrictive direction; built-in file tools are software-checked only and remote MCP servers are outside the policy.

links.title: Understanding filesystem policies for local sandboxing

riskNotes.note: Autopilot and --yolo exist by design; CVE-2026-29783 showed the read-only classifier itself could be tricked by bash parameter expansion. disableBypassPermissionsMode plus a managed sandbox is the only configuration where a bad tool call is contained rather than merely prompted.

Repository files, MCP responses and hook output all feed the agent; the vendor's fix for CVE-2026-29783 added parse-time blocking and prompt hardening but no classifier. Domain() deny rules and sandbox allowOutbound=false bound the exfiltration path.

Session transcripts sync to github.com wherever the policy allows it and remote steering publishes them to the agents list; OTLP captureContent can also carry prompts. Decide the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy and lockCaptureContent explicitly.

Plugins and MCP servers install by name from marketplaces and npx commands; only strictKnownMarketplaces and the managed allowlist (URL and stdio command match) bound the sources — the registry restriction is name-only and bypassable.

controls.mechanism: GitHub's own second-factor requirement (Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security > "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations", optionally "Only allow secure two-factor methods") plus the device-delivered managed key forceLoginOrgs, which pins the CLI to the organization's accounts and refuses personal accounts and BYOK/API-key sign-in

steps.title: Require two-factor authentication for every organization
body: Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security: select "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations" and "Only allow secure two-factor methods"; members without 2FA cannot reach organization resources until they enable it. Not available to Enterprise Managed Users, whose second factor is the IdP's.

steps.title: Pin the CLI to your organizations
body: Deliver forceLoginOrgs (an array of organization logins) through MDM (com.github.copilot plist, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot) or a root-owned managed-settings.json: Copilot then runs only for an account in a listed organization, refuses personal accounts, other enterprises and BYOK/API-key authentication, and fails closed if the policy cannot be read.

steps.title: Bound the tokens that skip the second factor
body: Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens: set "Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens", require approval of fine-grained tokens and restrict classic tokens.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: GitHub's identity layer requires a second factor for every organization member and forceLoginOrgs pins the client to the organization account (MDM or file channel only — the server-managed channel reaches only accounts already signed in, so unmanaged devices are not pinned). With Enterprise Managed Users the 2FA policy is unavailable: MFA is the IdP's and, per GitHub, enforced only at IdP sign-in. Non-interactive paths that skip the second factor once issued: the OAuth token (gho_) kept in the OS keychain, whose lifetime "depend[s] on how the token was created"; fine-grained PATs with the Copilot Requests account permission and GitHub App user tokens (ghu_) read from COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN; and the gh CLI token fallback. forceLoginOrgs still requires those accounts to belong to a listed organization; whether the PAT lifetime and restriction policies govern the Copilot Requests permission is not documented.

original.mechanism: Copilot seat plus the Copilot CLI policy (and the separate GitHub Copilot app policy); OAuth device/browser flow or a fine-grained PAT with the Copilot Requests permission; SAML SSO authorisation per organisation

steps.title: Enable the CLI for the right organisations
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Clients: set Copilot CLI to Enabled everywhere, Disabled everywhere or Let organizations decide; users still need an assigned seat.

steps.title: Set the desktop app policy separately
body: Since 2026-07-27 the GitHub Copilot app has its own policy under AI Controls > Copilot Clients (default Enabled everywhere); it no longer follows the CLI policy.

steps.title: Constrain how the CLI authenticates
body: OAuth tokens (gho_) and fine-grained PATs (github_pat_, Copilot Requests permission) are accepted; classic PATs are not. Tokens live in the OS keychain with a plaintext fallback at ~/.copilot/config.json; SSO-protected organisations require Authorize at login.

controls.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow with Shell(), Read(), Edit() / Write() and Domain() selectors; root-owned policy hooks (preToolUse, permissionRequest) in /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/ or HKLM\Software\Policies\GitHub\Copilot

steps.title: Write the managed permission rules
body: Under permissions set deny (blocks from any source), ask (fresh approval every time; bypass, auto-approval, hooks and saved grants cannot satisfy it) and allow (intersection across sources) with Shell(...), Read(...), Edit(...) and Domain(...) selectors; any managed rule makes unmatched operations default to ask.

steps.title: Add a machine-wide policy hook
body: Deploy a root-owned JSON file in /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/ (Windows C:\ProgramData\GitHub\Copilot\policy.d\ or HKLM\Software\Policies\GitHub\Copilot) whose preToolUse hook returns permissionDecision "deny"; errors and exit code 2 deny, timeouts fail open, and disableAllHooks cannot switch policy hooks off.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: admin-delivered, user-proof deny/ask/allow rules over shell commands (including redirection and sed -i writes), file paths and network domains are evaluated before each call, and an admin-locked pre-tool hook can deny any tool, MCP tools included (managed selectors do not name MCP tools). The hook is an integration point whose logic the organisation writes: command hooks fail closed on error but open on timeout, and HTTP preToolUse hooks fail open on any error, so set timeoutSec and prefer command hooks. Remote MCP servers' own actions are outside both; decisions reach telemetry only as hook span events.

original.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow with Shell(), Read(), Edit(), Domain() selectors (GA 2026-09-09); root-owned policy hooks on preToolUse / permissionRequest

steps.title: Write the managed permission rules
body: Under permissions set deny (blocked from any source), ask (fresh approval every time, bypass cannot satisfy) and allow (intersection across sources) with Shell(...) / Bash(...) / PowerShell(...), Read(path), Edit(path) / Write(path) and Domain(host) selectors; mark team-relaxable keys { "overridable": ... }.

steps.title: Keep secret files out of context
body: Enterprise, organization and repository content-exclusion rules apply to the CLI ("Excluded files are not used as context").

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the CLI detects no secrets or PII in prompts or tool traffic itself. It masks two named token values and, per session, variables the user names with --secret-env-vars (a flag, not a managed key), and its policy hooks are an inline attach point that can block or rewrite traffic once the organisation attaches a detector (userPromptSubmitted config-file hooks cannot change the prompt; userPromptTransformed can). Content exclusion and managed Read(...) denies are path filtering, credited as data minimisation; the model still sees whatever the developer pastes. Local BYOK sends prompts straight to the configured provider.

The CLI's command safety analysis and the parse-time blocking added for CVE-2026-29783 judge proposed shell commands — action policy, not input screening — and web_fetch SSRF protection limits destinations, not content. Folder trust and MCP server trust levels are admission. An AI or MCP gateway classifier on the brokered path is the external complement.

A command already started runs to completion, BYOK sessions do not touch the Copilot API (forceLoginOrgs keeps them off managed devices), and remote "End the current operation" is the session owner's control, not an admin's. EDR process kill is the external complement.

summary: The cloud agent takes an issue, PR comment, chat hand-off or automation trigger and works in an ephemeral GitHub Actions environment (59-minute hard limit) on a copilot/ branch, pushing a draft PR that a human must review and merge. Code review, partner agents (Claude, Codex), agent apps and Agentic Workflows run on the same Actions substrate and share its mitigations; automations re-run the agent on schedules and repository events.

Inference runs on the Copilot API against enterprise-enabled models; the runner talks to api.<plan>.githubcopilot.com behind an egress firewall that, by default, allows package registries and certificate authorities only. The GitHub MCP server is wired in with a read-only token scoped to the repository; other MCP servers run with whatever secrets the administrator places in the Agents secret type — and are used without approval prompts.

Governance is enterprise-first: AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent with Enabled for selected organisations (custom properties via REST), organisation and repository access controls, Actions workflow approval, validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency review, Copilot review), runner type and the firewall. Sessions are visible at github.com/copilot/agents and in the audit log as actor:Copilot with agent_session_id.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All paid Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise require the cloud agent policy. Billing is GitHub Actions minutes plus AI credits; user-level budgets always hard-stop, organisation and enterprise budgets block only with "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" (off by default).

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API from the Actions runner (api.business / api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com); models per the enterprise Configure models policy; data-resident routing under the "Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models" policy (+10% credits). Enterprise BYOK does not apply to the cloud agent.

facts.label: Data leaving the environment
facts.value: Repository contents, issue and PR text and tool output go to the Copilot API; outbound network from Bash tools is firewalled; MCP servers and copilot-setup-steps are not firewalled; session logs and commits persist on GitHub.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Ephemeral environment destroyed after the session; each agent commit links permanently to its session logs (application card). GitHub does not use Copilot Business or Enterprise customer data to train AI models; provider terms are per model on the model-hosting page (OpenAI and xAI zero retention, Anthropic per its ZDR documentation, Google no training).

facts.label: Policy change 2026-09-28
facts.value: Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in GitHub Mobile and the cloud agent merge under one policy on or after 2026-09-28; chat retention moves from 28 days to the life of the account. Admins must confirm the unified policy before that date.
