items.title: Enablement, targeting and repository scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent: Disabled (default), Enabled for all organizations, Enabled for selected organizations (UI, or by custom property through the REST API), or let organisations decide. Organisation owners then set Repository access (all or selected repositories); owners and users can opt individual repositories out. Only users with write access can trigger the agent, and automations ignore events from users without write access by default.

Third-party agents and agent apps are separate policies: disabling the cloud agent does not disable Claude or Codex agents, and the "Agent apps" policy gates partner apps installed in the enterprise's organisations. Content exclusion does not apply to third-party agents.

links.title: Enabling the cloud agent in your enterprise
Managing access to the cloud agent

items.title: The environment — setup steps, secrets, runners, firewall
body: .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml on the default branch (job name copilot-setup-steps; only steps, permissions, runs-on, services, snapshot and timeout-minutes are honoured; 59 minutes maximum) prepares the runner. Secrets and variables come only from the Agents type (repository or organisation Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents); COPILOT_MCP_* entries reach MCP servers only; Actions, Codespaces and Dependabot secrets are never exposed.

The firewall is on by default with a recommended allowlist (OS and language package registries, container registries, certificate authorities, Playwright browser hosts); organisations and repositories add domain or URL rules or disable it. It applies only to processes the agent starts through its Bash tools — not MCP servers, not setup steps. Blocked requests are reported in the PR body or a comment. Runners default to a standard GitHub-hosted runner; organisation owners can set a Runner type and stop repositories overriding it. Larger and self-hosted runners (Ubuntu x64 or Windows 64-bit; ephemeral single-use self-hosted runners recommended) need uploads.github.com, user-images.githubusercontent.com and api.<plan>.githubcopilot.com, and the firewall must be disabled on self-hosted runners.

links.title: Configure secrets and variables for the cloud agent
Configuring runners for the cloud agent in your organization

items.title: Output controls — workflow approval, validation, code review approvals
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent: Validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency advisories, Copilot code review; on by default) and Actions workflow approval (Require approval for workflow runs; keep it on — the docs warn about auto-running workflows on agent code). The agent cannot mark a PR ready, approve or merge; rulesets add one more approval when the PR is opened under the agent's app identity, and the requesting user cannot approve their own request.

Copilot code review can be authorised to approve PRs (public preview): enterprise "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" is Disabled everywhere by default, organisations choose whether approvals count toward merge requirements, repositories can limit that to file-path globs.

links.title: Configuring settings for the cloud agent

riskNotes.note: Every trigger is attacker-reachable text (issues, PR bodies, comments, repository files). GitHub strips hidden characters and HTML comments before prompting and ignores non-write-access events for automations, but MCP tools run without approval, so an injection that reaches a write-capable MCP tool acts immediately.

The firewall covers only Bash-spawned processes; MCP servers and copilot-setup-steps have unrestricted egress, and Agents secrets are plain environment variables inside the runner. Put nothing in the Agents secret type that a compromised MCP server should not see.

Automations act under their creator's identity and cannot approve the resulting PRs; partner agents install as GitHub Apps (anthropic code agent, openai code agent) with their own permissions. Rulesets and the extra-approval rule are the boundary, not the agent.
Cloud agent, third-party agents and agent apps are three independent policies; a "disabled" cloud agent still leaves Claude, Codex and any installed agent app enabled unless each is switched off.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent policy (REST policy_state enabled_for_all_orgs, disabled_for_all_orgs, enabled_for_selected_orgs, configured_by_org_admins) and the "Block Copilot cloud agent in all repositories" toggle; organisation Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent > Repository access, Allow automations, Runner type and Partner agents; trigger fixed by GitHub to users with write access

steps.title: Choose which organisations get the cloud agent
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent: select Enabled for selected organizations and pick them in the UI, or by a one-time custom-property match through the REST API, rather than enabling everywhere.

steps.title: Scope repositories and automations in each organisation
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent: set Repository access to Selected repositories, and turn the Allow automations toggle off unless automations have an owner and a reviewed tool set.

steps.title: Lock where sessions run
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent > Runner type: choose the runner, then turn off Allow repositories to customize the runner type so copilot-setup-steps.yml cannot move sessions to other runners.

steps.title: Switch partner agents separately
body: On the same Cloud agent page, the Partner agents toggles enable Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex; agent apps are governed by the separate enterprise "agent apps" policy. Disabling the cloud agent does not disable either.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted D3-APA rule. Enablement is administrable per organisation, repository and licensed user, and the runner, firewall (see egress) and partner-agent switches are admin-controlled, all enforced by GitHub server-side. But the trigger condition is fixed by GitHub, not configured: only users with write access can trigger or steer a session, comments from anyone else are never presented to the agent, and Slack guests and outside collaborators cannot start sessions. Two widening switches sit below the administrator: an automation's creator can opt in to events from users without write access, and a repository administrator can turn off Require approval for workflow runs. Custom-property selection of organisations is evaluated once and not kept in sync. Copilot Pro, Pro+ and Max users have the agent on by default; in enterprise repositories only the Block toggle covers them.

original.mechanism: Enterprise policy Enabled for selected organizations (UI or custom properties via REST), organisation Repository access, per-repository opt-out; write access required to trigger

steps.title: Enable for selected organisations
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent: choose Enabled for selected organizations and pick organisations, or select them by custom property with the REST API.

steps.title: Scope repositories
body: Organisation owners set Repository access to all or selected repositories; repository owners can opt out. Only users with write access can trigger the agent.

controls.mechanism: Commits authored by Copilot and signed ("Verified") with the requester as co-author; audit events actor:Copilot with actor_is_agent and agent_session_id; pull requests attributed to the requesting person, or to Copilot's app identity from shared Slack or Teams contexts; automations attributed to their creator; partner agents act through the "anthropic code agent" and "openai code agent" GitHub Apps

steps.title: Attribute agent actions in the audit log
body: Enterprise Settings > Audit log: search actor:Copilot for agent activity (180 days on GitHub) and action:copilot for policy and configuration changes.

steps.title: Tie each event to a session and a person
body: Agentic events carry actor_is_agent=true, agent_session_id and the user who initiated the session; use them to separate agent actions from the person's own.

steps.title: Keep the extra approval for app-identity pull requests
body: In branch rulesets leave "Require an additional approval for unattributed Copilot pull requests" on (the default), so a pull request Copilot opens under its own app identity needs one more human approval.

steps.title: Inventory partner-agent apps from the policy, not the installations list
body: Allow Claude coding agent installs "anthropic code agent" and Allow Codex coding agent installs "openai code agent"; their actions are in the audit log but the apps do not appear in the installations list.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted D3-AA rule. The agent has a distinct actor for commits and audit events, but it is GitHub's identity, not an installation or service account the organisation inventories or revokes on its own. Its authority derives from the initiating user (write access to the repository; the agent tasks API accepts only user-to-server tokens), its pull requests are attributed to that person except in shared Slack or Teams contexts, and stopping it means disabling the policy, opting the repository out or removing the user's access — there is no per-agent credential to revoke. The GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN set in each job's sandbox are GitHub-issued; their lifetime is not documented. Partner-agent apps are installed by a policy toggle and are hidden from the organisation's app installations list.

original.mechanism: The agent acts under its own app identity with signed ("Verified") commits, co-authored by the requesting human; audit events carry actor_is_agent and agent_session_id; partner agents install as named GitHub Apps
original.note: The identity is GitHub's, not the customer's: there is no key custody or lifecycle to manage, only the app installations of partner agents and agent apps to review. Compared with Claude Tag: the organisation owns Tag's per-tool service accounts and their lifecycle; here GitHub owns the app identity, so the organisation manages only which installations are permitted. PR and commit actions carry the agent's app identity; workflow runs carry the repository's Actions token.

steps.title: Review partner-agent app installations
body: Enabling Claude or Codex agents installs the "anthropic code agent" / "openai code agent" GitHub Apps; their actions appear in the audit log — review installations under third-party access.

steps.title: Attribute agent actions in the audit log
body: Filter actor:Copilot; agentic events carry actor_is_agent=true, agent_session_id and the initiating user.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom agents in a designated .github-private governance repository (AI controls > Agents, "Protect agent files using rulesets", AI managers); AI controls agent sessions list (last 24 hours, filterable); the organisation Allow automations switch; repository configuration readable over REST; automations are private to their creator

steps.title: Publish approved agents from one governance repository
body: Create a .github-private repository, select it as the enterprise's source of governance, keep agent profiles under /agents/, and in AI controls > Agents use "Protect agent files using rulesets" > Create ruleset.

steps.title: Review what ran
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agent sessions > View all lists sessions from the last 24 hours; filter by agent, organization, repository, status, timeframe and user.

steps.title: Decide on automations as a class
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent > Allow automations: an automation is visible only to the user who created it, so leave it off where the organisation needs an inventory with owners.

steps.title: Reconcile repository agent configuration
body: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/copilot/cloud-agent/configuration returns each repository's MCP server configuration, review tools, workflow-approval and firewall settings for a registry or SSPM tool to reconcile.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted registry rule. GitHub gives the enterprise a governed catalogue of custom agents and a 24-hour session list, but no administrator inventory of automations (each is private to its creator; even repository administrators cannot see it), MCP servers are registered per repository rather than in a registry the agent consults (the private MCP registry and its restriction do not apply to the cloud agent), partner-agent apps are hidden from the installations list, and nothing denies an agent or automation for being unregistered: the default agent and repository-level custom agents in .github/agents/ remain available. The only denies are class-wide — Allow automations and the agent policies.

original.mechanism: Enterprise-level custom agents (AI Controls, REST API), agent sessions list at github.com/copilot/agents, agent apps marketplace category
original.note: The enterprise can publish approved custom agents and see sessions, but partner agents and agent apps are approved by policy toggle, not registered — and content exclusion and the registry restriction do not apply to them.

steps.title: Publish enterprise custom agents
body: Define custom agents at enterprise level under AI Controls or through the REST API and control who may manage them.

controls.mechanism: Repository Settings > Copilot > MCP servers "tools" arrays per server (repository administrators); enterprise "MCP servers in Copilot" policy (on/off); custom-agent "tools" lists; repository .github/hooks/*.json preToolUse deny; GitHub-fixed repository token (one branch, no git commands, no merge, approve or ready-for-review) under rulesets and branch protection; enterprise-managed permissions keys not supported on this surface

steps.title: Name the tools each MCP server may expose
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > MCP servers: set "tools" to specific read-only tool names rather than "*"; the agent uses configured tools autonomously and never asks for approval.

steps.title: Decide the enterprise MCP switch
body: Enterprise > AI controls > MCP > "MCP servers in Copilot"; the "MCP Registry URL" and "Restrict MCP access to registry servers" policies do not apply to the cloud agent.

steps.title: Keep the GitHub MCP server on its repository-scoped token
body: By default the built-in GitHub MCP server uses a read-only token scoped to the current repository; do not widen it with a personal access token or GitHub App key unless the task needs it.

steps.title: Deny by argument with a preToolUse hook
body: Commit .github/hooks/*.json on the default branch with a preToolUse command hook returning permissionDecision "deny"; crashes and non-zero exits deny, timeouts allow, and "ask" is treated as deny.

controls.note: Downgraded from native to partial on the AML.M0028 rule applied to every vendor. The MCP "tools" arrays are per-tool on/off without argument scoping and are set per repository by its administrators, not locked by the organisation or enterprise; argument-level rules exist only as preToolUse hooks, which are repository code that anyone who can merge to the default branch can change and which fail open on timeout; the built-in bash, edit and view tools cannot be restricted by policy (a custom agent's "tools" list narrows them only when the user picks that agent); and the enterprise-managed permissions.deny, permissions.ask and allowedMcpServers keys are marked not supported for the cloud agent. There is no bypass mode to remove because every tool call is pre-approved. The strong part is the repository side, enforced by GitHub: one branch, no git push, no merge, approval or ready-for-review, subject to rulesets. Automations add a per-automation tool selection made by their creator; setup steps run with the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions their file declares.

original.mechanism: MCP configuration "tools" arrays, read-only GitHub MCP token scoped to the repository, per-automation tool selection, least-privilege permissions in copilot-setup-steps, no push to default branch / no merge

steps.title: Name the tools each MCP server may expose
body: In Repository Settings > Copilot > MCP servers set "tools" to the specific tool names rather than "*"; Copilot uses configured tools autonomously and will not ask for approval.

steps.title: Pick tools per automation
body: When creating an automation choose exactly which tools it can use; Suggest tools proposes a minimal set.

steps.title: Keep setup-step permissions minimal
body: Set permissions in copilot-setup-steps.yml to the lowest needed (contents: read only if the step clones).

original.note: tools arrays hide MCP tools, the read-only token and no-push/no-merge rules limit resources; nothing pre-approves because runs are unattended. copilot-setup-steps permissions are the customer's to keep minimal.

original.mechanism: preToolUse and permissionRequest hooks from the repository run inside the job's sandbox and can deny a tool call; command preToolUse hooks fail closed on error; no enterprise-managed permission rules reach this surface

steps.title: Commit fail-closed hooks
body: Add preToolUse and permissionRequest hooks under the repository's hooks configuration; a crash or non-zero exit denies the call even if stdout says allow, and hooks run inside the ephemeral sandbox.

original.note: Rated partial on the same rule as Cursor cloud: hooks are repository code, writable by anyone with push access, not enterprise policy — the enterprise-managed permissions.deny rules apply to the CLI and VS Code Agent Host, not to the cloud agent. The deterministic organisation-level controls here are the tools arrays, the firewall and branch rules.

original.mechanism: Enterprise policy "MCP servers in Copilot" applies to the cloud agent (on or off); the registry restriction does not; servers configured per repository by administrators in a JSON configuration with tools arrays; GitHub and Playwright MCP servers enabled by default

steps.title: Decide the enterprise switch, then the repository lists
body: The MCP servers in Copilot policy covers the cloud agent, but Restrict MCP access to registry servers does not; the allowlist for this surface is the per-repository MCP configuration.

steps.title: Name every server and its tools per repository
body: In repository settings configure only the servers needed and set tools to specific names rather than a wildcard; custom-agent servers are processed before repository configuration.

original.note: Rated partial on the hosted-runtime rule: there is no organisation-level allowlist of servers for this surface, only an on/off policy and per-repository admission by whoever administers the repository. Admission is not integrity — nothing pins what a server serves, and MCP server processes sit outside the firewall.

controls.mechanism: Draft pull request reviewed and merged by a person other than the requester; "Approve and run workflows" gate (repository Require approval for workflow runs, on by default); ruleset "Require an additional approval for unattributed Copilot pull requests"; enterprise "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" (Disabled everywhere by default); no per-action approval inside the session

steps.title: Keep workflow approval on
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent > Actions workflow approval: leave Require approval for workflow runs enabled so a user with write access must click Approve and run workflows.

steps.title: Require approvals, including the extra one for unattributed pull requests
body: In the branch ruleset's "Require a pull request before merging", require at least one approval and leave "Require an additional approval for unattributed Copilot pull requests" on (the default).

steps.title: Keep Copilot from approving
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot code review > "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests": keep Disabled everywhere (the default); organisations otherwise decide "Count Copilot approvals toward merge requirements".

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every hosted product: a merge gate approves the output, not the actions. Every tool call, MCP call and network request in the session is pre-approved and has already happened when the reviewer arrives (a preToolUse "ask" is treated as deny because nobody is there to answer). The requester's own approval does not count toward required approvals, and workflows wait for a person. The workflow gate is a repository setting a repository administrator can turn off, not locked at organisation level. The automation "Full control" level for issue changes is, in GitHub's words, a workflow convenience and not a security control. Copilot code review approvals are an AI reviewer and never count as human approval here.

original.mechanism: Human review and merge of draft PRs; Actions workflow approval; ruleset extra approval for agent-opened PRs; code review approval policy off by default
original.note: The human gate is the pull request and the workflow-run approval; tool calls, network access and MCP actions taken while the agent produces the PR are not individually approved.

steps.title: Keep workflow approval on
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent > Actions workflow approval: leave Require approval for workflow runs enabled so a user with write access must click Approve and run workflows.

steps.title: Keep the extra approval rule and required checks
body: Rulesets require one more approval when a PR is opened under the agent's app identity (enabled by default); the requester cannot approve, and branch protections apply.

steps.title: Decide whether Copilot may approve PRs
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot code review > "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" is Disabled everywhere by default; organisations decide whether approvals count toward merge requirements.

controls.mechanism: GitHub strips hidden characters and HTML comments from issue and comment text before prompting; comments from users without write access are never presented; automations ignore events from those users by default; repository postToolUse hooks can replace a tool result (modifiedResult) before the model sees it; no classifier

steps.title: Leave untrusted-event handling at its default
body: When creating an automation keep events from users without write access ignored (the default); the opt-in is per automation, so review automations whose tool set is not read-only.

steps.title: Attach an inspector with a postToolUse hook
body: Commit .github/hooks/*.json with a postToolUse command hook that sends each tool result to your classifier and returns modifiedResult to replace flagged output; hook traffic is subject to the agent firewall.

steps.title: Use Agentic Workflows for event-driven automation that must be hardened
body: Agents run read-only; writes are buffered as safe outputs, scanned by a detection job and executed by a separate job, with @mention neutralisation, size limits and min-integrity filtering of inputs.

controls.note: Rated partial on the input-screening rule. GitHub's hidden-character and HTML-comment filtering normalises one input class and is not admin-configurable; the postToolUse hook is an attach point — repository code, changeable by anyone who can merge to the default branch, that screens nothing until the organisation attaches a classifier, and that fails open on timeout. Repository files, command output and MCP tool results are not screened by GitHub. Putting instruction files, hooks and setup steps under CODEOWNERS with "Require review from Code Owners" (GitHub's own guidance) is a process control, credited here, not screening. Agentic Workflows adds input sanitisation and an AI threat-detection job on outputs; that is a variant, not this agent's default path.

original.mechanism: Hidden-character and HTML-comment stripping before prompting, automations ignore non-write events, a content safety system on prompts and responses; Agentic Workflows sanitise user content and gate writes behind a threat-detection job
original.note: No customer-configurable classifier; the structural gates (firewall, tool selection, workflow approval) carry the weight once injection succeeds.

steps.title: Leave untrusted-event handling at its default
body: Automations ignore events from users without write access by default; do not opt in unless the tool set is read-only.

steps.title: Use Agentic Workflows for event-driven automation that must be hardened
body: Agents run read-only; writes are buffered as safe outputs, scanned by a detection job and executed by a separate job — with @mention neutralisation, size limits and min-integrity filtering of inputs.

controls.mechanism: No product feature; the organisation's TPRM platform assesses GitHub — and, for partner agents, Anthropic and OpenAI — from the GitHub Copilot Trust Center artefacts

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot Trust Center (compliance list and resources, checked 2026-09-25)
About third-party coding agents (partner apps and data path)
Hosting of models for GitHub Copilot (per-provider training and retention terms)

controls.note: External by rule: the assessment belongs to the organisation's TPRM platform. The GitHub Copilot Trust Center overview lists SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001:2013, CSA STAR Level 2, TISAX and ISO/IEC 42001:2023, with SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports, the 2026 ISO/IEC 42001 certificate, a 2026 CAIQ, a PCI DSS attestation and bug-bounty letters behind Request access; the overview shows no penetration-test summary. Partner agents (Claude, Codex) add model providers whose data terms are on the model-hosting page; the third-party agents page does not describe partner-side processing, so obtain it before enabling them. Re-assess on vendor changes such as the unified Copilot policy from 2026-09-28. For posture evidence, GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/copilot/cloud-agent/configuration and the audit log are the read points a TPRM or SSPM tool can poll.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; partner agents add Anthropic and OpenAI as processors of repository content
original.note: The third-party agent page does not state where partner agents execute or what data reaches the partner; obtain that from the partner before enabling the policy.

steps.title: Record the partner-agent data path before enabling
body: Partner agents consume Actions minutes and AI credits and install partner GitHub Apps; the docs do not describe partner-side processing — ask the vendor.

original.mechanism: REST endpoints for cloud agent management and the audit log stream are the inputs an SSPM product would read
original.note: No first-party posture report; poll the cloud agent management API and audit log from an SSPM tool to evidence firewall, approval and policy settings.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: "Copilot Usage Records Streaming" and "Copilot Usage Records API" policies (AI controls > Copilot; Enterprise Managed Users and data-residency enterprises, public preview): request and response bodies from cloud agent sessions to the audit-log stream or GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/copilot/usage-records; agentic audit events with agent_session_id; session logs in the agents panel

steps.title: Stream Copilot usage records
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot: set "Copilot Usage Records Streaming" to Enabled everywhere, then add a destination under Settings > Audit log > Log streaming (S3, Azure Blob or Event Hubs, Datadog, Google Cloud Storage, Splunk, or Microsoft Purview for agent session events only).

steps.title: Or pull them over the API
body: Set "Copilot Usage Records API" to Enabled everywhere and read GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/copilot/usage-records as an EMU enterprise owner; the records include cloud agents operating on github.com.

steps.title: Correlate on agent_session_id
body: Agentic audit events carry actor_is_agent=true, agent_session_id and the initiating user; stream the enterprise audit log to keep them beyond 180 days.

steps.title: Review the session log
body: github.com/copilot/agents or the repository Agents tab shows each session's reasoning and tools used, and every agent commit message links to its session log.

controls.note: Upgraded to native on the tracing rule because a programmatic export now covers this hosted surface: the usage-records stream and API deliver the request and response body of each Copilot API call — where the session's prompts, proposed tool calls and returned tool results travel — to a store the organisation controls. Boundary: public preview, and only for Enterprise Managed Users enterprises and GHEC with data residency; other enterprises have the UI session log and the audit log only, which is partial. Records carry user_id, github_request_id and event_id, not agent_session_id, so joining them to the audit trail is by user and time; bodies over 1 MB are truncated. Command output appears only as far as it reaches the model; MCP server traffic and setup steps are not traced. The enterprise-managed "telemetry" (OpenTelemetry) key is not supported for the cloud agent. Tamper resistance is the destination's.

original.mechanism: Session logs (reasoning, tool calls, token usage) at github.com/copilot/agents and in the repository Agents tab; commit messages link to sessions; no OpenTelemetry export for the cloud agent
original.note: Logs are queryable in the UI and streamed live, but the managed telemetry export does not cover the cloud agent, so traces cannot leave GitHub programmatically.

steps.title: Use session logs and the agents panel
body: Open github.com/copilot/agents or the repository Agents tab; each session shows internal reasoning, tools used, token usage and session length, and every agent commit links back to it.

original.mechanism: Enterprise / organisation audit log (actor:Copilot, actor_is_agent, agent_session_id, 180 days, streaming to SIEM); signed commits with human co-author

steps.title: Stream agent audit events
body: Filter actor:Copilot for agent actions and action:copilot for policy changes; stream the enterprise audit log to a SIEM for retention beyond 180 days.

steps.title: Correlate on agent_session_id
body: Agentic events record the action, actor_is_agent=true, agent_session_id and the initiating user; available to EMU enterprises and GHEC with data residency.

original.note: The audit log attributes agent events and the commits are signed, but a signed commit attests the commit, not the session's tool calls and network actions that produced it. 180-day retention; tamper evidence beyond that is the SIEM's.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Memory policy (off by default on Business and Enterprise; public preview): repository facts validated against the current branch by citation and deletable under repository Settings > Copilot > Memory, user preferences exportable and deletable by administrators, 28-day unused expiry; cloud agent session logs shared with repository readers and archivable, not deletable; instruction files protected only by rulesets

steps.title: Set the Memory policy
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Features > Copilot Memory, or Organization Settings > Copilot > Policies > Copilot Memory; it stays off unless enabled.

steps.title: Review repository facts and user preferences
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > Memory lists stored facts to delete; Organization Settings > Copilot > Access > Get usage report > Download user memories or Delete user memories handles preferences.

steps.title: Lock the enterprise agent profiles
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > "Protect agent files using rulesets" > Create ruleset, so only enterprise owners can edit agent profiles in the governance repository.

controls.note: Rated partial on the memory-hardening rule. An administrator can disable memory, and repository facts are validated against the current branch before use and reviewable by repository owners, but user preferences are checked only by the model's "best judgment", facts can be captured from pull requests closed without merging, and there is no quarantine or rollback — only deletion. Instruction sources other than enterprise agent profiles (copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md, repository custom agents, hooks, copilot-setup-steps.yml) are repository files protected only by the organisation's own rulesets and CODEOWNERS. Persistence with no admin setting: session logs are shared by default with everyone who can read the repository and can be archived but not deleted; a snapshot key in copilot-setup-steps.yml creates a custom runner image version that outlives the session.

original.mechanism: Copilot Memory policy (public preview): repository-scoped facts validated against the current branch, user preferences owned by the billing entity, 28-day unused expiry, admin export / delete

steps.title: Set the Memory policy
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Features > Copilot Memory: Enabled everywhere, Disabled everywhere or Let organizations decide.

steps.title: Know the scope and expiry
body: Repository facts stay in their repository and carry code citations; entries unused for 28 days are deleted; code review uses repository facts only.

original.note: Validation against the current branch and expiry are integrity and retention contributions; there is no quarantine or rollback — an admin can only delete. Public preview.

controls.mechanism: User-level budgets (Bundled AI credits budget, Users scope; always a hard stop); SKU-level "Copilot cloud agent" and organisation or enterprise budgets with "Stop usage when budget limit is reached"; the "AI credits paid usage" policy; GitHub Actions budgets; 59-minute session hard limit, shorter with timeout-minutes in copilot-setup-steps.yml

steps.title: Set a universal user-level budget
body: Enterprise > Billing & Licensing > Budgets and alerts > New budget > Bundled AI credits budget, scope Users with the user field empty; user-level budgets always enforce a hard stop.

steps.title: Cap the cloud agent and stop at the limit
body: Add a SKU-level budget for Copilot cloud agent (and an Actions product budget for its runner minutes) with "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" selected; without it usage is not stopped.

steps.title: Decide on paid overage
body: Disable the "AI credits paid usage" policy in AI controls to block usage once the included pool is exhausted; it is enabled by default.

steps.title: Shorten the session ceiling where tasks are small
body: Set timeout-minutes (maximum 59) on the copilot-setup-steps job; the 59-minute session limit itself cannot be extended.

controls.note: Rated native on the AML.M0036 rule: administrators set per-user and per-organisation caps that GitHub checks on every AI-credit request — user-level budgets always hard-stop and a $0 budget blocks immediately — so a session is refused at its next model call once its user's budget or a stopping budget is exhausted. GitHub documents the per-request check, not what the session then shows. Organisation, cost-centre and enterprise budgets stop usage only when "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" is selected (off by default). Automations bill to their creator. Duration is bounded by the 59-minute hard limit and, below it, by timeout-minutes in a repository file any writer can edit; there is no admin-set concurrency or per-session tool-call cap, and Actions minutes need their own Actions budget. Premium-request budgets were converted to AI-credit budgets.

original.mechanism: 59-minute hard session limit, organisation AI-credit budgets that block agent features when exhausted, Actions minutes, autopilot continuation limits in automations

steps.title: Set AI-credit budgets
body: When budget limits are exhausted, code reviews and other AI-credit features are blocked; enable AI credits paid usage deliberately.

steps.title: Rely on the session ceiling
body: Each cloud agent session runs at most 59 minutes and cannot be extended; setup steps share that limit.

original.note: Sub-limits: runtime (59-minute session limit, hard), spend (AI-credit budgets that block features when exhausted, hard at the organisation), Actions minutes (hard). No per-session tool-call or iteration cap.

controls.mechanism: Stop session in the session log viewer (ends the Actions run, keeps pushed commits); enterprise "Block Copilot cloud agent in all repositories owned by ENTERPRISE-NAME" toggle and Copilot Cloud Agent policy; organisation Repository access, Allow automations and Partner agents switches; 59-minute hard limit

steps.title: Stop a running session
body: Open the session from github.com/copilot/agents or the repository Agents tab and click Stop session; the GitHub Actions run ends and commits already pushed remain.

steps.title: Block new sessions across the enterprise
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent: toggle "Block Copilot cloud agent in all repositories owned by ENTERPRISE-NAME", which also covers users licensed elsewhere.

steps.title: Stop scheduled and event-triggered runs
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent: turn off Allow automations, and narrow Repository access to remove the agent from affected repositories.

steps.title: Switch off the partner agents too
body: The Partner agents toggles (Claude, Codex) on the Cloud agent page and the enterprise agent apps policy are separate; disabling the cloud agent leaves them on.

controls.note: Downgraded from native to partial on the hosted kill-switch rule. The documented stop for a running session is Stop session in the session view; GitHub does not say an organisation or enterprise administrator can use it on another user's session, the AI controls session list offers view and filter only, and the agent tasks API has no cancel endpoint. The administrator switches (Block toggle, policy, Repository access, Allow automations, partner-agent and agent-app policies) prevent new sessions; their effect on a session already running is not documented — delay not documented. Every session ends within the 59-minute hard limit. Revocation of the session's git token is not documented, and pushed commits stay on the branch.

original.mechanism: Enterprise policy Disabled, repository opt-out, Stop session, firewall on, separate third-party and agent-app policies

steps.title: Stop a running session
body: Click Stop session in the session log viewer to end the Actions run; pushed commits are preserved.

steps.title: Disable every agent policy, not just one
body: Set Copilot Cloud Agent to Disabled, and separately disable Third-party agents and Agent apps under AI controls > Agents — disabling the cloud agent does not disable the others.

controls.mechanism: One ephemeral GitHub Actions environment per session, destroyed when the session ends; a fresh virtual machine per session on GitHub-hosted runners; organisation Runner type with "Allow repositories to customize the runner type" off pins that for every repository; 59-minute hard limit

steps.title: Pin the runner at organisation level
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Cloud agent > Runner type: Standard GitHub runner, then turn off Allow repositories to customize the runner type so copilot-setup-steps.yml cannot move sessions elsewhere.

steps.title: Keep sessions on fresh machines
body: GitHub recommends GitHub-hosted runners so each session runs on a fresh virtual machine; if you must use self-hosted runners, use ephemeral single-use ones — their isolation is then yours.

steps.title: Know what runs inside the sandbox
body: Hooks run in the ephemeral, non-interactive Linux sandbox the cloud agent provisions for each job, with a constrained network, and anything they write is discarded when the job ends.

controls.note: Native on the hosted D3-EI rule, re-verified: GitHub documents an ephemeral environment per session, destroyed when the session ends, with each session on a fresh virtual machine on GitHub-hosted runners, and an organisation owner can lock the runner type. Inside the boundary: setup steps, the agent's commands, hooks and local MCP server processes. Outside: the model, GitHub's services and remote MCP servers. The guarantee does not hold on self-hosted runners (GitHub recommends ephemeral single-use runners; reuse is possible) and GitHub's single-CPU hosted runners are containers on a shared VM. What crosses sessions: pushed commits, the session log, Copilot Memory and any custom image version saved with the setup job's snapshot key.

original.mechanism: Ephemeral development environment per job powered by GitHub Actions — a non-interactive Linux sandbox with a constrained network, destroyed when the job ends; 59-minute hard limit; optionally on the organisation's own runners

steps.title: Keep the agent on the ephemeral Actions environment
body: Each task runs in its own ephemeral environment on GitHub Actions and ends within 59 minutes, a limit that cannot be extended; if you route it to self-hosted runners (configure-runners), the isolation of that runner is yours.

steps.title: Know what runs inside the sandbox
body: Setup steps, the agent's commands, hooks and MCP server processes all run inside the job's sandbox; the firewall applies to the agent's Bash processes but not to MCP server processes.

original.note: Inside the boundary: commands, setup steps, hooks and MCP servers. Outside: the model and GitHub's own services, reached through the agent's app identity. The boundary is a job, not a session: nothing persists after it ends except what was pushed.

controls.mechanism: Agent firewall under Copilot > Internet access: organisation "Enable firewall" and "Recommended allowlist" (Enabled, Disabled or Let repositories decide), "Allow repository custom rules" and an organisation custom allowlist repositories cannot delete; domain and URL rules; blocked requests reported in the pull request; enforced only on processes the agent starts through its Bash tool

steps.title: Lock the firewall at organisation level
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Internet access, Copilot cloud agent section: set Enable firewall to Enabled (the default is Let repositories decide) so repositories cannot turn it off.

steps.title: Own the allowlist
body: Set Allow repository custom rules to Disabled, maintain the Organization custom allowlist (domains or URL prefixes), and set Recommended allowlist deliberately — it admits public package and container registries.

controls.note: Partial on the hosted egress rule even though the organisation can now author and lock the list. It is enforced on processes the agent starts through its Bash tool, not around the sandbox: MCP server processes and copilot-setup-steps are outside it (there is no separate setup-phase policy — setup is unfirewalled), GitHub states sophisticated attacks may bypass it, and it operates only inside GitHub's Actions appliance — it must be disabled on self-hosted runners and is not compatible with Windows. GitHub's own hosts and the Copilot API are always allowed. On self-hosted or Azure-private-network runners the organisation's network controls are the egress control.

original.mechanism: Firewall on by default with the recommended allowlist (OS packages, container and language registries, certificate authorities, Playwright hosts); custom allowlist per repository; organisation Settings > Copilot > Internet access can enforce or delegate

steps.title: Enforce the firewall at organisation level
body: Under Settings > Copilot > Internet access keep the firewall enabled and enforce it for every repository, adding only the hosts your builds need; disabling it lets Copilot connect to any host.

original.note: Rated partial on the egress rule: the firewall applies only to processes the agent starts through its Bash tool, not to MCP server processes — including the Playwright MCP server enabled by default — and the vendor states that sophisticated attacks may bypass it. Bound MCP servers through their configuration and tools arrays, and treat the firewall as blast-radius reduction.

controls.mechanism: No git proxy: GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN are set in the sandbox, the repository credential limited to the working repository and one branch; Agents secrets and variables reach setup steps and the agent's commands as environment variables, COPILOT_MCP_* values only MCP servers; secret values masked in session logs; Actions, Codespaces and Dependabot secrets never passed

steps.title: Scope Agents secrets to the repositories that need them
body: Organization Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents > New organization secret, Repository access: Selected repositories; repository-level secrets live under the repository's Secrets and variables > Agents.

steps.title: Keep MCP credentials MCP-only
body: Prefix values meant for MCP servers COPILOT_MCP_ so only the MCP configuration receives them; every other Agents secret is an environment variable the agent's commands can read.

steps.title: Keep everything else out of the Agents type
body: Store tokens the agent must not reach as Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets, which it never receives; setup steps get the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN with only the permissions the file declares.

steps.title: Leave the GitHub MCP server on its repository-scoped token
body: Set COPILOT_MCP_GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN only when needed, and then as a fine-grained, read-only token limited to specific repositories.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted D3-CTS rule. GitHub does not proxy the repository credential: the hooks reference lists GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN among the sandbox's environment variables, so both sit inside the boundary where any command can read them. What bounds them is scope — the working repository, one branch, no merge, and GitHub states the agent cannot run git push itself — and their lifetime is not documented. Agents secrets are not removed after setup: setup steps and every command the agent runs receive them, so the model sees any value a command prints; masking applies to session logs, not the model's context. Only COPILOT_MCP_* values are confined to MCP servers. The strong part is exclusion: no Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secret reaches the agent. Agentic Workflows (a variant) shows the proxy pattern: the engine key stays in the AWF API proxy sidecar and the agent sees a dummy key.

original.mechanism: Agents secrets and variables (repository or organisation) exposed as environment variables to setup steps and the agent's commands; COPILOT_MCP_ prefix limits a value to MCP servers; no access to Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets; pushes go through the agent's own push path, not git commands

steps.title: Scope secrets to MCP servers with the prefix
body: Store values MCP servers need under COPILOT_MCP_* so they reach only those servers; everything else under Agents secrets is an environment variable every command can read.

steps.title: Keep the agent's own reach narrow
body: The agent cannot run git push itself and can only perform simple push operations; rulesets keep the requester from approving its PR.

original.note: Rated partial because Agents secrets sit inside the execution boundary: any command in the job can read them and print them to the model. The isolation that exists is scope — no other secret types, MCP-only values, and an app identity rather than a person's token. No on-behalf-of exchange: actions carry the agent's app identity with the requesting human as co-author.

original.mechanism: Agents-type secrets and variables (repository / organisation Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents); COPILOT_MCP_* prefix scopes values to MCP servers; no access to Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets

steps.title: Use the Agents secret type only
body: Add secrets under Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents; prefix MCP credentials COPILOT_MCP_ so they are only available to MCP server configuration and never exported as general environment variables.

steps.title: Keep engine credentials out of Agentic Workflow agents
body: In Agentic Workflows the real engine key stays in the AWF API proxy sidecar; the agent container sees only a dummy key — configure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY as repository secrets, not in the workflow body.

original.note: Agents secrets are readable by the setup steps and MCP servers they are scoped to (COPILOT_MCP_*), and by commands the agent runs in the session; the model sees a value if a command prints it. They are stored secrets, not ephemeral issuance.

controls.mechanism: Agents secrets and variables encrypted (LibSodium; list and get return metadata, never the value) and scoped by organisation owners to selected repositories; git and Copilot API tokens set by GitHub in each job's sandbox (lifetime undocumented); OIDC federation available in copilot-setup-steps; no vendor tunnel — private reach is self-hosted or Azure-private-network runners

steps.title: Keep session secrets in the Agents store, scoped
body: Organization Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents > New organization secret with Repository access set to Selected repositories; repository administrators add repository-level Agents secrets.

steps.title: Rotate through the API
body: PUT /orgs/{org}/agents/secrets/{secret_name} with a value encrypted to the key from GET /orgs/{org}/agents/secrets/public-key; list and get endpoints never reveal the encrypted value.

steps.title: Prefer federated credentials in setup steps
body: Grant id-token: write on the copilot-setup-steps job and sign in with OIDC (GitHub's Azure DevOps example uses azure/login) instead of storing a long-lived cloud key as an Agents secret.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted D3-CH rule. The store is sound — Agents secrets are encrypted, never returned by the API and scoped per repository — but inside the session they are plain environment variables readable by every command and so by the model (masking covers session logs only), and GitHub documents no expiry or rotation for them; rotation is the organisation's job. The session's own GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN are GitHub-issued, but their lifetime is not documented. Tunnel: GitHub offers no tunnel or connector for this product; reach into private networks is through self-hosted runners or larger runners with Azure private networking, so there is no tunnel token to harden, and credentials for internal MCP servers are Agents secrets (COPILOT_MCP_*). A token obtained by OIDC in setup steps is short-lived but also lands in the sandbox.

summary: Governance runs through the enterprise AI-controls tab and organisation Copilot settings: Feature, Privacy and Models policies set enterprise-first (enable, disable, or let organisations decide), with content exclusion and MCP governance layered on for Business and Enterprise plans.

Inference runs on GitHub's Copilot API (api.*.githubcopilot.com per plan) against models hosted on Azure, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, GCP, xAI and Fireworks; with local BYOK the prompts go straight from the editor to the chosen provider and bypass GitHub. Prompts, open-file context, tool arguments and (in agent mode) shell output leave the device; the audit log never sees them — only an OpenTelemetry export the enterprise pins in managed settings does.

Two admin planes overlap in VS Code: device policy (Windows registry Software\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode, macOS configuration profiles, /etc/vscode/policy.json) and GitHub's managed-settings.json (MDM key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot / com.github.copilot, then server-managed copilot/managed-settings.json, then a local file). Where both set the same policy the Copilot managed setting wins. JetBrains honours the managed file for MCP, plugins, telemetry and bypass-mode lockout (2026-08-18) and a managed sandbox in preview (2026-09-08); Visual Studio is ADMX-only.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max; Business and Enterprise carry policies, content exclusion, MCP governance and managed settings.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: GitHub Copilot API by plan (*.business / *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com); OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS Bedrock / Anthropic / GCP, Gemini on GCP, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry/Fireworks. Data residency (US, EU) is a policy at +10% credits.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training; model providers run under zero-data-retention except Claude Fable 5 / 5.1, which retain by default with a ZDR exemption available through end-2026.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: GitHub Copilot documentation, plus the VS Code enterprise policy reference.

items.title: Enterprise and organisation policy framework
body: Policies gate which Copilot features, agents and models users can access — named policies include MCP servers in Copilot, restricting MCP to registry servers, allowed models, custom models, web search, Copilot Memory and suggestions-matching-public-code (blocked by default for Business seats). Conflict rules matter for design: within one enterprise the least restrictive setting wins across a user's organisations, so a lockdown must be set at the enterprise level to be a lockdown.

items.title: MCP governance and content exclusion
body: The MCP policy gates whether MCP servers run at all across Copilot clients; server allowlisting comes in two strengths — a GitHub-hosted Managed Settings File (GA, matched on name, URL and stdio command, not user-bypassable) and a Custom MCP Registry (preview, name matching only, bypassable by editing local config). Content exclusion (Business and Enterprise) applies at repository, organisation and enterprise scope with fnmatch patterns, but is not honoured by the edit and agent modes of Chat in VS Code and other editors, nor by third-party agents — scope guidance accordingly.

items.title: Audit surface and network posture
body: The organisation audit log records Copilot licensing, settings and policy changes (action:copilot) and the cloud agent's website activity (actor:Copilot) with 180-day retention — it does not capture client-side prompts, so IDE-level telemetry needs its own answer. Proxy and firewall allowlists are documented per-plan, with a /meta API endpoint for the current domain set.
