tools.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio (agents, knowledge, tools and connectors, autonomous triggers, computer use)

variants.name: Agents on the standard harness (topics, generative orchestration, agent flows)
variants.note: The harness most governance pages are written for (Entra Agent ID, tools, connectors, computer use); publishes to Teams and Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Direct Line websites, WhatsApp, Facebook and Dynamics 365 Customer Service.

variants.name: Agents on the GitHub Copilot harness (goal-driven, multi-step, files, skills, memory, sandbox)
variants.note: A Copilot Studio runtime, not the GitHub Copilot service; customer data is not sent to GitHub Copilot and Copilot Studio's privacy, compliance and residency commitments apply. Runs each task in a sandbox governed by Copilot Studio.

variants.name: Agents on the Copilot chat harness (extend Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat)
variants.note: Published to internal teams only; billed by consumption or included in the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. Conversation transcripts are not written to Dataverse for Microsoft 365 Copilot agents.

summary: Microsoft's low-code agent builder: makers author agents from instructions, knowledge sources (SharePoint, OneDrive, uploaded files, public websites, Dataverse, connectors), tools (Power Platform connectors, agent flows, MCP servers, REST APIs, prompts, computer use) and event triggers, then publish them to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot, SharePoint, websites and messaging channels. Agents run in Microsoft's cloud on Azure OpenAI models by default, with Anthropic, Mistral and xAI models available per environment once an administrator allows them; connectors reach third-party services from Microsoft's cloud, and on-premises systems through the on-premises data gateway.

The administrator is the Power Platform administrator: data policies and advanced connector policies, environment and environment-group settings (Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents), Managed Environments sharing limits, Manage > Inventory with Block and the quarantine API, Security > Threat detection and Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels. Each new agent gets a Microsoft Entra Agent ID; maker and user activity is audited in Microsoft Purview; conversation transcripts land in the environment's Dataverse.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Standalone Copilot Studio subscription (any supported channel, premium connectors, Copilot Credits); Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams plan in select Microsoft 365 subscriptions (classic orchestration, Teams only); the Copilot chat harness is billed by consumption or included in Microsoft 365 Copilot. The free trial cannot publish.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Generative AI features draw on Azure OpenAI Service and Bing Search. External models (Anthropic, Mistral, xAI) need access allowed in the Microsoft 365 admin center and then Enable External Models per environment or environment group; Anthropic is a Microsoft subprocessor under the DPA since 2026-01-07 but is excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and xAI is US-only.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: A vendor-hosted platform: prompts, knowledge, tool calls and model calls are processed in Microsoft's cloud. In some geographies outside the United States, generative AI features move data across regional boundaries once a Global or Power Platform administrator allows it; Bing-powered features fall under the Microsoft Services Agreement and Privacy Statement. A configured external threat-detection provider receives the prompt, recent history, prior tool outputs and proposed tool inputs.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Transcripts are saved to the environment's Dataverse (a bulk-delete job removes them after 30 days unless changed) and held in Copilot Studio storage for up to 28 days; administrators can stop saving per environment or environment group. Purview retention covers interactions under Microsoft Copilot Experiences. The tenant setting Data sharing for Dynamics 365 Copilot and Power Platform Copilot AI Features (human review and model improvement) is disabled by default.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio (Security and governance overview)

facts.label: Admin planes
facts.value: Power Platform admin center (Security > Data and privacy > Data policy; environment Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents; Managed Environments; Manage > Inventory and Manage > Copilot Studio; Security > Threat detection; Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels; Tenant settings), Microsoft Entra admin center (agent identities), Microsoft Purview (Audit, DSPM for AI, DLP) and the Teams or Microsoft 365 admin center for org-catalogue approval.

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: The on-premises data gateway opens outbound connections to Azure Service Bus on TCP 443 (default), 5671, 5672 and 9350-9354; no inbound port is required.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Power Platform admin center: Security > Data and privacy > Data policy (Copilot Studio connectors for authentication, knowledge, HTTP, skills, triggers and channels; Configure connector > Connector actions and Connector endpoints); environment Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents (Control maker credential options, transcript settings, Enable External Models); Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing; Manage > Inventory (Block, Download); Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection; Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels; Copilot > Settings (Connected Agents Copilot Studio); Settings > Tenant settings (Publish Copilots with AI features, Environment routing); Manage > Data (preview) for gateways. Microsoft Entra admin center: agent identities. Microsoft Purview: Audit, DSPM for AI, DLP on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location.

links.title: Security and governance in Copilot Studio

items.title: Whose credentials a tool runs on
body: Each tool's Authentication is End user (the default for connectors and flows) or Maker-provided; computer use defaults to Maker-provided. The automatic security scan warns the maker before publishing when Maker-provided is chosen, the inventory records connectionProvider Maker or User per connector operation, and Control maker credential options lets the administrator remove the Maker-provided choice per environment or environment group, at the cost of autonomous and scheduled runs, which then fail.

links.title: Automatic security scan in Copilot Studio

riskNotes.note: Both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default, and computer use defaults to the maker's. A tool on maker credentials lends the maker's access to every consumer; the inventory's connectionProvider field finds them and Control maker credential options removes the choice.

Any licensed user can build in the default environment unless environment routing sends makers to personal developer environments; the inventory lists drafts and Agent Builder agents but not classic chatbots.

Knowledge sources, connector and MCP results and web pages re-enter the orchestrator. Built-in UPIA and XPIA blocking is vendor-run and always on; the admin-configured external threat detection (preview) sees proposed tool calls only and allows them by default if it does not answer within one second.

No authentication lets anyone with the link chat with the agent unless a data policy blocks Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio; locally uploaded knowledge files are served to anyone who can use the agent, whatever the source file's permissions.

Event triggers and computer use act with no person present; Ask the end user before running is off by default on every tool, and computer use can operate on any website or application unless the maker turns on access control.
SharePoint and OneDrive files and folders added through Upload files are synchronised into a Dataverse index, so whoever can write the folder writes what every agent grounded on it reads.

Anthropic models sit outside the EU Data Boundary, Bing-powered features fall under the Microsoft Services Agreement, and an external threat-detection provider receives conversation and tool data under its own terms.

controls.mechanism: Purview DLP policy on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location with Content contains > Sensitivity labels, which Microsoft documents as restricting Copilot Studio agents in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing labelled SharePoint knowledge; encrypting labels without EXTRACT withhold content; sensitivity labels shown on responses; SIT classification of prompts and responses in DSPM for AI (detect only); data policies block knowledge-source types (Knowledge source with documents / SharePoint and OneDrive / public websites in Copilot Studio)

steps.title: Keep labelled SharePoint content out of agents
body: In the Purview portal create a DLP policy on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location with Content contains > Sensitivity labels and Prevent Copilot from processing content; Microsoft applies it to Copilot Studio agents grounded on SharePoint in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

steps.title: Configure the label rule
body: Use Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Custom policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location, one rule per label condition (SIT and label conditions cannot share a rule).

steps.title: Detect sensitive data in agent conversations
body: In DSPM for AI (classic) > Recommendations run Detect unethical behavior in AI, which detects sensitive information in prompts and responses of Copilot Studio agents; review in activity explorer.

controls.note: Partial on the redaction rule (core rule 5): the enforcing control is label-based, not content inspection. Purview lists only the SharePoint-knowledge label restriction as the DLP capability for Copilot Studio agents, and only for agents in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot; files a maker uploads, public websites, connector payloads and tool calls are not inspected, nothing masks a span, and SIT detection in DSPM for AI raises findings without blocking. Blocking knowledge-source connectors in a data policy (Knowledge source with documents in Copilot Studio) is minimisation, not detection. Encrypted and password-protected files are never grounded. Agents on non-Microsoft channels need Purview pay-as-you-go billing. The toolM365Copilot prompt-level SIT block is not documented for Copilot Studio agents.

controls.mechanism: Data policy blocking the connector Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio (No authentication becomes unavailable and Require users to sign in cannot be turned off); environment or environment-group setting Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options (End-user credentials / Maker-provided credentials); Managed Environments agent sharing rules (Let people grant Viewer permissions, Only share with individuals, Limit number of viewers; bot-limitSharingMode, bot-maxLimitUserSharing, bot-authoringSharingDisabled); Agent access channels (preview)

steps.title: Require authentication on every channel
body: In Security > Data and privacy > Data policy, in a policy scoped to all environments, block Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio so only Authenticate with Microsoft or Authenticate manually can be published.

steps.title: Remove maker-provided credentials
body: In Manage > Environment groups (or Environments) > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents, set Control maker credential options to End-user credentials only.

steps.title: Limit who an agent can be shared with
body: In Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing, clear Let people grant Viewer permissions when agents are shared, or select Only share with individuals and set Limit number of viewers.

steps.title: Restrict the publishing channels
body: In Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels, clear the channels an environment group may not publish to (preview; published agents on a blocked channel fail at runtime).

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule: the administrator can enforce authentication on every channel, remove maker credentials (the confused-deputy case) and cap who may use or co-author an agent, tenant-wide through data-policy scope and environment groups. Defaults to change: new agents start on Authenticate with Microsoft, but makers may pick No authentication until the data policy blocks it; both credential modes are allowed by default, and computer use defaults to maker credentials. Costs and gaps: with maker credentials removed, scheduled and autonomous runs fail for lack of a live user; sharing rules need Managed Environments, apply only to new shares (non-compliant agents can only be unshared) and take up to an hour; Generic OAuth agents cannot restrict which users chat. Policy administration is not the enforcement path: Entra and the connector runtime enforce it.

controls.mechanism: A Microsoft Entra Agent ID created automatically for every new agent since May 2026 (no opt-out), a child of the Microsoft-owned Microsoft Copilot Studio agent identity blueprint, with the owner as sponsor, connector API permissions attached at publish (Operations.Execute.All or per-operation scopes) and deletion with the agent; legacy agents keep app registrations until migrated (Actions > Recommendations > Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID, preview)

steps.title: Find each agent's identity
body: Read the GUID at agent Settings > Advanced > Metadata > Entra Agent ID, or the entraAgentId field in the inventory, and review the identity, its sponsor and its API permissions in the Entra admin center.

steps.title: Migrate legacy app-registration agents
body: In Actions > Recommendations open Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID for enhanced agent governance, migrate a pilot batch, and validate before the next.

steps.title: Put Conditional Access on connector scopes
body: Target the connector permissions on agent identities with Conditional Access (network location, device compliance, risk); today it is evaluated only when the agent runs in Microsoft Teams.

steps.title: Give agent access an expiry
body: Assign agent identities access through Entra ID Governance access packages with an end date so access lapses unless the sponsor extends it.

controls.note: Partial on the agent-identity rule, the same word as toolM365Copilot: a directory principal is minted per agent, inventoried with a sponsor and deleted with the agent, and no one in the tenant can mint tokens for it. But what the agent does in connected systems is authenticated as the end user or the maker through the Power Platform connection, not as the agent identity; Conditional Access on the agent identity is evaluated only in Teams (other channels use the existing connector authentication flow); custom connectors, MCP servers and REST API tools add no permissions to it; agents created before May 2026 run on app registrations until migrated; Agent Builder agents have no identity. Disabling the agent identity as a revocation path is not documented; deleting the agent is.

controls.mechanism: Power Platform inventory (Manage > Inventory and Manage > Copilot Studio; Power Platform API inventory, Azure Resource Graph, Power Platform for Admins V2 connector): every Copilot Studio and Agent Builder agent, drafts included, with ownerId, createdBy, environment, lastPublishedAt, authentication, channels, sharedWithViewers (entireTenant), entraAgentId, isQuarantined, and powerPlatformConnectors[].operations[] with connectionProvider (Maker or User) and connectionIdSharedByMaker; Block in the command bar and the quarantine API

steps.title: Query the inventory for maker-credential agents
body: In Manage > Inventory filter Copilot Studio agents, add the Connectors column, and query powerPlatformConnectors operations where connectionProvider is Maker through Azure Resource Graph or the inventory API; export to CSV for reconciliation.

steps.title: Find public and tenant-wide agents
body: Filter on authentication None and sharedWithViewers.entireTenant true, and on owners who have left, to reassign or block.

steps.title: Block what should not run
body: Select a published agent in Manage > Inventory or Manage > Copilot Studio and choose Block; unblock once remediated.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule: the platform itself keeps an authoritative, queryable record of every agent with owner, channels, authentication mode and, per connector operation, whether it runs on the maker's or the user's connection, and the administrator can block or quarantine from it. Limits: most configuration fields are preview; capabilities reflect the published version only; detailed capability data covers Power Platform connectors and a web-search flag, not HTTP nodes, REST API tools, computer use or other knowledge sources; at most 200 resources of each type per agent; changes appear within 15 to 20 minutes; classic chatbots are listed separately. The inventory records agents after the fact rather than admitting them, so the publication gate is a separate row.

controls.mechanism: Solutions as the versioned unit; Power Platform pipelines with delegated deployments (approval before deploying as a service principal or pipeline owner), stages the same exported artifact must pass in order, and redeploy of previous solution versions; Settings > Tenant settings > Environment routing to personal developer environments and Publish Copilots with AI features; Submit for admin approval to list an agent in the org catalogue of Teams and Microsoft 365

steps.title: Route makers out of the default environment
body: Turn on Environment routing in Settings > Tenant settings so makers land in managed personal developer environments governed by environment-group rules.

steps.title: Promote through an approved pipeline
body: Build a pipeline (development, test, production) in the Deployment Pipeline Configuration app with delegated deployments so a named approver releases each stage.

steps.title: Keep a way back
body: Turn on the pipeline setting that allows redeploying previous solution versions from the run history.

steps.title: Approve org-wide listing
body: Review agents submitted with Show to everyone in my org in the Teams admin center Manage apps page before they appear in Built for your org.

controls.note: Partial on the rollout rule. Met: versioning (solutions, managed layers), a promotion gate a person approves (delegated deployments) that cannot skip a stage, and rollback by redeploying an earlier version. Not met: nothing forces a maker to use the pipeline, since anyone with maker rights in an environment can publish straight to its channels; the org-catalogue approval covers the listing and its details only, and content changes republish without re-approval; no canary or percentage release, and no evaluation gate. Publish Copilots with AI features is an all-or-nothing switch. Pipeline targets must be Managed Environments.

controls.mechanism: Built-in user prompt-injection (UPIA) and cross-domain prompt-injection (XPIA) blocking on every published agent, always on, with blocked-message counts in the maker's Protection status and Security analytics; admin-configured external threat detection (preview) at Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection per environment (Microsoft Defender or a partner webhook) that allows or blocks each proposed tool call, with Set error behavior; content moderation level set per agent by the maker

steps.title: Connect runtime threat detection
body: Register the Entra app with the provider's federated credential, then in Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection select the environment, choose Set up and Allow Copilot Studio to share data with a threat detection provider.

steps.title: Fail closed
body: Change Set error behavior from Allow the agent to respond to Block the query, so a provider timeout (one second) or error blocks the tool call.

steps.title: Review blocked prompt attacks
body: Ask makers to review Protection status > See details > Security analytics (Reason for block) for their agents.

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: the injection classifiers that screen prompts and knowledge are vendor-internal, always on and not admin-tunable, and their detections surface in a per-agent maker view rather than an administrator event stream. External threat detection is an attach point where a Defender or partner classifier can block, but it judges proposed tool calls (with the prompt, history and prior tool outputs as context) rather than screening each knowledge chunk before context assembly; it is preview, generative orchestration only, set per environment or environment group with no tenant-wide, PowerShell or API setting (new environments start without it), and allows the call by default when the provider is slow. Content moderation is a maker setting. Our gateway's classification of grounding it returns is the other half of this pin.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Studio compliance offerings (HIPAA BAA, HITRUST, FedRAMP, SOC, ISO, PCI DSS, CSA STAR) and the Service Trust Portal audit reports feed the organisation's TPRM platform; external-model and threat-detection provider terms assessed separately

evidence.title: Copilot Studio compliance offerings
Get started with the Microsoft Service Trust Portal
Allow external language models (Anthropic subprocessor, EU Data Boundary and FedRAMP exclusions)

controls.note: External: the assessment, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform, as for every vendor. Copilot Studio is an Online Service covered by HIPAA (BAA), HITRUST, FedRAMP, SOC, ISO, PCI DSS and CSA STAR, but Anthropic models are outside the EU Data Boundary, FedRAMP and PCI DSS, xAI is US-only, and an external threat-detection provider handles data under its own terms. Re-assess when external models are enabled, when a threat-detection provider is connected and when harnesses change. The Service Trust Portal renders client-side and was not read.

controls.mechanism: Power Platform data policies (Security > Data and privacy > Data policy): every connector classified Business, Non-business or Blocked, connectors in different groups cannot be combined, Copilot Studio connectors for HTTP, skills, event triggers (Microsoft Copilot Studio), knowledge and channels; Configure connector > Connector actions (per-action allow or deny, default for new actions); Connector endpoints (preview); advanced connector policies (default-deny allowlist, MCP server-level blocking); enforced in real time with the Publish button unavailable on violation; exemptions no longer supported

steps.title: Classify connectors tenant-wide
body: In Security > Data and privacy > Data policy create a policy with Add all environments, move each connector to Business, Non-business or Blocked, and block HTTP, Skills with Copilot Studio and the Microsoft Copilot Studio (event triggers) connector where they are not needed.

steps.title: Allow only the actions you need
body: On a blockable connector choose Configure connector > Connector actions, deny write actions you do not accept, and set Default connector action settings to block new actions.

steps.title: Pin connectors to known endpoints
body: Use Configure connector > Connector endpoints on HTTP and the SharePoint and public-website knowledge connectors to allow only approved URLs (preview).

steps.title: Move to default-deny
body: In an environment group's Rules tab add Advanced connector policies with only the approved certified and MCP connectors; new connectors are blocked automatically.

controls.note: Native on the tool-permission rule: a tenant policy classifies connectors, refuses violating combinations at authoring and publish and again at runtime, and restricts individual operations and endpoints; blocking a connector also blocks MCP tools that rely on it, and tools on end-user credentials keep the caller's authority. Limits: in classic data policies new connectors land in Non-business by default, so unclassified is blocked only under advanced connector policies; ACP does not cover custom connectors, HTTP or the Copilot Studio virtual connectors and is runtime-only in Copilot Studio until its design-time enforcement ships; action control excludes custom and unblockable connectors and handles triggers only in PowerShell; endpoint filtering is preview; scoping is per environment, not per user; computer use's website and app allowlist is a maker setting, off by default.

controls.mechanism: On-premises data gateway: data-source credentials encrypted with asymmetric encryption before storage in the gateway cloud service and decrypted only on the gateway host; outbound-only relay; administrator-assigned recovery key; Manage > Data (preview) for gateway users, members, clusters and Manage gateway installers; maker OAuth connections held in the Power Platform connection store; computer-use stored credentials in internal storage or the customer's Azure Key Vault

steps.title: Restrict who can install gateways
body: In Manage > Data (preview) turn on Tenant administration and use Manage gateway installers to name the users allowed to register gateways.

steps.title: Control gateway use and remove members
body: Use Manage users on each gateway cluster to limit Can use and Can use + share (and the data-source types they may create), and Remove members or clusters that should no longer relay.

steps.title: Hold the recovery key
body: Keep the recovery key assigned at install where administrators can find it; it is required to restore, migrate or take over the gateway.

steps.title: Keep computer-use passwords in your vault
body: Under the computer use tool's Stored credentials choose the Azure Key Vault option (subscription, resource group, vault and secret name) instead of internal storage.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule, the same word as toolM365Copilot: Microsoft ships the gateway, the relayed credential is encrypted to the host and never reaches the model, nothing is opened inbound, and gateway access and installation are administrator-controlled. But the gateway uses one stored standing credential per data source for every caller, rotation is a manual edit of that connection, no short-lived issuance or rotation of the gateway key pair is documented, and maker OAuth connections sit in Microsoft's connection store with lifetimes set by the target service and no documented bulk revocation; removing the Maker-provided choice (D3-APA) stops their use rather than revoking them. The gateway can also carry standard connectors straight to on-premises sources, bypassing our gateway (a recorded deviation).

controls.mechanism: SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge retrieved on behalf of the signed-in user (Authenticate with Microsoft by default) with sensitivity-label permission trimming; synced Upload files > SharePoint/OneDrive items check the user's permission before answering; connector tools default to end-user credentials; administrator control of attachable sources through data-policy knowledge connectors (documents, SharePoint and OneDrive, public websites), Connector endpoints filtering and Control maker credential options

steps.title: Stop uploads that bypass source permissions
body: Block Knowledge source with documents in Copilot Studio in the data policy; locally uploaded files are answered to anyone who can use the agent.

steps.title: Allow only governed sites as knowledge
body: On Knowledge source with SharePoint and OneDrive in Copilot Studio and on the public-websites connector use Configure connector > Connector endpoints to allow only approved site URLs (preview).

steps.title: Keep every read on the user's entitlement
body: Set Control maker credential options to End-user credentials so connector knowledge and tools run as the invoking user.

controls.note: Native on the retrieval rule, the same word as toolM365Copilot: SharePoint, OneDrive and synced knowledge is retrieved with the invoking user's permissions and label trimming, and the administrator decides which source types and sites makers may attach and can remove maker credentials. Outside it: locally uploaded documents are not identity-scoped (block the connector), public websites are public, content already overshared in SharePoint is returned (remediate with the DSPM and SharePoint Advanced Management reports on toolM365Copilot), No-authentication agents cannot use SharePoint, encrypted files are not grounded at all, and endpoint filtering is preview. Restricted SharePoint Search, where still on, blocks SharePoint knowledge.

controls.mechanism: Purview unified audit log: maker events (BotCreate, BotUpdateOperation-BotPublish, -BotShare, -BotAuthUpdate, BotComponentUpdate, AIPluginOperationUpdate, BotDelete) and CopilotInteraction per user turn with the channel in AppHost and the transcript thread ID, readable through the Office 365 Management Activity API; conversation transcripts in the environment's Dataverse ConversationTranscript table (Content JSON of every activity; node-level nodeTraceData only with the maker's enhanced-transcripts toggle); per-agent Application Insights set by the maker; Entra sign-in logs for agent identities

steps.title: Keep transcripts in Dataverse
body: In the environment group rule Accessing transcripts from conversations in Copilot Studio agents (or environment Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents) keep Allow conversation transcripts and their associated metadata to be saved in Dataverse on.

steps.title: Retain and export transcripts
body: Cancel the Bulk Delete Conversation Transcript Records Older Than 1 Month job, create one with your retention, and ingest the ConversationTranscript table into your store.

steps.title: Stream maker and usage audit events
body: Filter Copilot Studio activities in Purview Audit and collect them through the Office 365 Management Activity API for the SIEM.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule: run and maker records land where we can query them (our Dataverse, Purview, the Management Activity API), but per-step capture of tool and connector calls with arguments is not documented as part of the default transcript; node-level trace and Application Insights are maker toggles per agent that the administrator cannot floor. Transcripts are not written for Dataverse for Teams environments, developer environments or Microsoft 365 Copilot agents; SharePoint-grounded answers are REDACTED; records are written after 30 minutes of inactivity; audit records carry the transcript thread ID, not the text; some channels are excluded from logging, and non-Microsoft channels need Purview pay-as-you-go billing. Capture is not tamper resistance: the SIEM copy is the record.

controls.mechanism: Block on a published agent in Manage > Inventory or Manage > Copilot Studio (reversible); Power Platform API POST .../copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/botQuarantine/SetAsQuarantined; org-wide levers: data-policy blocks on channels and connectors (enforced in real time), Agent access channels (preview), Publish Copilots with AI features, Control maker credential options; deleting an agent deletes its Entra Agent ID

steps.title: Block one agent
body: In Manage > Inventory select the published agent and choose Block; makers can still test it, but no other channel can use it.

steps.title: Quarantine by API
body: As an AI, Power Platform or Global administrator call botQuarantine/SetAsQuarantined with a token carrying CopilotStudio.AdminActions.Invoke, and check isBotQuarantined.

steps.title: Cut maker-credential connections
body: Set Control maker credential options to End-user credentials on the environment group; every tool switches to end-user sign-in immediately.

steps.title: Close channels org-wide
body: Clear channels in Agent access channels, or block the channel connectors in the data policy; agents already published there fail at runtime.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the administrator can block or quarantine a specific agent and close channels or connectors for all agents, but whether a conversation or autonomous run already in progress stops is not documented, no delay is published for block or quarantine (the maker-credential switch may take a minute to propagate), and revoking the OAuth connections a maker authorised is not a documented bulk action; the maker-credential switch stops their use for tools. Quarantine and block do not cover classic chatbots. Deleting the agent removes its Entra Agent ID.

tools.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Microsoft Copilot app, Copilot Chat, in-app Copilot, agents and connectors)

variants.name: Microsoft Copilot app and Copilot Chat (web, desktop, mobile; copilot.cloud.microsoft)
variants.note: Copilot Chat (Basic) is included for Entra users with a qualifying Microsoft 365 subscription and is web-grounded; Graph-grounded chat needs the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence.

variants.name: Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams
variants.note: Built into the apps, not an add-in; the Multiple account access to Copilot for work documents policy decides whether a personal Copilot subscription can act on work files.

variants.name: Researcher and Analyst
variants.note: Part of the core Copilot Chat experience and outside agent-related settings; availability is controlled only by blocking the agent tenant-wide.

variants.name: Agents from the Agent Store and Copilot connectors (synced and federated MCP connectors)
Copilot Cowork (agentic system, usage-based billing, local Edge browser use)
variants.note: Access is granted only by a spending policy that selects Cowork (Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration); the Cowork entry under Agents > All agents no longer controls access.

summary: Microsoft's work-grounded assistant, renamed Microsoft Copilot (and Copilot Chat to Microsoft Copilot Chat) during 2026 with no change to its security, compliance or privacy terms: the Copilot app and Copilot Chat, Copilot inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, the Researcher and Analyst reasoning agents, agents from the Agent Store, Copilot connectors, and the Cowork agentic system. Inference runs inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary on Microsoft-hosted models, with OpenAI and Anthropic as subprocessors; grounding reads Microsoft Graph content with the signed-in user's permissions, and web grounding sends a generated query to Bing outside the DPA and EU Data Boundary.

The admin planes are the tenant's own: Microsoft Entra (Conditional Access, tenant restrictions v2, agent identities), the Microsoft 365 admin center (Copilot > Settings, Agents > All agents, Copilot connectors > Your connections), Microsoft Purview (DLP location "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat", sensitivity labels, DSPM, audit, retention, eDiscovery), the SharePoint admin center (SharePoint Advanced Management), Cloud Policy (Allow web search in Copilot) and Defender. Interaction content is stored in the user's mailbox and exported through a Graph API; CopilotInteraction audit records stream through the Office 365 Management Activity API.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Copilot Chat (Basic): web-grounded, no extra cost with a qualifying Microsoft 365 subscription. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) add-on: Graph and Work IQ grounding and the full in-app experience; Cowork is billed by usage on top. Microsoft 365 E7 bundles E5, Microsoft Copilot, Agent 365 and the Entra Suite.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Microsoft-hosted models plus OpenAI and Anthropic as subprocessors (admin toggle at Copilot > Settings > Data access > AI providers for other large language models). LLM calls go to the closest region and may overflow to other regions at peak; EU traffic stays in the EU Data Boundary, except Anthropic models, which are currently excluded from it.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, grounding content and responses are processed in the Microsoft 365 service boundary. With web search on, a generated query (the whole prompt only when it is very short; no user or tenant identifiers) goes to Bing, where the DPA, HIPAA and the EU Data Boundary do not apply.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models; Azure OpenAI abuse monitoring is opted out. Interaction history is stored with the organisation's Microsoft 365 content, deletable by users in My Account and governed by Purview retention policies (location Microsoft Copilot experiences).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot (Copilot documentation hub; Copilot controls overview)

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: Allow *.cloud.microsoft (primary URL copilot.cloud.microsoft); Microsoft does not support managing Copilot Chat through domain, URL or IP blocking.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: A covered workload in the Product Terms data-residency commitments since 2024-03-01, including Advanced Data Residency and Multi-Geo.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot > Settings (User access, Data access, Copilot actions), Copilot > Overview > Security (the Copilot security dashboard), Agents > All agents (Registry, Requests, Block, Delete), Agents > Settings (Allowed agent types, User access, Sharing, Agent management rules) and Copilot connectors > Your connections. Purview portal: Data Loss Prevention, DSPM, Audit, eDiscovery, Data Lifecycle Management. SharePoint admin center: Active sites (Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot), Reports > Data access governance, Advanced Management. Entra admin center: Conditional Access, Cross-tenant access settings, Agent identities.

links.title: Manage Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Security for Microsoft Copilot (security dashboard, Security Dashboard for AI)

items.title: Prompt-injection defence in depth
body: Microsoft runs jailbreak and cross-prompt-injection (XPIA) classifiers on inputs before model execution and sanitises hidden Unicode in pasted prompts; detections surface as JailbreakDetected and XPIADetected in CopilotInteraction audit records and as Defender alerts. The customer-side levers are source controls: DLP exclusion of external email from grounding, Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 prompt-injection detection on inbound mail, web-grounding domain exclusion and the web search policy.

links.title: Microsoft Copilot prompt defense in depth

riskNotes.note: Every mail, file, chat and connector result Copilot grounds on is model input. MSRC has published a run of server-side-fixed Critical command-injection disclosures (CVE-2025-32711, the EchoLeak zero-click chain; CVE-2026-26129, -26164, -42824); the XPIA classifiers that answer them are vendor-run and may not cover every scenario.
Copilot returns whatever the user's permissions already reach, so oversharing in SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams becomes an answer. Web-grounding queries leave the DPA and the EU Data Boundary.

Agent Builder agents can be shared with named colleagues without admin approval; a personal Copilot subscription can act on work documents unless Multiple account access to Copilot for work documents is disabled; consumer Copilot with a personal Microsoft account is outside the tenant.
Federated connectors gain write, update and delete tools from early October 2026 and Cowork automated tasks run without a person present; both let users persist approval.

Federated connectors are Microsoft-published or partner-submitted and Microsoft-approved, and the tools an MCP server exposes can change after approval; Microsoft-published connectors are on by default.
Shared agents become ownerless when their creator is deleted, and per-user connector OAuth grants have no admin-visible expiry.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy (Users: All users; Target resources: All resources; Grant: Require authentication strength > Multifactor authentication), which Copilot honours like every Microsoft 365 service; security defaults turn MFA on for tenants without Entra ID P1

steps.title: Require MFA for every user
body: In the Microsoft Entra admin center go to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy: include All users (exclude break-glass accounts), target All resources, grant Require authentication strength > Multifactor authentication, then move the policy from Report-only to On.

steps.title: Confirm Copilot inherits the policy
body: Copilot honours Conditional Access and the tenant's MFA settings, including Intune device compliance conditions; on tenants without Entra ID P1, keep security defaults on.

controls.note: Native on the MFA rule applied to every vendor: the product's own identity layer (the tenant's Entra ID) can require a second factor for every member, and Copilot sits behind it. Outside it: break-glass accounts excluded by design; service principals and apps using application permissions such as AiEnterpriseInteraction.Read.All (Conditional Access for workload identities is separate); sessions that live on refresh tokens between sign-ins (sign-in frequency bounds them); agent identities, which do not use human MFA; and consumer Copilot on a personal Microsoft account, which the tenant policy never sees (tenant restrictions v2 is that lever). Conditional Access needs Entra ID P1, which Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 include.

controls.mechanism: Tenant restrictions v2 in Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings, enforced by Entra when the sec-Restrict-Tenant-Access-Policy: <TenantId>:<policyGuid> header reaches login.live.com, login.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com and login.windows.net (proxy injection, authentication plane only) or through universal tenant restrictions (Global Secure Access) or Windows GPO

steps.title: Block external tenants and personal Microsoft accounts
body: In Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings set the default tenant restrictions to block external accounts and apps, and add a policy for the Microsoft account tenant so personal-account sign-ins are refused.

steps.title: Signal the policy on every sign-in
body: Have the proxy insert sec-Restrict-Tenant-Access-Policy with your tenant ID and the cross-tenant access policy ID on the four Microsoft sign-in domains, or use universal tenant restrictions in Global Secure Access to tag traffic without a proxy.

controls.note: Partial on the browser-pin rule: Microsoft documents a tenant-restriction header that the organisation's proxy or SSE injects and Entra enforces server-side, so personal tenants and personal Microsoft accounts are refused at sign-in. Proxy injection covers only the authentication plane (Windows GPO and Global Secure Access add data-plane coverage), and anonymous resources are not blocked. Microsoft does not support managing Copilot Chat by domain, URL or IP blocking. A customer proxy does not control Microsoft's own egress: Bing web grounding, federated connector calls and Cowork's hosted environment leave from Microsoft's cloud; the vendor-side levers there are the Allow web search in Copilot policy and web-grounding domain exclusion (up to 1,000 sites).

controls.mechanism: Microsoft Purview DLP policy on the "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat" location: Content contains > Sensitive information types with Prevent Copilot from processing content > Processing prompts (preview) or > Performing Web Searches, and Content contains > Sensitivity labels to keep labelled files and email out of grounding; encrypting labels without the EXTRACT usage right withhold content; Endpoint DLP blocks paste into web Copilot Chat

steps.title: Block prompts that carry sensitive information
body: In the Purview portal go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy, turn on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location, and add Content contains > Sensitive information types with Prevent Copilot from processing content > Processing prompts (and > Performing Web Searches to keep those prompts off Bing).

steps.title: Keep labelled items out of responses
body: In a separate rule of the same location add Content contains > Sensitivity labels with Prevent Copilot from processing content, so labelled files and email are cited but not read.

steps.title: Withhold EXTRACT on encrypting labels
body: Configure encrypting sensitivity labels so groups that must not get Copilot answers lack the EXTRACT usage right; Copilot returns encrypted content only with VIEW and EXTRACT.

steps.title: Block paste into web Copilot Chat
body: Use Endpoint DLP to block paste of sensitive content and files by sensitivity label into the web version of Copilot Chat on onboarded devices.

controls.note: Native on the redaction rule: a vendor tenant control inspects typed prompts for sensitive information types and blocks the turn, and excludes labelled items from grounding, server-side. Boundaries: block only, no masking; the prompt block is in preview and rolling out; DLP does not scan files uploaded into a prompt, only the typed text; no response-side inspection is documented (labels are displayed and inherited, not enforced on output); SIT and label conditions cannot share a rule; the label rule covers files and email sent on or after 2025-01-01, not calendar invites, and in Word, Excel and PowerPoint is evaluated at file open; policy changes take up to four hours; evaluations that time out are deferred (DLPEvaluationDeferred in the audit record), so watch that field.

controls.mechanism: Service Trust Portal audit reports and whitepapers, and the Copilot privacy page's compliance statement, feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Get started with the Microsoft Service Trust Portal (ISO/IEC, SOC 1-3, GDPR, FedRAMP, PCI, CSA STAR)
Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot (compliance offerings, subprocessors, EUDB)

controls.note: External: the assessment, its evidence expiry and the reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform. The Service Trust Portal publishes the ISO/IEC, SOC 1-3, GDPR, FedRAMP, PCI and CSA STAR material behind an Entra sign-in and NDA; the privacy page states GDPR, ISO 27001, HIPAA and ISO 42001 coverage for Copilot, points to a Copilot & Copilot Chat Risk Assessment Quickstart, and names OpenAI and Anthropic as subprocessors with Anthropic excluded from the EU Data Boundary. Re-assess on model and subprocessor changes; the portal itself renders client-side and was not read.

controls.mechanism: Federated connector write, update and delete tools (rolling out from early October 2026) show a confirmation card with the action parameters and default to Needs approval per tool, with Allow once, Allow for conversation or Always allow; Cowork asks before an automated task sends email, posts or changes a shared system, and users can pre-authorise; no admin setting forces approval

steps.title: Review which connectors can write
body: In the Microsoft 365 admin center open Copilot connectors > Your connections, select a federated connector and read its Tools section (coming soon); disable or scope connectors whose write tools you do not accept.

steps.title: Tell users how to reset approvals
body: Users set the connector's Write/Delete tools back to Needs approval in Copilot Settings > Sources; a publisher change to a tool resets it to Needs approval.

steps.title: Limit who can run Cowork
body: Grant Cowork only through a spending policy scoped to a security group at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration; users outside every Cowork policy cannot start tasks.

controls.note: Partial on the human-approval rule: a present person approves each write seeing its parameters, but users can persist Always allow per tool or pre-authorise Cowork automated tasks, and the administrator can neither require approval nor remove Always allow. Read tools never prompt. Actions run with the user's own permissions in the target system. Agents with their own actions (Copilot Studio, API plugins) carry their publisher's confirmation behaviour, which this row does not cover.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-run jailbreak and cross-prompt-injection (XPIA) classifiers screen inputs before model execution, always on and not configurable, logged as JailbreakDetected and XPIADetected in CopilotInteraction audit records and raised as Defender alerts; admin-set source controls: DLP Email is received from > External users (preview), Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 prompt-injection detection on inbound mail, web-grounding domain exclusion

steps.title: Watch the classifier signals
body: In the Purview portal Audit search, filter the CopilotInteraction operation and alert on AccessedResources.XPIADetected and Messages.JailbreakDetected; SecOps sees the same detections in the Defender portal.

steps.title: Keep external email out of grounding
body: Add a rule to the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat DLP location with Email is received from > External users and Prevent Copilot from processing content.

steps.title: Screen inbound mail for injection
body: With Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, inbound messages carrying prompt injection get the High confidence phishing verdict with detection technology Prompt injection protection; route that verdict to quarantine in your anti-spam policy.

steps.title: Narrow web grounding
body: Run ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 (Search Administrator) to exclude up to 1,000 sites from web grounding, or disable web search with the Allow web search in Copilot policy.

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: screening of retrieved content is vendor-internal, documented but not configurable ("may not be available in all Microsoft Copilot scenarios"), and a detection is an audit event, not an admin quarantine. The switches the administrator does own act on sources rather than classifying content: the external-email rule reads sender metadata only; Defender for Office 365 covers inbound mail only and a focused set of intents (URL exfiltration, system-prompt and tool discovery). SharePoint files, Teams chats, Copilot connector content and federated MCP results have no admin-tunable screening.

controls.mechanism: Copilot acts as the signed-in user; agents with a Microsoft Entra agent identity (Agent 365 instances, Copilot Studio agents with automatic identity creation, preview) are listed in the Entra admin center with a sponsor, get expiring access-package assignments and transfer sponsorship to the manager when the sponsor leaves; the Agent Registry flags ownerless agents; connector grants are per-user OAuth consents that users disconnect in Settings > Sources

steps.title: Inventory agent identities
body: Review agent identities and their sponsors in the Microsoft Entra admin center; agent sign-ins are logged as AI agents.

steps.title: Give agent access an expiry
body: Assign agent identities access through access packages with an end date (policy "For users, service principals, and agent identities" > All agents) so access lapses unless the sponsor extends it.

steps.title: Resolve ownerless agents
body: At Agents > Settings > Agent management rules run Reassign ownerless agents created with Agent Builder to manager, or Block ownerless agents without usage.

controls.note: Partial on the connector-grant rule: agent identities are inventoried with sponsor lifecycle and expiring access (Agent 365 licence with Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 E3), but the grants that carry Copilot into third-party systems, federated and self-serve connectors, are per-user OAuth consents the administrator cannot list or expire per grant; the only admin lever is disabling a connector for everyone. Disabling the Entra user stops Copilot use; revocation of the third-party tokens Microsoft holds for that user is not documented. Agents without an agent identity run under the user.

controls.mechanism: Purview DSPM data risk assessments (default weekly assessment of the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage, custom and item-level assessments) with sensitive-information classification and oversharing counts; SharePoint Advanced Management data access governance reports and the Content Management Assessment

steps.title: Run data risk assessments
body: In the Purview portal open Solutions > DSPM > Discover > Data risk assessments, review the default weekly assessment and create custom assessments for the sites and users Copilot will serve.

steps.title: Run the data access governance reports
body: In the SharePoint admin center open Reports > Data access governance and run Site permissions across your organization and Sensitivity labels applied to files, then the Sharing links and 'Everyone except external users' activity reports.

steps.title: Start the Content Management Assessment
body: In the SharePoint admin center select Advanced Management > Start assessment and rerun it every 30 days to track oversharing, inactive and ownerless sites.

controls.note: Native on the inventory rule: the vendor inventories and classifies what Copilot can reach in SharePoint and OneDrive and reports the oversharing. Limits: the default assessment covers the top 100 sites by usage; 200,000 items per location; item-level scanning is SharePoint only and at most 10 sites; Exchange mailboxes, Teams chats, synced Copilot connector content and federated sources are not in the oversharing assessments; results lag by days. DSPM needs Purview licensing; SharePoint Advanced Management features come with Copilot licences, and E5 alone gets only part of the reports.

controls.mechanism: No customer-run tunnel for MCP servers; the Microsoft Graph connector agent (on-premises, outbound port 443) authenticates with an Entra app registration's client secret (expiry chosen at creation) or certificate; connectors such as ServiceNow offer Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect federated auth with no stored secret; federated connector OAuth tokens are held by Microsoft per user; Entra sessions are bounded by sign-in frequency and revoked with Revoke-MgUserSignInSession

steps.title: Prefer secretless connector auth
body: Where the connector offers it, choose Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect (Federated Auth) so the connector authenticates to the source without storing or rotating a client secret.

steps.title: Bound the connector agent's credential
body: Configure the Graph connector agent with a certificate, or a client secret created under App registration > Certificates and secrets with a short expiry, and rotate it there.

steps.title: Revoke a user's tokens
body: Run Revoke-MgUserSignInSession to invalidate the user's refresh tokens; access tokens last up to an hour unless the app supports continuous access evaluation.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule for a product without an MCP tunnel: the Entra-issued credentials (connector agent app, Graph export apps, user sessions) are scoped, expiring and rotatable by the administrator, and connector tokens never reach the model; but the per-user OAuth tokens federated connectors hold for third-party services are in Microsoft's custody with lifetime set by the third party and no admin rotation or revocation documented, and some synced connectors still accept Basic authentication with a stored password. The Graph connector agent is an indexing agent for synced connectors, not a tunnel; its app credential is the load-bearing secret on that path.

controls.mechanism: Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types (built by Microsoft / your organization / external publishers; also governs default federated connectors), Agents > Settings > User access, per-agent publish and install audiences, and per-connector allowed-user scope and staged rollout to Entra groups at Copilot connectors > Your connections; write, update and delete tools are not enabled separately

steps.title: Switch connectors to allowlist mode
body: At Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types clear the Microsoft-published and third-party options so federated connectors, including future ones, are off until an administrator enables each one.

steps.title: Scope each connector to groups
body: At Copilot connectors > Your connections enable a connector and use Add staging to limit it to specific Microsoft Entra ID groups.

steps.title: Scope agent access
body: At Agents > Settings > User access choose Specific users/groups, and publish each agent to named groups rather than everyone.

controls.note: Partial on the tool-permission rule: an admin-locked allowlist of connectors and agents with group scoping, but no per-tool or read/write scoping: a connector admitted for reads admits the write, update and delete tools its publisher ships (from early October 2026), and the admin Tools list is view-only. Actions keep the caller's authority (the user's own permissions at the source). Researcher and Analyst sit outside agent settings. The Set-FederatedConnectorToggle cmdlet is retired; its state is honoured only until 2026-10-20.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 admin center Agents > All agents > Registry (every agent available to the tenant, with publisher type, owner, channel, platform, status and risk signals; Export; Agents without owners), Requests (Pending review / update / activate; Publish to store or Reject submission), Block, and Copilot connectors > Your connections; Allowed agent types for allowlist mode

steps.title: Review and export the registry
body: At Agents > All agents > Registry filter by publisher type, platform and status, export to CSV, and work the Agents without owners card.

steps.title: Approve before anything is published
body: At Agents > All agents > Requests review each agent's data sources, tools and permissions, then Publish to store to a named audience or Reject submission; updates wait as Pending update.

steps.title: Close the default-allow paths
body: Restrict Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types and Sharing (Specific users), and Block any agent in the registry that should not run.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule: an authoritative record of every agent and connector in the tenant with owner and approval state, and admin enforcement (approval queue, allowed types, block). Gaps to watch: Agent Builder agents can still be shared with named individuals without approval (Sharing set to No users keeps direct sharing, and the control covers only Agent Builder agents); they appear in the registry and can be blocked, but are not pre-approved. Microsoft-published federated connectors are on until Allowed agent types is changed. Registry risk signals need E7 or Agent 365; Cowork plugins are managed on their own page.

controls.mechanism: CopilotInteraction records in the unified audit log (Audit Standard; auditing on by default for new tenants) with AppHost, AgentId, AISystemPlugin (BingWebSearch), AccessedResources (SensitivityLabelId, PolicyDetails, XPIADetected) and Messages (JailbreakDetected), streamed through the Office 365 Management Activity API (Audit.General, record type 261); prompt and response text through the Graph getAllEnterpriseInteractions API

steps.title: Stream the audit records to the SIEM
body: Subscribe to the Audit.General content type in the Office 365 Management Activity API and parse record type 261 (CopilotInteraction) with the Copilot schema.

steps.title: Export prompts and responses
body: Grant an app AiEnterpriseInteraction.Read.All and call GET /copilot/users/{id}/interactionHistory/getAllEnterpriseInteractions per user, or subscribe to aiInteraction change notifications.

steps.title: Confirm auditing and search it
body: In the Purview portal Audit, filter Activities - operation names on CopilotInteraction; web queries appear as AISystemPlugin.Id BingWebSearch.

controls.note: Native on the telemetry rule: programmatic export of interaction events (with the files, sites, plugins, agents and policy decisions involved) and of conversation content, for fusion with the gateway's record. Limits: audit records carry references, not prompt text, so content comes from the Graph export API, which needs a Copilot licence, has no delta and does not return Copilot Studio agent interactions; capture is not tamper resistance, so the SIEM copy is the record of truth.

controls.mechanism: Nothing in Copilot lists personal accounts or unsanctioned assistants; Microsoft's own SSE/CASB products (Defender for Cloud Apps cloud app catalog, Generative AI category; Global Secure Access shadow AI discovery) and Purview DSPM browser and endpoint signals do the discovery

evidence.title: Manage generative AI apps for your organization (DSPM for AI, Defender for Cloud Apps)
Shadow AI discovery in Global Secure Access
Multiple account access to Microsoft Copilot for work and school documents

controls.note: External on the discovery rule: Copilot does not report personal Microsoft accounts on the organisation's domains or other AI tools staff use; the integration points are Defender for Cloud Apps (Cloud apps > Cloud app catalog, Category Generative AI, tag Unsanctioned), Global Secure Access and the Purview browser extension; the Security Dashboard for AI aggregates their findings (third-party AI apps, shadow agents) but is Microsoft's security stack around Copilot, not Copilot. The Agent Registry's Unmanaged agents count covers agents inside the tenant only. Prevention, credited here only: tenant restrictions v2 refusing the Microsoft account tenant, and the Cloud Policy setting Multiple account access to Copilot for work documents set to Disabled so personal Copilot subscriptions cannot act on work files.

controls.mechanism: Grounding through Microsoft Graph and the Semantic Index with the signed-in user's permissions, synced connector items carrying source ACLs, federated connectors calling as the user; admin corpus scoping with Restricted Content Discovery (Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot, Set-SPOSite -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch), the DLP sensitivity-label exclusion and connector allowed-user scope

steps.title: Pull sensitive sites out of Copilot
body: In the SharePoint admin center open Sites > Active sites > the site > Settings and turn on Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot, or run Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true; report with Start-SPORestrictedContentDiscoverabilityReport.

steps.title: Exclude labelled content from grounding
body: Add a Content contains > Sensitivity labels rule to the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat DLP location with Prevent Copilot from processing content.

steps.title: Limit connectors to the groups that need them
body: Scope each Copilot connector at Copilot connectors > Your connections to specific Entra ID groups with Add staging.

controls.note: Native on the retrieval rule: retrieval runs with the requesting user's entitlements at the source, and the administrator can restrict which sites, labels and connectors are returned. Limits: Restricted Content Discovery changes no permissions, still lets users reach content they own or recently used, does not apply to OneDrive and takes time to propagate on large sites; Restricted SharePoint Search is retiring (no new enablement from 2026-07-31) and was never a security boundary; synced connectors are only as tight as the ACLs they map; what is already overshared is returned until permissions are fixed (see D3-DI).

controls.mechanism: Group-based authorisation administered in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Copilot licence assignment, Agents > Settings > User access, per-agent publish and install audiences, connector allowed-user scope, AI Administrator role); consent paths documented: Review permissions > Grant admin consent when an agent is published or installed, and connector apps registered in the target system (for example ServiceNow System OAuth > Application Registry with Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect)

steps.title: Decide who gets Copilot and agents
body: At Agents > Settings > User access choose Specific users/groups, and publish or install each agent to named groups.

steps.title: Grant admin consent deliberately
body: When installing or publishing an agent, read the Review permissions pane before selecting Grant admin consent and Accept.

steps.title: Register the connector in the target system
body: For a synced connector, register the app in the target (ServiceNow: System OAuth > Application Registry, OIDC provider Microsoft Entra ID) and limit its scope there.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule: the console administers group-scoped authorisation over Copilot, agents and connectors, and Microsoft documents the consent path for agent permissions and per-connector target registration. The target tenant's consent (ServiceNow, Google, HubSpot) is that tenant's control; federated connectors authenticate each user into the third party, and whether its admin must approve the app is the third party's setting, not documented per connector by Microsoft. Policy administration is not the enforcement path: Entra and the source system enforce.

controls.mechanism: Block access to Copilot Chat for all users or groups; remove Microsoft 365 Copilot licences; Agents > All agents > Block per agent (Researcher and Analyst only tenant-wide); disable the agent type used by connectors or set a connector to No users (up to 10 minutes); drop users from Cowork spending policies; Revoke-MgUserSignInSession per user

steps.title: Block an agent for the whole organisation
body: At Agents > All agents select the agent, choose Block > Block agent and Save; delete it for a 30-day soft delete, or Permanently delete.

steps.title: Block Copilot Chat
body: Block access to Copilot Chat for all users or selected groups, and set Custom link for blocked Microsoft Copilot app under Copilot > Settings to explain why.

steps.title: Cut every connector
body: Disable the agent type used by Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors in Allowed agent types; each connector's allowed-user scope becomes No users within about ten minutes.

steps.title: Revoke a user's sessions
body: Run Revoke-MgUserSignInSession for the user; access tokens already issued last up to an hour unless the app supports continuous access evaluation.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the administrator can switch Copilot, agents and connectors off org-wide, but the docs do not say that work already running stops (Cowork automated tasks, a Researcher run, an agent mid-task), the delay for agent and Chat blocks is not documented (connector changes take up to 10 minutes), third-party OAuth grants are not revoked in bulk by any documented action, and blocking a SharePoint or Foundry agent affects only Copilot Chat. Session revocation leaves issued access tokens alive for up to an hour.
