EX-AGENT-ACTION-POLICY-ENFORCEMENT.note: Not deployed. Baseline is toolApproval opaPolicy with default deny and requires-approval on mutating tools, signed approvals, and server-side history so an approval stays in its conversation; the signature does not bind the session

EX-AML-M0036.note: Not deployed. Baseline is stopWhen isStepCount(8), timeout totalMs and toolMs, maxOutputTokens, and a StopCondition over steps usage for the per-turn token budget, which is our code rather than an SDK limit

EX-D3-CTS.note: Not deployed. The SDK performs no token exchange and forwards whatever token sits in the MCP headers; redirect stays at its 'error' default, and narrowed tokens would come from the API gateway

EX-MCP-TOOL-INTEGRITY.note: Not deployed. Baseline is a fingerprintTools baseline stored at review and detectToolDrift before every call withholding changed or added tools; the SDK hashes but does not block, so the check is our code

EX-AGENT-EGRESS-CONTROL.note: Not deployed. The SDK sets no outbound allowlist; tools run in the function's process, so egress would be bounded at the platform network and an egress proxy

orgToolPosture.note: Reachable in the Microsoft 365 tenant by default (Copilot Studio for Teams plan in the Microsoft 365 licences, Copilot chat harness for the Microsoft 365 Copilot pilot group); no standalone Copilot Studio capacity bought. Governed as a default-on builder while makers are moved out of the default environment.

EX-SENSITIVE-DATA-REDACTION.note: Purview DLP rule on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location (Content contains > Sensitivity labels, Prevent Copilot from processing content) keeps Highly Confidential SharePoint knowledge out of Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot agents; uploads, connector payloads and web knowledge have no content inspection, so Knowledge source with documents in Copilot Studio is blocked in the data policy

EX-D3-APA.note: Tenant-wide data policy blocks Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio; Control maker credential options set to End-user credentials on the production environment group only (autonomous agents in the pilot still need maker credentials); agent sharing limits wait on Managed Environments for the default environment

EX-D3-AA.note: New agents get Entra Agent IDs automatically and are reviewed with their sponsors in Entra; legacy app-registration agents being migrated in batches through Actions > Recommendations; Conditional Access on connector scopes only takes effect in Teams, and agent actions still run as the user or the maker

EX-AGENT-TOOL-REGISTRY.note: Power Platform inventory queried monthly through Azure Resource Graph for agents with connectionProvider Maker, authentication None and sharedWithViewers.entireTenant; results reconciled against the governance register and blocked from Manage > Inventory where unowned

EX-STAGED-ROLLOUT-GATE.note: Environment routing on for new makers, but no pipeline with delegated-deployment approval yet and makers can still publish straight from their environment; org-catalogue listing is approved in the Teams admin center, which does not re-review content changes

EX-INPUT-GUARDRAILS.note: Vendor UPIA and XPIA blocking is always on and not configurable; Defender external threat detection piloted on the production environment with Set error behavior at Block the query; other environments have no runtime tool-call screening

EX-AI-VENDOR-ASSESSMENT.note: Covered by the Microsoft TPRM record (Service Trust Portal SOC 2 and ISO reports); Enable External Models left off pending a separate assessment of Anthropic outside the EU Data Boundary

EX-AML-M0028.note: Tenant-scoped data policy classifies every connector, blocks HTTP, Skills with Copilot Studio and the event-trigger connector outside production; connector actions restricted to reads on SharePoint and Outlook; advanced connector policies in mixed mode on the production group

EX-D3-CH.note: Gateway installers limited through Manage gateway installers and the recovery key held in the vault; data-source credentials on the gateway are standing service accounts rotated by hand; maker OAuth connections in Microsoft's store cannot be bulk-revoked

EX-DATA-ACCESS-GOVERNANCE.note: SharePoint knowledge runs on the user's permissions; local document uploads blocked in the data policy; Connector endpoints filtering (preview) on the SharePoint knowledge connector not yet configured, and overshared sites are handled through the SharePoint Advanced Management reports

EX-AGENT-TRACING.note: Copilot Studio audit events streamed to the SIEM through the Management Activity API; transcripts kept in Dataverse with the 30-day bulk delete replaced by a 12-month job; per-step tool traces depend on makers enabling enhanced transcripts and are not guaranteed

EX-AGENT-KILL-SWITCH.note: Runbook blocks the agent in Manage > Inventory or calls botQuarantine/SetAsQuarantined, then sets Control maker credential options to End-user credentials for the environment; the stop of in-flight conversations and autonomous runs is untested and the delay unmeasured

orgToolPosture.note: Not in use. No Salesforce org is licensed for Agentforce; assessed as a candidate CRM-embedded agent builder should the sales team adopt it. Each note below is the baseline the Salesforce administrator would set before the first agent is activated.

EX-SENSITIVE-DATA-REDACTION.note: Not deployed. Einstein Trust Layer data masking is disabled for agents, so nothing inspects Data Library uploads or agent prompts; baseline is SSE inline DLP on browser sessions to Salesforce, Knowledge libraries limited to Use Public Knowledge Articles, file_upload mode disabled on Service agents, and Data 360 Dynamic Data Masking on session-trace data

EX-D3-APA.note: Not deployed. Baseline is Employee agents only (they run as the logged-in user), Agent Access granted to pilot permission sets, Manage AI Agents held by the admin team alone, and no Service agent on an unauthenticated channel; there is no org-wide switch that forces authentication, so verification filters would be reviewed per agent

EX-D3-AA.note: Not deployed. Baseline is one new agent user per Service agent (named after the agent, Einstein Agent User profile, its own [Agent_Name]_Permissions set) and reassignment after every deployment; Employee agents have no identity of their own and the agent user is not an Entra identity, so conditional access does not apply

EX-AGENT-TOOL-REGISTRY.note: Not deployed. Baseline is a monthly BotDefinition query and Metadata API retrieve of every agent (*) reconciled against the governance register, and MCP servers admitted only through Setup > Agentforce Registry with High-risk tools refused; the agent record has no owner field, so owners are kept in the register

EX-STAGED-ROLLOUT-GATE.note: Not deployed. Baseline is build and Testing Center runs in a sandbox, promotion of committed versions to production by Salesforce CLI from source control, Manage AI Agents withheld from makers in production, a pilot permission set first, and rollback by activating the prior committed version; no approval or evaluation gate exists in the product

EX-INPUT-GUARDRAILS.note: Not deployed. Baseline is Einstein Trust Layer > Safety & Security > prompt injection detection (beta) on, with Audit and Feedback scores alerted in the SIEM; detection scores but does not block, so Web-to-Lead and other public-write objects stay out of agent grounding and grounding through our gateway is classified there

EX-AI-VENDOR-ASSESSMENT.note: Not assessed. Would be assessed in the TPRM platform against the Einstein Platform and Data 360 SPARC, the Infrastructure & Sub-processors list and the compliance portal reports, with re-assessment on new model providers and on ForcedLeak/SalesBleed-class disclosures

EX-AML-M0028.note: Not deployed. Baseline is Agentforce Registry tool allowlists, an Agentforce Gateway MCP Attribute-Based Access Control policy per agent, Restrictive Access on API connections and least-privilege agent users; the platform has no connector classification, so read-plus-send combinations are reviewed per agent

EX-D3-CH.note: Not deployed. Salesforce has no on-premises gateway; baseline is Private Connect to the AWS VPC with Named Credentials and External Credentials granted through dedicated permission sets, and secrets rotated by our process because no rotation or short-lived issuance is documented

EX-DATA-ACCESS-GOVERNANCE.note: Not deployed. Baseline is Employee agents so reads follow the user's sharing, Data Library creation limited to administrators (Data Cloud admin plus System Administrator), and Knowledge libraries filtered by data category; Data Library indexes are not documented as trimmed per user, so no restricted content is indexed

EX-AGENT-TRACING.note: Not deployed. Baseline is Agentforce Session Tracing and Audit and Feedback on in Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup, the Allow All data-space policy narrowed, and the session DMOs exported to the SIEM; agent edits are not in Setup Audit Trail, so committed versions are diffed from source control

EX-AGENT-KILL-SWITCH.note: Not deployed. Runbook would deactivate the agent (interrupts ongoing conversations) with the CLI agent deactivate command, remove its MCP tools and external credential permission sets, and turn off model providers in Einstein Setup for an org-wide stop (up to ten minutes)

orgToolPosture.note: Not in use. Assessed as the way the approved coding agents would reach GitHub (remote server for GitHub.com, local binary for any GHES instance); no host app is approved in the GitHub organizations yet. Each note below is the baseline the platform team would set before the first connection.

EX-D3-CTS.note: Not deployed. Baseline is fine-grained PATs only (Tokens (classic) restricted, Require administrator approval on), SAML SSO enforced so every token is authorized per organization, and approved host apps; GitHub offers no audience-bound token for the MCP endpoint, so any valid GitHub token is accepted by design

EX-AML-M0004.note: Not deployed. Only GitHub's per-identity API limits apply (5,000/h per user, 15,000/h for apps on Enterprise Cloud, secondary limits); unattended agents to run on their own GitHub App installation so a loop exhausts the app's budget, not a person's; no per-tool quota exists in the server

EX-AML-M0028.note: Not deployed. Baseline is host configs pointing at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/x/{toolset}/readonly (or --read-only --toolsets on the local binary) with write toolsets added per team, and fine-grained PAT permissions reviewed at approval as the enforceable ceiling, since remote headers are user-editable

EX-MCP-TOOL-INTEGRITY.note: Not deployed. Local binary to be pinned to a release by image digest with the cosign signature verified in the admission pipeline and github-mcp-server-config.json absent; the remote server changes without a version, so definition hash pinning would need an MCP gateway we do not run

EX-DATA-ACCESS-GOVERNANCE.note: Not deployed. Every call runs as the caller under repository roles, SSO authorization, OAuth app restrictions and PAT approval; baseline adds lower base permissions, host GitHub Apps on Only select repositories, and X-MCP-Lockdown for agents reading public repositories (a filter, not a boundary)

EX-D3-CH.note: Not deployed. Baseline is OAuth login (token in memory) or GitHub App auth with --app-private-key-path on a read-only mount for the local server, PAT maximum lifetime set under Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens, and no PATs in .env files; the caller's token is relayed to GitHub's API by design

EX-AML-M0024.note: Not deployed. Baseline is audit log streaming to the SIEM with Enable API Request Events, knowing MCP calls appear only as ordinary API activity with no tool name or parameters; self-hosted instances to run with --log-file and --enable-command-logging shipped to the SIEM

EX-AGENT-KILL-SWITCH.note: Not deployed. Runbook would use Enterprise Settings > Authentication security to revoke SSO authorizations (per user, per credential type or bulk), Active tokens > Revoke for fine-grained PATs, and suspend or uninstall host GitHub Apps; "MCP servers in Copilot" reaches Copilot hosts only

EX-D3-APA.note: Not deployed. Baseline is OAuth app access restrictions on with each host's app approved individually, fine-grained PAT approval, classic PATs restricted, and "MCP servers in Copilot" set at enterprise level; GitHub offers no single per-group switch for the server, so the approved-host list is kept by process

EX-D3-AA.note: Not deployed. Unattended agents to authenticate as a dedicated GitHub App installation (--app-id, --app-installation-id, key file) on selected repositories with read-only permissions where possible; installations reviewed in organization settings; PATs not permitted for automation

orgToolPosture.note: Not in use. Inference is consumed from managed APIs; vLLM is the candidate serving engine if a model is brought in-house, and each note below is the baseline the platform team would set before the first tenant.

EX-AML-M0014.note: Not deployed. vLLM verifies no signature or digest at load, so the baseline is an init container that runs the model-signing verifier against the promoted path before `vllm serve` starts, a read-only model volume, and --revision / --code-revision / --tokenizer-revision pinned to a commit for any hub load on v0.28.0 or later (the release that closed the artifact-pin-decay advisories)

EX-AML-M0023.note: Not deployed. Baseline is the inventory job collecting GET /v1/models (id, root, parent for LoRA adapters), GET /version and the system_fingerprint from every instance, joined to the deployment manifest and promotion record, which hold the revision, digest and scan result vLLM does not expose

EX-AML-M0024.note: Not deployed. The privacy-conscious record of prompts and completions would be the AI gateway's; on the engine, --enable-log-requests at VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO (no prompt text), --enable-request-id-headers and --otlp-traces-endpoint for metadata spans, with --enable-log-outputs left off because it logs raw output

EX-AML-M0008.note: Not deployed. vLLM evaluates nothing; baseline is the evaluation and red-team harness run against a staging instance with the candidate's exact serving flags through /v1, with the approval recorded before promotion

EX-STAGED-ROLLOUT-GATE.note: Not deployed. vLLM has no split or rollback; baseline is one instance per promoted version (or named --lora-modules adapters), a weighted route at the AI gateway for the canary slice, and rollback by re-pointing the route at the previous instance, with VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING left unset

EX-D3-AA.note: Not deployed. Tenant workload identity would be enforced at the AI gateway; vLLM would accept only the gateway, by --api-key from the secrets manager plus client-certificate TLS (--ssl-ca-certs, --ssl-cert-reqs 2), on v0.22.0 or later for the Host-header auth bypass fix

EX-AML-M0004.note: Not deployed. Per-tenant quotas would sit at the AI gateway because vLLM has no caller identity; the engine would add --max-num-queued-reqs (503 beyond the cap), VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES=64, explicit --max-model-len and --max-num-seqs, and --scheduling-policy priority set per tenant by the gateway

EX-OUTPUT-GUARDRAILS.note: Not deployed. vLLM returns raw completions; baseline is the AI gateway's content classification on both legs, with the reverse proxy allowlisting only the /v1 routes so /invocations cannot bypass it

EX-AML-M0031.note: Not deployed. Baseline is the gateway setting a random 256-bit cache_salt per tenant on every request and overwriting caller values, stripping caller-supplied multimodal uuid fields, and --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256; --no-enable-prefix-caching for the highest-sensitivity instances

EX-D3-NI.note: Not deployed. The serving plane would run on its own network with a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy admitting only the gateway to port 8000 and only peer pods to the torch.distributed, KV-transfer (14579) and data-parallel (29500) ports; VLLM_HOST_IP pinned to the private interface and --grpc-port left unset

orgToolPosture.note: Not deployed. No self-hosted model registry is approved yet; fine-tuned models would be promoted through MLflow 3.16 with basic-auth on, and each note below is the baseline the ML platform team would enforce before approving it.

EX-DATA-ACCESS-GOVERNANCE.note: Not deployed. Baseline is mlflow server --app-name basic-auth with default_permission = NO_PERMISSIONS in basic_auth.ini, READ roles per experiment and registered model under /admin → Roles, and proxied artifacts (--artifacts-destination) so the S3 credential sits only on the server; corpus reads stay with the bucket policies, and per-user read logging comes from the reverse proxy because MLflow keeps no audit log

EX-AML-M0029.note: Not deployed. Baseline is separate dev and prod registered models, training users with EDIT on the dev model only, and promotion by copy_model_version then set_registered_model_alias from a CI job with required reviewers; MLflow has no approval step and one EDIT grant covers version, alias and stage on a single model

EX-AML-M0013.note: Not deployed. MLflow signs nothing; baseline is model_signing sign (OpenSSF Model Signing, Sigstore keyless under the promotion pipeline's identity) after copy_model_version, the bundle kept in a bucket the training role cannot write and referenced by a model version tag, and model_signing verify in the serving tier before load

EX-AML-M0008.note: Not deployed. Baseline is mlflow.models.evaluate or mlflow.genai.evaluate into an evaluation experiment the trainers can only READ, with mlflow.validate_evaluation_results thresholds failing the promotion job; backdoor and memorisation probes are custom scorers not yet written, and the registry will alias a failed version

EX-AML-M0012.note: Not deployed. MLflow holds no keys; baseline is SSE-KMS default encryption with an organisation-managed key on the artifact bucket, a bucket policy denying other keys, MLFLOW_S3_UPLOAD_EXTRA_ARGS set to aws:kms with that SSEKMSKeyId on the server, MLFLOW_S3_EXPECTED_BUCKET_OWNER pinned, and TLS at the reverse proxy

EX-AML-M0023.note: Not deployed. Baseline is log_model with registered_model_name inside the run that called log_input, the transformers flavor for adapters so MLmodel records source_model_name and source_model_revision, and MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX limited to mlflow-artifacts sources; the lineage stays MLflow's own graph, with no CycloneDX or SPDX export

EX-AML-M0024.note: Not deployed. Run records (parameters, input datasets, code version) would sit in a PostgreSQL backend store; MLflow has no audit log and the run's user is sent by the client, so who did what comes from the authenticating reverse proxy's access log shipped to the SIEM

EX-D3-ORA.note: Not deployed. Model documentation baseline is registered-model and version descriptions, signature and input_example on every log_model, and a validation_status=approved version tag set by the evaluation job and checked by the promotion job before set_registered_model_alias; MLflow generates no model card and enforces no approval state

EX-D3-AA.note: Not deployed. Baseline is one MLflow user per training job (MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME and MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD from the secrets manager) with role grants on its experiment and the dev registered model only, moving to MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH=kubernetes behind kube-rbac-proxy; corpus access stays with the job's cloud IAM role

EX-AGENT-KILL-SWITCH.note: Not deployed. Withdrawal runbook is search_model_versions by run_id to find affected versions, then set_registered_model_alias back to the last good version or delete_registered_model_alias and delete_model_version (MANAGE), with a model_version_alias.deleted webhook telling the deployment system to reload; copies already loaded keep serving until reloaded

landscape.attribution: The framing is borrowed, not invented — CISA's Zero Trust Maturity Model pillars and cross-cutting capabilities. Placing each MITRE capability onto it is this repository's authored judgement, one primary home per capability; it does not claim CISA would place it the same way.
